notes: Added isValidRistVirtualPort between isValidIngestLatency and isValidPort, matching the Swift insertion point.
Swift's `UInt(value)!` force unwrap after isValidPort is translated with toUIntOrNull(), which cannot fail at that point but keeps the file's existing defensive style.
The even check uses UInt modulo: port % 2u != 0u.
All other lines are byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.

Swift's synthesised Codable for enums with associated values uses the externally tagged form {"case":{...}}, so each sealed class gets a hand-written KSerializer that reproduces that exact JSON, including {} for payload-less cases.
MoblinkResult has no raw values in Swift but is Codable, so it encodes as {"ok":{}}; it is an enum class with rawValue/fromRawValue plus MoblinkResultSerializer producing that single-key object.
moblinkJson uses explicitNulls = false to match Swift's encodeIfPresent, so nil batteryPercentage/thermalState/data keys are omitted instead of written as null.
Optional payload fields get Kotlin default null so a missing key decodes like Swift's decodeIfPresent.
Swift JSONEncoder writes UUID as an uppercase string; MoblinkUuidSerializer reproduces that and accepts any case when decoding.
UInt16 port is translated to UShort per the wire-format rule; kotlinx.serialization serialises it as a plain unsigned JSON number.

The Swift 'Not a UTF-8 string' / 'Encode failed' guards disappear: Kotlin Strings are already decodable, so fromJson just throws SerializationException on bad input and toJson() on MoblinkMessageToRelay still returns null via runCatching.
Sealed subclass names are capitalised (StartTunnel, Status, Hello, ...) but the JSON keys stay byte-identical to the Swift case names.
[[UInt8]] maps to MutableList<UByteArray>: the 2D grayscale buffer stays byte-oriented and mutates in place like the Swift arrays.
UByte comparisons need toInt() (UByte has no compareTo(Int)), so pixel reads are widened where arithmetic happens.
Swift's ternary threshold becomes a Kotlin if/else; newColor stays Int so the diff arithmetic is unchanged.
Int division by 8 keeps Kotlin's truncate-toward-zero semantics, matching Swift for negative diffs.
guard with multiple conditions becomes an early return with a negated conjunction, preserving the exact bounds check.
min/max clamping becomes coerceIn(0, 255) before converting back with toUByte().
The instance keeps the same mutable state fields (image, width, height) and the same apply/adjustPixel call order.
No Apple frameworks are used, so there is nothing unsupported.
Swift's `extension Bool { var uint8: UInt8 }` becomes a top-level extension property `val Boolean.uint8: UByte` in this file.
UInt8 maps to UByte; Kotlin has no UByte literal syntax, so the values are written as `1u.toUByte()` and `0u.toUByte()`.
The property is a getter-only computed property, matching the Swift read-only computed property.
Swift extends the ExpressibleByIntegerLiteral protocol; Kotlin has no such common supertype for primitives, so `data` is declared once per integer type instead.
Memory layout in Swift's withUnsafeBytes is native byte order, which is little-endian on both Apple and Android platforms; java.nio.ByteBuffer.LITTLE_ENDIAN reproduces it exactly.
Byte.data is a direct byteArrayOf(this) because a single byte needs no buffer.
Unsigned types (UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong) are included so call sites using unsigned literals still compile; UByte reuses the Byte path.
Extension properties are top-level in the file, matching the Swift extension in a separate file.
No top-level types are declared here, only extension properties, so declared_types is empty.
The file-private Swift constant averageSampleCount becomes a private top-level const val; it is only used inside this file.
Both Swift classes are non-final, so they are translated as open class with open functions; the private stored properties stay non-open.
The UInt16 crank revolution and event-time counters are wire values from the CSC characteristic, so they stay UShort and are converted with toInt() (which yields the unsigned value for UShort).

ContinuousClock.now / ContinuousClock.Instant come from com.moblin.android.platform.core; the three second stale timeout is written as .duration(to = now) > 3.seconds with kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds imported.
Swift's values.reduce(0, +) is DoubleArray.sum() and Array(repeating:count:) is DoubleArray(n).
Swift's min(cadence, 10000) is minOf(cadence, 10000.0); Int(averageCadence.averageIgnoreZeros()) is Double.toInt(), which truncates toward zero like Swift.
The Swift shadowed optional bindings inside update(revolutions:time:) are translated with local vals so the assignments to the stored previous* properties stay writes to the properties.
Swift struct with mutating methods becomes a Kotlin class so counters can be mutated in place.
The (Int, Int)? tuple return becomes Pair<Int, Int>?, keeping the same field order (duplicated, dropped).
The Swift `defer` block that zeroes both counters is expressed by snapshotting the counters into a local Pair before resetting them and returning it.
`private static let outputInterval` becomes a private const in the companion object.
Comparison logic was inverted into early returns to mirror the two `guard` statements.
Since this is pure logic with no Apple frameworks, unsupported is empty.
Pixel bytes stay UByte (matching Swift's UInt8) inside MutableList<MutableList<UByte>>; every arithmetic step converts with toInt() first because Kotlin has no implicit unsigned promotion.
The threshold test uses this.image[y][x].toInt() > 127 instead of comparing a UByte with an unsigned literal, avoiding cross-width unsigned comparison ambiguity.
Swift's value semantics are preserved by copying the incoming rows into fresh MutableLists, so the caller's array is not mutated.
Integer division (diff * 7 / 16 etc.) truncates toward zero in both languages, so the error diffusion weights are byte-identical.
clamping uses coerceIn(0, 255).toUByte(), the equivalent of Swift's UInt8(min(255, max(0, value))).
The private state (image, width, height) is kept exactly as in Swift so instances can be reused exactly like the original.
The method name apply is retained for side-by-side reading; it resolves to the member function because the stdlib scope function apply requires a lambda argument.
AVCaptureColorSpace is an AVFoundation type with no Android counterpart, so it is declared in this file as an enum class that keeps the Swift case names, raw values and a companion fromRawValue.
The Swift `description` computed property in the extension becomes a top-level Kotlin extension property on AVCaptureColorSpace in this same package.
CustomStringConvertible has no Kotlin equivalent; toString() is overridden on the enum to delegate to description so string interpolation matches Swift.
Raw values follow AVFoundation (sRGB = 1, P3_D65 = 2, HLG_BT2020 = 3, appleLog = 4); verify against the platform header if these numbers are ever persisted or sent over the wire.
The Swift `default:` branch is kept as `else -> "Unknown"` so values that do not map to a known case keep the same output.
If another Moblin module already declares AVCaptureColorSpace, remove the declaration here and import that one instead.
Kotlin enums are closed, so unknown platform values can only be represented by a null return from fromRawValue or by the else branch of description.
Swift's `Any` maps to Kotlin's `Any?`; the parameter is nullable so callers can pass anything.
Swift `Int` is 64-bit while Kotlin `Int` is 32-bit, so a boxed `Long` value will not match the `is Int` branch; use `Long` at call sites only if that parity is required.
The value is matched with Kotlin `is` checks, which correspond exactly to Swift's conditional `as?` casts, including falling through to `false` for any other type.
No Android or Apple frameworks are used, so the translation is complete and compiles as-is.
CoreAudio is not available on Android, so the `AudioStreamBasicDescription` struct itself is declared here as a Kotlin `data class` with the nine fields used by the Swift extension.

The Swift extension only adds `Equatable`; in Kotlin the data class generates `equals`/`hashCode` over exactly the same nine properties, so the `==` implementation is reproduced without an explicit operator.

Fields are mutable (`var`) to mirror the mutability of the imported Swift C struct, and are declared in the canonical CoreAudio order (`mSampleRate`, `mFormatID`, `mFormatFlags`, `mBytesPerPacket`, `mFramesPerPacket`, `mBytesPerFrame`, `mChannelsPerFrame`, `mBitsPerChannel`, `mReserved`).
The `UInt32` fields are mapped to Kotlin `UInt` because an audio stream format description is wire-format/byte-parsing data, and `mSampleRate` (`Float64`) is mapped to `Double`.
All fields are defaulted to `0u`/`0.0` so a zeroed format description can be built without arguments, matching C's zero-initialised struct.
No `CoreAudio` symbol remains to be stubbed, so no `TODO()` and no unsupported entries are needed.
BitrateStatsInstant is a plain value holder, so it becomes a data class with ULong properties like the Swift UInt64 ones.
BitrateStats mutates its own stored state, so it is translated as a Kotlin class instead of a data class; no copy-on-write value semantics are needed by the algorithm.
private(set) members become public properties with a private setter (totalBytes and latestSpeed).
Swift's default parameter value 100 becomes the ULong default 100uL on the constructor.
add(bytesTransferred:) converts the Int argument with toULong() before adding it to the running total.
The subtraction (100 - speedChangeRate) is kept as unsigned ULong arithmetic, matching the Swift expression exactly.
The smoothing formula uses the same multiplication/addition/division-by-100 ordering as Swift, so results are bit-identical.
The mutating funcs become regular member functions and return BitrateStatsInstant directly, as in the Swift source.
Swift UInt32 bitrate values became Int: this port reserves UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong for wire-format code, and bitrates are never negative.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent; it is stored as a plain nullable reference, so the delegate is not weakly held.
ContinuousClock.Instant mapped to monotonic System.nanoTime() nanoseconds (type Long) so the 15 second expiry test is immune to wall-clock jumps.
swift-collections Deque mapped to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque (firstOrNull peek, addLast, removeFirst).
DateFormatter mapped to java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter with the system default zone, formatting an Instant.
logger.debug mapped to android.util.Log.d with tag "AdaptiveBitrate".
The Swift method-name typo logAdaptiveAcion is preserved verbatim so both codebases read side by side.
limitByTransportBitrate keeps Swift's integer arithmetic (17 * transportBitrate) / 10 using maxOf/minOf on Long.
The caseless Swift `enum AudioSpecificConfig` used only as a namespace becomes a Kotlin `object` holding three nested `enum class` types, preserving the nesting and declaration order.
UInt8 raw values are mapped to UByte (MPEG-4 ASC values are byte-level wire data); literal values use the `u` suffix.
Each enum gets a `companion object` with `fromRawValue(value: UByte)` to mirror the `init?(rawValue:)` initializer Swift synthesizes for raw-value enums.

Enum case names are kept byte-identical to the Swift names (lowerCamelCase, e.g. `aacLc`, `hz44100`, `frontLeftAndFrontRight`) so the two codebases can be read side by side instead of being renamed to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
`SamplingFrequency.sampleRate` (Float64) becomes a computed `val sampleRate: Double` implemented with a `when (this)` expression; the values and their order match the Swift switch.
No imports are required; the file only declares nested enums and one numeric mapping.
No Apple platform frameworks are used, so nothing needed a TODO().
Data is mapped to ByteArray; the private(set) setters become Kotlin 'private set'.
top-level 'let nalUnitEmulationPreventionByte' becomes a top-level const val of type UByte to stay in wire-format semantics.
UInt8 bit-write APIs use UByte and UInt32 uses UInt, matching the wire-format mapping rules.
Swift Data.insert(at:) has no ByteArray counterpart, so insertEmulationPreventionByteIfNeeded reallocates the buffer and copies both segments with ByteArray.copyInto.
Swift '|=' on a Data byte is expressed as an explicit toInt() or mask then toByte().
The emulation-prevention toggle is kept as a private val field declared after data/bitOffset to preserve the Swift declaration order.
writeRawBytes keeps 'self.data += data' as an explicit this.data = this.data + data assignment.
URL extension becomes a java.net.URI extension because this file parses URL components, not a stored string.

absoluteWithoutAuthenticationString rebuilds the URI with the 7-argument java.net.URI constructor passing a null userInfo, which drops both user and password; java.net.URISyntaxException is caught with runCatching.
When the URI has no user info the original toString() is returned verbatim, so URIs are not needlessly re-normalised.
dictionaryFromQuery works on rawQuery and percent-decodes names and values itself; the '+' character is kept literal, matching Foundation's URLComponents.
Query items without '=' are skipped, matching the Swift `if let value` check.
The helper percentDecode is a private top-level function used only by dictionaryFromQuery.
Malformed percent escapes are decoded leniently instead of yielding an empty map as URLComponents would.
File-scope `let defaultStunServer` becomes a top-level `const val defaultStunServer` with the identical name and value.
`setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` keeps its signature but its body only calls `rtcInitLogger`, which comes from the libdatachannel C library; no Kotlin binding exists in this port, so the body is a TODO().
The debug-log callback would have been translated to `android.util.Log.i` with the class name as tag, but it is unreachable because the registration call is a TODO().
No Apple-only framework is used here; the only missing piece is the native WebRTC logger bridge.
When a JNI wrapper for libdatachannel is added, `setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` should register a callback that forwards the C string to `Log.i("WebrtcCommon", "webrtc: $message")`.
Two top-level Swift functions become top-level Kotlin functions in com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.twitch.
The Swift switch with implicit case values becomes a Kotlin `when` expression returning Int, with the same 1/2/3/default mapping.
The Swift tuple (moving:still:) has no Kotlin equivalent, so it is modelled by a small data class TwitchEmoteUrls with properties in the same order.
URL is translated to String because these URLs are only built and passed on for image loading, never parsed.
The Swift optional return survives a failing URL(string:) call; Kotlin string concatenation cannot fail, so the nullable return type is kept only for call-site fidelity.
No Apple framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Crc32 remains a class with a private constructor and a companion object holding the single `mpeg2` instance, mirroring Swift's `static let mpeg2`.
Swift `Data` becomes `ByteArray`; CRC arithmetic keeps unsigned semantics with `UInt`/`UIntArray` since this is wire-format bit math.
Kotlin's infix bitwise functions (`and`, `shl`, `xor`) are all left-associative and bind looser than `==`, so the Swift expressions were parenthesised to keep the exact same evaluation order.
The Swift constructor parameter `polynomial` is kept as a constructor parameter, not a property, and is only used while building the lookup table.
The table build loop, the 0xFFFFFFFF seed and the byte-sequential update loop are translated literally, including the wrap-around `shl 24` for indices 128..255.
`data[i].toUInt() and 0xFFu` reproduces Swift's `UInt32(data[i]) & 0xFF`, so negative bytes cannot sign-extend into the index.
No Apple platform framework is used in this file, so nothing is stubbed with TODO().
@MainActor is translated to a CoroutineScope bound to Dispatchers.Main, so both handlers run on the main thread exactly like the main-queue DispatchSourceTimer in Swift.

DispatchSourceTimer single-shot and repeating schedules become coroutine Jobs driven by delay(): the single shot delays 'timeout' then runs, the periodic timer delays 'initial ?? interval', runs, then loops with 'interval' delays.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for delay(); sub-millisecond precision is lost.

The Swift 'isolated deinit { stop() }' has no deterministic Kotlin counterpart because Kotlin objects are not deinitialized eagerly; callers must call stop() (the timer Job keeps the scope alive otherwise).
The stored 'timer' property keeps its Swift name and now holds a Job? instead of an optional DispatchSourceTimer.
stop() cancels the Job and resets the property to null, matching timer?.cancel(); timer = nil.
The 'initial: Double? = nil' optional parameter is preserved as a Kotlin nullable parameter with a default value.
The `handler` closure becomes a nullable `(String) -> Unit` property; call it with `handler?.invoke(line)`.
The `@autoclosure` parameter of `debug` is translated to a `() -> String` lambda so the message is only evaluated when `debugEnabled` is true.
Swift's `DateFormatter` is replaced by a thread-safe `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter` held in the companion object; `Instant.now()` is converted with the system default zone before formatting.

The compile-time `#if DEBUG` print is replaced by an unconditional `android.util.Log.d` with tag `EasyLogger`; R8/ProGuard or a `BuildConfig.DEBUG` check can be added if release stripping is required.
The global `nonisolated(unsafe) let logger` becomes a top-level `val logger`, initialised once when the file's class is loaded.
`makeTimestamp` and `log` stay `private` instance members and the timestamp prefix format `HH:mm:ss.SSS` is preserved byte-for-byte.
`nonisolated(unsafe)` has no Kotlin counterpart; the singleton is a plain top-level property whose mutable state is not synchronised (same as the Swift original).
Swift enums used purely as namespaces of static constants become Kotlin objects.
UInt16 port constants are translated to Int (const val) because java.net Socket/ServerSocket/DatagramSocket APIs take Int ports and the values fit comfortably.
Values are compile-time constants so they use const val, mirroring Swift 'static let' semantics.
Names and declaration order are preserved exactly for side-by-side reading.
No Apple frameworks, so the unsupported list is empty.
OSAllocatedUnfairLock has no Android counterpart and is replaced by java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock (non-fair, like the Swift lock) used through kotlin.concurrent.withLock.
The Swift Sendable constraints are dropped: Kotlin generics are unconstrained, so Atomic<A> and mutate<R> are plain generics.
Swift's inout A cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so mutate hands the transform a nested mutable holder MutableRef<A>; callers read and write ref.value instead of using $0.
Atomic is a class rather than a data class because instances own a lock and mutable state; value semantics would copy the lock.
value stays a read-only property whose getter reads the state under the lock, mirroring Swift's computed var.
mutate executes the transform while holding the lock and returns R unchanged; the primary constructor parameter is named initialValue to avoid shadowing the value property.
Call sites such as atomic.mutate { $0.count += 1 } become atomic.mutate { it.value.count += 1 }.
No Apple-only framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Swift Data becomes ByteArray; the private(set) data property stays publicly readable but is mutated through local copies, matching Swift value semantics.
UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 map to UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong because this is wire-format byte handling; Int32 maps to Int.
The Data.bigEndian.data and Double.data.reversed() extensions from the HaishinKit extensions file are inlined with java.nio.ByteBuffer using BIG_ENDIAN order.
writeBytes(UnsafeRawBufferPointer) is translated to an overload taking java.nio.ByteBuffer, consuming its remaining bytes via duplicate() so the caller's position is untouched.
In sequence(_:lambda:) the trailing `data.advanced(by: data.endIndex - r)` is treated as the remainder slice data[count-r ..< count] and wrapped in a new ByteWriter.
UInt32(data:) used by toUInt32() is reimplemented inline reading 4 bytes big-endian from the region starting at position.
Both Swift initialisers are kept as Kotlin secondary constructors.
The subscript is translated to operator get/set with UByte values, writing into the backing signed ByteArray.
Data maps to ByteArray and the private(set) var data becomes a var with a private setter; the Swift init(data:) becomes the primary constructor in the class header.
The private Swift.Error enum is translated to a private sealed class Error with the nested objects eof and utf8 so thrown failures keep the same names.

readUInt16 and readUInt32 no longer use the UnsafeRawBufferPointer helpers (which do not exist in Kotlin) and assemble the bytes explicitly big-endian, matching the high/low ordering of readUInt64 and the separate readUInt16Le/readUInt32Le variants.

readDouble keeps the Swift semantics verbatim: it consumes 8 bytes, reverses them and decodes them as a little-endian double, which is identical to decoding the untouched bytes big-endian as AMF0 requires.
defer { position += n } became an explicit increment placed after the read value has been captured.
readUtf8Bytes uses a strict UTF-8 decoder with CodingErrorAction.REPORT so malformed input throws Error.utf8 exactly like Swift's String(data:encoding:).
Unsigned wire values use UByte, UShort, UInt and ULong; callers outside this file therefore see Kotlin unsigned types.
skipBytes and readBytes keep the length >= 0 precondition and throw Error.eof on short buffers.
DispatchSourceTimer + DispatchQueue are replaced by a CoroutineScope backed by the given CoroutineDispatcher; the timer field holds the running Job.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for kotlinx.coroutines delay.
Swift's deinit calling stop() becomes AutoCloseable.close(), which calls stop(); callers should call close() when done.
The handler is a plain () -> Unit lambda; @Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
startPeriodic fires the first handler invocation after `initial ?: interval` and then repeats every interval, matching the Swift schedule.
startSingleShot and startPeriodic still call stop() first, so a previously running timer is always cancelled.

Swift's Data byte-reading extension methods (getUInt16Be/getUInt32Be) are not declared in this file and no shared byte-reader package was provided, so they are re-implemented here as file-private helpers readUInt16Be/readUInt32Be on ByteArray.
16-bit and 32-bit wire values are kept as UShort/UInt as prescribed for byte-parsing code; callers using the packet type should use SrtPacketType.fromRawValue(type).
packet[0] is a signed Byte in Kotlin, so the Swift UInt8 mask test became (packet[0].toInt() and 0x80) == 0.
SRT sequence numbers rely on wrapping unsigned arithmetic; Kotlin's UInt operators already wrap, so Swift's &- is no longer needed in processSrtNak.
SrtPacketType keeps the Swift lowerCamelCase entry names so both files can be read side by side; rawValue stays a UShort with identical raw values.
Swift's guard offset <= packet.count - 4 else { return } became an early return; the guard ... else { continue } became if (upToNakSn - fromNakSn >= 100_000u) continue.
The Swift closed range fromNakSn ... upToNakSn maps to fromNakSn..upToNakSn; a descending range is empty in Kotlin instead of trapping as it does in Swift (only reachable in a wrap-around edge case).
srtControlTypeSize is a const val Int and srtControlPacketTypeBit stays a top-level val UShort, matching the file-scope lets in Swift.
Keychain is backed by androidx.security:security-crypto EncryptedSharedPreferences (1.1.x) with a MasterKey using AES256_GCM; keys use AES256_SIV and values AES256_GCM.

The Swift version got the security context implicitly; here the application Context must be assigned to Keychain.appContext at app start, otherwise store/load/remove log and no-op and loadStreamIds returns an empty list.

Each server maps to its own encrypted preferences file named 'moblin_keychain_' + SHA-256 hex of the server, so that the static loadStreamIds(server) can enumerate all account names (streamIds) belonging to that server, like the kSecAttrServer query did.
Each streamId is the SharedPreferences key inside its server's file, matching kSecAttrAccount.

update/add use commit() instead of apply() so the Swift success/failure logging semantics are preserved; SharedPreferences has no separate update vs add, so update() only succeeds when the key already exists and store() falls back to add().
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "Keychain" (the class name).
The Swift guard on value.data(using: .utf8) is dropped since Kotlin String -> UTF-8 conversion cannot fail.
SharedPreferences files are cached per server in a synchronized map, and creation failures (GeneralSecurityException/IOException) are caught and logged like the original keychain status errors.
CMVideoDimensions is a CoreMedia struct with no Android counterpart, so it is mapped to android.util.Size; the Swift extension methods become top-level Kotlin extension functions on Size.
The @retroactive Equatable conformance needs no Kotlin code: android.util.Size already implements equals()/hashCode().
toSize() returns android.util.SizeF, the Float width/height analogue of CGSize (CoreGraphics CGFloat -> Float per the port rules).
convertTo(dimension:) keeps the Swift optional return type (Size?) and the odd-size rounding: the derived dimension is incremented when it is odd; it never actually returns null.
Int32 arithmetic maps to Kotlin Int; Swift traps on overflow while Kotlin wraps, which is unreachable for realistic video dimensions.
`public import AVFoundation` has no Kotlin equivalent; only android.util.Size and android.util.SizeF are imported.
Function names, parameter names and body order follow the Swift source; visibility is Kotlin's default public so other port files can call them.
ObservableObject with @Published became a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow named followUser / followHeading, matching the _name/name convention.

Because Swift hand-writes encode(to:) and init(from:) over @Published properties, the class uses @Serializable(with = SettingsNavigationSerializer::class) and a hand-written KSerializer that mirrors the Swift container encode/decode calls.
The Swift decoder defaults were false for both keys; deserialize() starts both locals at false so a missing key keeps the Swift behaviour.
The nested CodingKeys enum kept its name and nesting and stores the serialized key string in stringValue (the CodingKey.stringValue counterpart).
The Swift no-argument init() is preserved as a secondary constructor that delegates to the internal primary constructor with false/false.
The primary constructor is internal so the serializer in the same package can build an instance, matching the Swift required init(from:) role.
No Apple-only frameworks are used in this file, so nothing was replaced with TODO().
No comments were added; the full file is a single Kotlin file in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift Character (grapheme cluster) indexing is translated to Kotlin UTF-16 Char indexing, so matches can differ for strings containing combining marks or non-BMP emoji.
The Swift `for shift in minShift ... maxShift` closed range can never be empty here because minShift <= 0 <= maxShift, so Kotlin's `minShift..maxShift` is safe.
Swift `func update(text newText: String)` becomes `fun update(newText: String)`; the external label is dropped as Kotlin has no argument labels.
`String.index(_:offsetBy:)` calls are replaced by direct Char indexing, with the same bounds guarantees (endOffset keeps offset + shift within oldText).
`abs`, `minOf` and `maxOf` come from kotlin.math and the Kotlin stdlib and preserve the original comparison semantics exactly.
Exactly one edit remains: there is no edit, as the source is pure logic with no Apple frameworks.
The `text` property stays private and is only mutated inside `update`; `position` remains a public var so callers keep the same API.
No coroutines, serialization or platform APIs are needed; the file is a self-contained class.
Subtitles is a plain class; the Swift `let length` computed in init becomes a Kotlin `val length` assigned once in an init block.
String length/indexing uses Kotlin UTF-16 offsets (`text.length`, `substring`) instead of Swift Character-based indices, so offsets differ for text containing surrogate pairs such as emoji.
`max(lastLinePosition, 0)` becomes `maxOf(lastLinePosition, 0)` since `max` is removed from Kotlin stdlib.
`.trim()` maps to Kotlin's built-in `String.trim()`, which trims whitespace like Moblin's String.trim() extension, so no extra extension is declared here.
The inner `offset` that shadows the outer one in updateSubtitles is kept with the same name for side-by-side readability (Kotlin emits a shadowing warning only).
`var lines: [String]` becomes `MutableList<String>` and array literals become `mutableListOf(...)` since `lines` is reassigned.
The `guard` statements become early returns, including the `offset < text.count` guard inside the firstLinePosition branch.
ObservableObject with @Published properties became private MutableStateFlow backing fields with public StateFlow exposure; setEnabled/setMicId replace direct assignment from outside.
The hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) pair is realised by SettingsTalkbackSerializer, attached with @Serializable(with = ...), so the class itself keeps no serialization boilerplate.

Persisted JSON keys remain exactly "enabled" and "micId"; the private surrogate EncodedSettings carries @SerialName for both and gives them the Swift defaults (false / ""), so missing keys decode to the same values kotlinx.serialization fallback gave in Swift.
The nested CodingKeys enum is kept as an enum class with a rawValue property and a companion fromRawValue, matching the Swift coding keys byte for byte.
The empty Swift init() is the implicit no-arg Kotlin constructor; SettingsTalkback() is used by the deserializer to build the instance before applying decoded values.
EncodedSettings is an internal implementation detail of the port and has no counterpart in the Swift source.
any Encoder / any Decoder maps to kotlinx.serialization Encoder / Decoder.
CMVideoDimensions is not given a mapping in the port spec; it is translated to android.util.Size, which has the same width/height shape and value equality.
convertTo(dimension:) is assumed to be a top-level extension function on Size declared in this same package (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension), so it needs no import here.
Swift Testing struct becomes a JUnit 4 class; @Test func becomes @Test fun with org.junit.Test.
#expect(a == b) becomes assertEquals(b, a) with kotlin.test, keeping the argument order of the Swift expectation.
There is no suite-level init in the Swift struct, so no @Before fun setUp() is generated.
All width/height literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift suite.

Swift's custom init that divides by the reference image size is kept as a companion operator invoke; the primary constructor is private so call sites keep the swift spelling AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle(topLeftX = 40.0, ...).
The two file-level size constants stay private top-level const vals, matching Swift's private file scope.
AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle maps to a data class with val fields so equality and copy() behave like the Swift struct.
width() and height() stay functions (not properties) so the two codebases read side by side.
AlertsEffectFaceLandmark is an enum class; the Swift case order is preserved.
AlertsEffectLandmarkSettings is a data class with the same four val fields.
The four global rectangles are top-level vals initialised with named arguments, exactly as in Swift.
No platform frameworks are used, so there are no TODO markers.
Swift struct became a Kotlin class because it holds mutable state and methods, not a data class.
static let fixedSectionSize is exposed via a companion object property; instance code reads it as fixedSectionSize.
Data is mapped to ByteArray; Data(repeating:count:) became ByteArray(size) { 0xFF.toByte() }.
UInt8 wire values are kept as UByte as required by the byte-parsing rule; arithmetic is done in Int and converted back with toInt()/toUByte().
Swift truncatingIfNeeded conversions map directly to Int.toUByte() truncation.
reader.position is read through .toInt() so the code compiles whether the ByteReader exposes an Int or Long position.
The throwing initializer just lets ByteReader/ByteWriter exceptions propagate, matching Swift's throws.
readUInt8() is normalized to Int for bit-flag tests to avoid Kotlin unsigned bitwise pitfalls.
Swift `throw "..."` (String errors) become IllegalStateException; callers catching strings must switch to try/catch on IllegalStateException.
Data -> ByteArray: `data.advanced(by: byteOffset)` maps to `data.copyOfRange(byteOffset, data.size)`, which yields the same zero-based tail slice.
UInt8/UInt32 are kept as UByte/UInt because this is wire-format bit parsing; values are assembled via Int/UInt arithmetic and converted back.
The UInt8 `isBitSet(index:)` helper is inlined as `((byte.toInt() shr bitOffset) and 1) == 1` so no extra extension is needed; signed bytes shift correctly because only bit 0 is kept.
byteOffset and bitOffset are regular vars rather than a primary-constructor property so the Swift declaration order is preserved.
`nalUnitEmulationPreventionByte` is a same-package top-level val, so it is used directly with `.toByte()` to compare against the signed ByteArray element.
`try` is dropped everywhere; Kotlin propagates the IllegalStateException implicitly, so no @Throws annotation is required for Kotlin callers.
The Zero byte comparisons `data[i] == 0` become `data[i] == 0.toByte()` since Kotlin Bytes are signed.

TranslationSession, TranslationError and Locale.Language come from the translation shim (platform/translation) on Android's on-device TranslationManager; Locale.Language is java.util.Locale and .init(identifier:) is localeLanguage(identifier = ...).
session.translate(text) is a suspend call; the Swift Task { @MainActor in } becomes mainScope.launch on Dispatchers.Main.
catch let error as TranslationError reports error.failureReason ?: error.localizedDescription, Apple's English failure reasons; other errors are only logged, as in Swift.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped; @MainActor static var translators becomes a companion object MutableList.
The weak delegate maps to a plain nullable property.
CMTime is ported to Long microseconds, so every expectation is asserted as a microsecond duration instead of a value/timescale pair.
Private helper cmTimeMicroseconds(value, timescale) replaces the CMTime(value:timescale:) initializer used by the Swift suite.
Assertions on .value and .timescale are folded into the single equivalent microsecond duration because the ported representation no longer stores them.
The unrelated-timescales addition can only be asserted after truncation (334_333 us for the exact 1003/3000 ratio).
Tests that depend on timescale quantisation (preferredTimescale, e.g. 0.333 s, 0 s, value 30000) have no counterpart in the microsecond port and are TODO.
The Swift suite has no init, so no @Before setup method is emitted.
Test class uses JUnit 4 with kotlin.test assertions, matching the port's test tier.
No Moblin types are imported: the file only exercises numeric duration arithmetic.
apple_only: no Android counterpart for CMTime preferredTimescale quantization

notes: Swift static-only enum becomes a Kotlin object; sigSize and protocolVersion are exposed as const val with the same names.

UInt8.random(in: 0...UInt8.max) becomes Random.nextInt(0, 256).toUByte(); the 1528 filler bytes are generated with repeat().

ByteWriter methods are called with the same names as the Swift source (writeUInt8, writeInt32, writeUInt32, writeBytes) and its result buffer is read through the 'data' property, assumed to be ByteArray.

Swift's Int64(x)/Int32(x) truncation maps to toLong()/toInt(), which also truncate toward zero, so negative spiked values behave identically.

logAdaptiveAcion(actionTaken:) is not declared here and is assumed to be inherited from AdaptiveBitrate in the same package; it is called by name with a named argument.

The multi-line Swift strings with a trailing backslash continuation are emitted as a single concatenated Kotlin string.

The Android-only SharedPreferences seed-on-first-use and `setup()` fallback behaviour of the current Kotlin file is untouched.

Swift Testing struct Md5Suite becomes a JUnit 4 class; @Test maps to org.junit.Test.

The Swift `var expected` reassignment pattern is kept so the two files read side by side.

Digest bytes are byte-identical to the Swift expectations; no hex string was altered.
FileManager.default has no Android counterpart, so the fileManager property was dropped and file operations use java.io.File / java.nio.file.Files directly.

Files.delete in remove(id:) throws when the file is missing, matching FileManager.removeItem(at:).
Swift Testing struct SrtSuite became a JUnit 4 class using org.junit.Test and kotlin.test assertions.

makeNakPacket stays a private top-level helper in the same file; Data(count: 16) became ByteArray(16) and Data became ByteArray.
UInt32 sequence numbers became UInt, matching the wire-format rule for ByteWriter.writeUInt32 and processSrtNak's callback.

The test data helper lives at the top of the same file, per the test-tier rules.

ContinuousClock.Instant maps to Long holding monotonic nanoseconds (System.nanoTime() base); use it only for elapsed-time arithmetic.
Date maps to java.time.Instant.

WeatherCondition becomes String (the WeatherKit case name that com.moblin.android.platform.weatherkit gives), Measurement<UnitTemperature> becomes Double? in degrees Celsius and Measurement<UnitSpeed> becomes Double? in metres per second, the units of the weatherkit shim.
heartRates keeps nullable values, so the Kotlin type is Map<String, Int?>.
runningMetrics values come from WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics (com.moblin.android.integrations.workoutdevice) and gForce from GForce (com.moblin.android.various.managers).
Swift Testing struct WorkoutDeviceCyclingPowerSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
powerMeasurement and powerAndCrankMeasurement stay file-private top-level helpers building the little-endian cycling-power measurement payloads byte for byte.
Int16 power -> Short, so call sites use e.g. 200.toShort(); revolutions and eventTime stay Int since they are only written little-endian into the payload.
Self-referencing try on handleMeasurement is dropped: the Kotlin handleMeasurement(value: ByteArray): Pair<Int, Int?> does not throw.
#expect(power == 100) -> assertEquals(100, power), #expect(cadence == nil) -> assertNull(cadence), #expect(cadence == 90) -> assertEquals(90, cadence).
Results do not depend on locale or time zone, so no @Config qualifiers or TimeZone setup is needed.
Swift Testing suite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; every @Test func keeps its name.
#expect(try x == true/false) on Booleans became assertTrue/assertFalse, other equality checks became assertEquals(actual-first-order swapped).
Hex byte literals above 0x7F need .toByte(); Data([...]) literals became byteArrayOf(...).
Data equality is asserted with assertContentEquals because Kotlin ByteArray uses identity-based equals.
Numeric reader results are compared via toLong() so Int, Long, UInt or ULong return types from NalUnitReader all compile and compare correctly.
#expect(throws: (any Error).self) maps to assertFailsWith<Throwable>, the closest analogue of Swift's any Error.
The Swift suite has no init block, so no @Before fun setUp() was emitted.
NalUnitReader is in the same package as this test, so no import is needed; its constructor is called positionally as (data, offset).
@MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped; these classes are plain classes and callers must ensure main-thread access.
The failable Swift init? becomes a private primary constructor plus a companion operator fun invoke returning RemoteControlRelay? so call sites keep the RemoteControlRelay(...) form.
Swift URL values are stored as String; java.net.URI is used only to validate the control URL the way URL(string:) did.
Decodable structs became kotlinx.serialization @Serializable data classes; Kotlin property names already match the Swift coding keys so no @SerialName is needed.
Deque<Connection> maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque using addLast and removeFirstOrNull (popFirst).
logger.info/debug map to android.util.Log.i/d with the tag "RemoteControlRelay".
WebSocketClient is assumed to expose delegate, start(), stop(), send(string) and constructors (url) and (url, loopback) matching the Swift type.
The String -> Data conversion in handleControlMessage is unnecessary and was dropped; decoding uses the raw String.
Added the two new private ByteArray constants djiDeviceModelNone and djiProductTypeOsmoPocket4Pro.
Added the djiDeviceModelNone branch inside the existing when in djiModelFromManufacturerData, calling the new fromNoneDevice helper with the full data.
Added the private fromNoneDevice helper that reads bytes 12..13 and maps djiProductTypeOsmoPocket4Pro to SettingsDjiDeviceModel.osmoPocket4Pro.
Swift slices data[2...3] and data[12...13] stay copyOfRange(2, 4) and copyOfRange(12, 14); Data equality is translated with contentEquals as before.
The branch on a model value of Data([0x00, 0x00]) must stay after the specific model cases and before else, exactly as in Swift.
SettingsDjiDeviceModel.osmoPocket4Pro is referenced; the enum in com.moblin.android.various.settings must gain that entry with rawValue "osmoPocket4Pro" so this file compiles.
All other Kotlin lines are unchanged from the previous translation.
JUnit 4 test class with kotlin.test assertions, mirroring the Swift Testing suite; no suite-level setup existed so no @Before is emitted.

CMTime(value:timescale:) is converted to 90 kHz tick arithmetic; timescale 90000 with value 0 maps to the Long microsecond/millisecond timestamp 0L used by the ported MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream.

CMTime.invalid has no direct Kotlin analog in this port; TSTimestamp.invalid is used as the sentinel for decodeTimeStamp. Adjust if the ported MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream declares decodeTimeStamp as a plain Long sentinel.
Data([0x65]) becomes byteArrayOf(0x65); Data(repeating: 1, count: n) becomes ByteArray(n) { 1 } so byte values stay identical.
arrayOfPackets(256, true, nil) becomes arrayOfPackets(256, true, null); the program clock reference argument is passed as 1234L for the two PCR tests.
packets.count becomes packets.size and MpegTsPacket.size is referenced as the companion constant of the ported packet type.
All types under test (MpegTsPacket, MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream, TSTimestamp) live in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg, so no imports for them are required.
AVFoundation import was dropped; no AVFoundation symbols are used in the test bodies.
UInt32 bitrate parameters/returns map to Int (bitrates are not wire-format here) and all Int64 arithmetic maps to Long.
adaptiveBitrateRistFastSettings is a top-level val, exactly like the other adaptive bitrate settings globals in this package.

Assumes the base AdaptiveBitrate exposes a nullable/protected delegate, logAdaptiveAcion(actionTaken:) and open overridable members setTargetBitrate/setSettings/getCurrentBitrate/getCurrentMaximumBitrateInKbps/getFastPif/getSmoothPif/update.
StreamStats.packetsInFlight and StreamStats.rttMs are Double (the Swift arithmetic requires it), while AdaptiveBitrateSettings.packetsInFlight and the other settings integers are Long.
stats.limitByTransportBitrate(currentMaximumBitrate) is called with one positional argument, i.e. as it is declared in the StreamStats translation.
The Swift check Int32(fastPif - smoothPif) > settings.packetsInFlight * 2 is performed in Long because packetsInFlight is 64-bit in Kotlin.
Multi-line Swift log messages are collapsed into single-line strings.
The unused Swift import of Collections is dropped.
Tests are plain JUnit 4 @Test methods; Swift `throws` disappears because Kotlin has no checked exceptions.
Assumes MobcamStreamMessageReader.read() returns Pair<MobcamStreamMessageType, ByteArray>? and append() takes a ByteArray, so `.0`/`.1` become `.first`/`.second`.

Assumes ByteReader(data) exposes readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16(): UShort, readUInt32(): UInt, readUInt64(): ULong, readBytes(count): ByteArray; results are compared via toInt()/toLong() so numeric literals still work.
Assumes the pack helpers take a ULong presentation timestamp plus a ByteArray payload (wire format types kept unsigned).
Swift `Data == Data` comparisons became kotlin.test assertContentEquals on ByteArray.
JSONDecoder for the device hello payload became kotlinx.serialization Json.decodeFromString over the UTF-8 decoded bytes.
Hex byte literals above 0x7F (0x90, 0x80, 0xBB) need an explicit .toByte() in Kotlin.
`mobcamStreamProtocolVersion + 1` is written as `(mobcamStreamProtocolVersion.toInt() + 1).toByte()` to stay valid for any integral type of the constant.
WavSuite is a JUnit 4 class: @Test methods use org.junit.Test and assertions come from kotlin.test.
Swift #expect(wav == createMonoWav(...)) on Data became assertContentEquals, because Kotlin ByteArray == compares references rather than contents.
ByteWriter methods are assumed to take wire types: writeUInt32Le(UInt), writeUInt16Le(UShort), writeUTF8Bytes(String), and expose data: ByteArray, per the byte-parsing mapping rule.
Int16 -> Short; UInt16(bitPattern: sample) -> sample.toUShort(), which preserves the same 16 bits. UInt32(...) -> .toUInt(), UInt16(...) -> .toUShort().
createWav is assumed to be (sampleRate: Int, samples: List<List<Short>>): ByteArray; it lives in this same package so it is not imported.
The Swift line comments (int16, Mono/Stereo, sample rate, 192 kbps) were dropped because comments are not allowed in the output; the byte values are unchanged.
List literals of Int16 are built with listOf(...).map { it.toShort() } to avoid implicit Int literal narrowing.
zip(...) with tuple destructuring became samplesRight.zip(samplesLeft) inside for ((a, b) in ...).
Swift's weak var processor becomes a nullable Processor property; JVM GC handles the weak semantics without an explicit WeakReference here.
Swift's unlabeled first parameter of update(_:_:) maps to a named parameter presentationTimeStamp in Kotlin, consistent with reading order of the source.
Int(fps) truncation is preserved with fps.toInt().
Integer division framesCounter / 2 matches Swift Int division exactly.
nextFpsReportTime == 0 becomes == 0.0 on the Double property.
The delegate call is chained as processor?.delegate?.streamVideoFps(fps) to preserve Swift's optional chaining.
Swift Testing #expect became kotlin.test assertEquals/assertNull inside a JUnit 4 class (org.junit.Test).
ByteArray literals with values above 0x7F (0x8D, 0xCF, 0xFF, 0x80, 0xC0, 0xF1) need .toByte() in Kotlin.
The 'try' before the throwing OptionalHeader initializer is dropped; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, tests declare no throws.
CMTime(value:timescale:) is replaced by a local cmTime(value, timescale) helper that converts to microseconds: value * 1_000_000 / timescale.
CMTime.invalid is replaced by the local constant CM_TIME_INVALID = Long.MIN_VALUE; adjust it to whatever sentinel the ported OptionalHeader actually returns.

Assumed OptionalHeader API: OptionalHeader(), OptionalHeader(data: ByteArray), encode(): ByteArray, getPresentationTimeStamp(): Long, getDecodeTimeStamp(): Long, setTimestamp(presentationTimeStamp: Long, decodeTimeStamp: Long) in microseconds.
Assumed TSTimestamp API: encode(value: Long, marker): ByteArray, decode(data: ByteArray, offset: Int = 0): Long?, dataSize: Int, matching the nil return used by the decodeTooShort case.
optionalHeaderRoundTrip only passes if the port rounds when converting microseconds back to 90 kHz ticks (11111 us <-> 1000 ticks); the 900/90000 case is exact either way.
Swift's `Deque` from the Collections package is replaced by Kotlin's `ArrayDeque` (append/removeFirst map to addLast/removeFirst).
The enum cases keep their lowercase Swift names so `toString()` in the log messages stays byte-identical ("audio"/"video").
`logger.debug` becomes `android.util.Log.d` with the tag "DriftTracker" declared in the companion object.
The Swift labeled tuple `(lower:upper:)` is translated into a private data class `Deviations`, added next to the other private helpers.
In `update` the two `guard let state` bindings shadow each other; Kotlin cannot redeclare a same-scope local, so they are named `mediaState` and `minState` (values are unchanged).
`min(by:)` is translated to `minByOrNull` and `map(\.1.lower).min()` to `minOfOrNull`; tie-breaking for equal deviations differs slightly from Swift.
The Swift multi-line string literals with a trailing `\` continuation are emitted as single-line concatenated strings with identical text.
`formatThreeDecimals` is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various and assumed to take a Double and return a String.
Swift struct with a single stored property becomes a Kotlin data class holding the raw bytes as ByteArray.
The throwing Swift init(reader:) maps to a Kotlin secondary constructor with the same parameter name; Kotlin has no checked exceptions so the signature stays clean.
NalUnitReader.readRawBytes() and NalUnitWriter.writeRawBytes(ByteArray) are imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.
The Swift memberwise initializer is not synthesized because the struct declares a custom init, so only the reader constructor is kept alongside the data property.
Data is mapped to ByteArray; no Apple-only API is used in this file.
Swift enum with associated values becomes a Kotlin sealed class named MpegTsVideoConfig with nested data classes Avc and Hevc.
The AVC and HEVC payload types are imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.avc and com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.hevc as given in the glossary.
Nested case types are named Avc/Hevc so pattern matching on the sealed class reads like the Swift switch over .avc / .hevc.
No behaviour is lost: the file only models the two possible video configs, so every member is preserved.
Consumers in Swift that did `case .avc(let config)` become `is MpegTsVideoConfig.Avc ->` with access to `config`.
No Apple frameworks, coroutines or serialization are involved, so the translation is a direct structural mapping.
The sealed class is declared in the same package as the mpeg helper types, keeping the original directory-to-package mapping.

httpGet from com.moblin.android.common.various is used as `suspend fun httpGet(request: Request): Pair<ByteArray, Response>?` and `suspend fun httpGet(url: String): Pair<ByteArray, Response>?`; verify these signatures against the real helper.
URLRequest.setAuthorization is not in the glossary, so the token is sent as an OkHttp header `Authorization: Bearer <apiToken>` inside createRequest.

Swift coding keys with underscores are preserved as property names (voice_id) and repeated in @SerialName; a private Json with ignoreUnknownKeys = true mirrors JSONDecoder's leniency about extra keys.
Locale(identifier:) is mapped to java.util.Locale.forLanguageTag with '_' replaced by '-'; an empty region or language becomes null exactly like Swift's optional chaining.
Swift's `metadata.split(separator: "|")` omits empty subsequences, so firstMetadataPart returns null for an empty metadata/first part, matching the Swift guards.
generateTts returns the downloaded audio as ByteArray (Swift Data) and decodes TtsMonsterGenerateResponse before fetching the produced URL.
baseUrl is a file-private HttpUrl built once; request paths are appended with HttpUrl.Builder.addPathSegment.
The second `guard let (data, response)` in generateTts is renamed audioData/audioResponse because Kotlin forbids redeclaring a local name in the same scope.
The Swift enum with associated values becomes a sealed class CatPrinterCommandMxw01 with object/data class cases named after the Swift cases.
The failable init?(data:) is translated to a companion operator fun invoke(data: ByteArray) so call sites keep reading CatPrinterCommandMxw01(data); it returns null where Swift returns nil.
CatPrinterCommandId is a file-private enum with a rawValue property and a fromRawValue companion; CatPrinterPrintMode is public with the same shape since catPrinterEncodeImageRow consumes it.
Data -> ByteArray, UInt8 -> UByte (UShort for the little-endian count), [UInt8] rows -> UByteArray, [[UInt8]] -> List<UByteArray>.
reasons.isBitSet(index:) comes from com.moblin.android.common.various, and readUInt8() results are compared against unsigned literals (0x22u).
String(bytes:encoding:.utf8) ?? "unknown" is a strict UTF-8 decode (invalid bytes give null, as in Swift) with the leading BOM stripped, falling back to "unknown".
logger.info(...) becomes Log.i with the class name as tag; the thrown Swift Strings become a file-private CatPrinterCommandException whose toString() is the message, so the logged text matches.

ByteWriter/ByteReader from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and the CrcSwift shim are called with their Kotlin signatures; catPrinterEncodeImageRow and catPrinterWidthPixels are reused from CatPrinter.kt in the same package.
Swift `final class` subclass becomes a plain Kotlin `class` extending the open `RtmpMessage` class.
The superclass initializer is called through Kotlin constructor delegation, so `RtmpAggregateMessage` forwards `RtmpMessageType.aggregate` as the message type.
No other members exist in the Swift source, so the Kotlin class body is empty apart from the inheritance clause.
The enum entry is referenced as `RtmpMessageType.aggregate` to match the Swift case name; align the casing with the sibling RtmpMessageType declaration if that file used uppercase constants.
`RtmpMessage` is imported from the same package `com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.message`, so no extra import statement is required.
No state, no coroutines and no platform APIs are involved; behaviour is identical to the Swift original.
Swift's private Codable structs became private @Serializable data classes; the file-level `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` mirrors JSONDecoder's tolerance of unknown keys.
`OpenAiError` is a sealed class extending Exception so kotlin's Result can carry it; the Swift `description` property is kept and `toString()` returns it (CustomStringConvertible).
`ask` keeps the callback API and now hands back `Result<String>`; the failure type is always OpenAiError, which is a Throwable.

The URLRequest plus setAuthorization/setContentType becomes an OkHttp request built inline; okhttp3.Request is written fully qualified because this file already declares a private `Request` payload type that would otherwise shadow the import.
`URL` is mapped to java.net.URI for the base URL, and the stored url is a plain String built as base + "/chat/completions" so it can be passed to OkHttp.

httpRequest is called as `(okhttp3.Request, (ByteArray?, NetworkResponse?, Throwable?) -> Unit)`, matching the ported helper's shape; success and 429 are checked through `NetworkResponse.statusCode` (200..299, 429) instead of helper properties.
@MainActor has no direct Kotlin equivalent, so every completion is dispatched through a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) held by the class.
`try? JSONDecoder().decode(...)` becomes runCatching { json.decodeFromString(...) }.getOrNull().
Swift struct becomes a Kotlin data class with the same defaulted properties: bitrate, channelsMap and format.
AVAudioFormat and AudioStreamBasicDescription are modelled with android.media.MediaFormat; sample rate and channel count are read via KEY_SAMPLE_RATE and KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer (packetCapacity 1, maximumPacketSize 1024 * channelCount) becomes a ByteArray of that maximum size, because MediaCodec owns the packet buffers on Android.
AAC and Opus are represented by MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_AAC and MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_OPUS.
framesPerPacket (1024 for AAC, 960 for Opus) and MPEG4ObjectID format flags have no MediaFormat counterpart; the platform codec handles packetisation.
private static let maximumNumberOfChannels is a private const in the companion object and is used by makeAudioFormat to clamp the channel count to 2.
Nested enum Format has no raw values, so it stays a plain enum class with aac and opus entries; makeAudioFormat keeps an optional return type to mirror AVAudioFormat?.

AvcSeiPayloadPictureTiming is a class whose properties are private-set vars; the Swift failable init?(reader:) becomes the companion factory fromReader(reader) returning null, because Kotlin constructors cannot be failable.

UInt8/Data were mapped to UByte/ByteArray and NalUnitReader/NalUnitWriter are assumed to expose readBits/readBit/readBitsU32/skipBits and writeBits/writeBit/writeBitsU32/writeBytes/data over those types.
Swift's thrown String errors became IllegalStateException with the identical message text.
The imported global `calendar` is not used: the clock initializer uses java.time Instant/ZoneId on the system zone, which is what Calendar.current.year/.hour would give.
AvcNalUnitSei's throwing init(reader:) is a secondary constructor delegating to a private companion function readPayload(reader) that throws.
The top-level hevc helpers writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are called with the writer argument, matching the Swift call sites.
enum with raw value -> enum class AvcSeiPayloadType with rawValue and fromRawValue; enum with associated value -> sealed class AvcNalUnitSeiPayload with nested data class PictureTiming.
Log.i is used with the class name as tag in place of logger.info.
RtmpMessage is assumed to expose an overridable 'encoded' property of type ByteArray (modeled from the Swift 'encoded: Data'); it is accessed via super.encoded in both accessors.
RtmpMessageType.windowAck is assumed to be the Kotlin enum entry matching the Swift '.windowAck' case; both types live in the same package so no imports are needed.
Swift's UInt32 constructors/initializers become secondary constructors delegating to super(RtmpMessageType.windowAck), since the base class has no no-arg constructor.
size stays a UInt because this class is RTMP wire-format code; byte serialization helpers convert to/from big-endian bytes matching Swift's 'bigEndian.data' idiom.
The setter reads the first 4 bytes big-endian, matching Swift's 'UInt32(data:).bigEndian' net behaviour (zero-fill for short arrays).
Swift's `@unchecked Sendable` has no Kotlin counterpart and was dropped.
`encoded` is fully overridden with a custom getter/setter that delegates to `super.encoded` for lazy caching; this assumes the base `RtmpMessage.encoded` is an open `var ByteArray`.
`Data` equality (`==`/`!=`) is translated to `ByteArray.contentEquals` and `Data.count` to `ByteArray.size`.
`Amf0Encoder.writeUInt8` is assumed to take a `UByte`; the Swift literal `0` becomes `0.toUByte()`.
Swift's `AsValue.string(handlerName)` is translated as the nested case `AsValue.String(handlerName)` of the AMF sealed type.
`logger.info(...)` is translated to `Log.i("RtmpDataMessage", ...)` using a private companion TAG.
`arguments` is declared `MutableList<AsValue>` so `decoder.decode()` results can be appended in the setter.
The inherited `type` property is compared against `RtmpMessageType.amf3Data`, matching the Swift `.amf3Data` case.
Enum entries keep the Swift case names verbatim; RtmpCommandName.fromRawValue(rawValue) returns null instead of the Swift optional, and the call site keeps the '?? .unknown' fallback.

The two Swift initializers became secondary constructors delegating to RtmpMessage(commandType); RtmpMessage is assumed to expose open 'encoded: ByteArray', 'length: Int', 'streamId: UInt32' and 'type'.
`encoded` overrides the base property and uses super.encoded for the cached value exactly like the Swift getter/setter pair (no backing field is generated).

Swift's do/catch became try/catch (e: Exception); Amf0Decoder/Amf0Encoder are assumed to expose decode(), decodeString(), decodeInt(), decodeObject(), bytesAvailable, position, encode(), writeUInt8() and data.
AMF values are built as AsValue.String / AsValue.Number / AsValue.Object / AsValue.Null; those sealed-class constructor names must match the AMF0.kt translation.
logger.info is mapped to Log.i with the class name as tag; Data.hexString() is not part of the glossary, so a private ByteArray.hexString() helper (lowercase hex) is provided at file level.
arguments is exposed as MutableList<AsValue> with a private setter so the in-place append/removeAll semantics of the Swift array are preserved.
The 'length == newValue.count' guard and the public setter write-through to super.encoded are kept unchanged.

RtmpSetPeerBandwidthMessage has no primary constructor: the two Swift inits become secondary constructors, both delegating to super(RtmpMessageType.BANDWIDTH) (assumed to be the existing RtmpMessageType entry for 0x06).

Swift's nested 'enum Limit: UInt8' becomes a nested Kotlin enum class with a UByte rawValue plus Limit.fromRawValue(...) replacing the failable raw-value initialiser; Swift cases hard/soft/dynamic/unknown are written HARD/SOFT/DYNAMIC/UNKNOWN per Kotlin enum conventions.

UInt32 fields stay unsigned (UInt) because they are wire-format values; size.bigEndian.data is produced with a big-endian java.nio.ByteBuffer and UInt32(data:).bigEndian is parsed with ByteBuffer.wrap(value, 0, 4).int.toUInt(), so both directions are big-endian on the wire.
Swift slicing newValue[0 ..< 4] is replaced by ByteBuffer.wrap(value, 0, 4) (offset overload) so no copy of the payload is made.
Data counting, appending and equality map to ByteArray.size, ByteBuffer.put, and contentEquals.
The overridden encoded getter/setter read and write the superclass storage via super.encoded, exactly like the Swift code uses super.encoded.
The payload is always 5 bytes: 4 bytes of size followed by the limit raw value byte, matching the RTMP Set Peer Bandwidth message layout.
No Apple-only frameworks are used, so nothing is stubbed out.
The Swift extension on Model becomes two top-level extension functions on Model in the same package.
Model's members used here (database, sceneSelector, isSceneVideoSourceActive(sceneId:), selectScene(id:)) must be at least internal in the Kotlin Model for these extension functions to compile.
SceneSelector.selectedSceneId is treated as a non-nullable java.util.UUID, matching the Swift non-optional argument passed to isSceneVideoSourceActive(sceneId:).
database.disconnectProtection.fallbackSceneId and liveSceneId are treated as nullable UUID values and unwrapped with ?: return, preserving the Swift guard-let order and short-circuiting.
No explicit java.util.UUID import is needed because the type only appears through inference in this file.
Swift guard ... else { return } is expressed as an early `if (condition) return`, keeping the logic byte-identical.
Swift failable initializer init?(reader:) has no Kotlin constructor equivalent, so it became the companion factory HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode.from(reader:).
Throwing initializers that throw a String now throw IllegalStateException.
private(set) var maps to a Kotlin var with a private setter; the clock initializer stays a public secondary constructor.
readBits/writeBits are assumed to take/return Int and readBitsU32/writeBitsU32 to use UInt; adjust if the ported NalUnitReader/NalUnitWriter use UByte.
Date maps to java.time.Instant and calendar is a java.util.Calendar; it is cloned before mutation so the shared instance is untouched.
logger.info maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are invoked as top-level functions taking the writer, matching their Swift signatures.
UInt8/UInt32 are kept as UByte/UInt because this is wire-format code.
RtmpChunkType becomes a Kotlin enum class with a UByte rawValue and a companion fromRawValue, keeping entry names zero/one/two/three.
The nested ChunkStreamId enum keeps UShort raw values and gets its own fromRawValue companion.
chunkStreamId comparisons are done via toInt() because Kotlin unsigned types do not compare against differently-typed literals.
Data is ByteArray; subdata(in:) becomes copyOfRange and count becomes size.
message.timestamp/streamId are treated as UInt, message.length as a mutable Int, matching the RtmpMessage port in the message package.
Little-endian (chunkStreamId - 64) and big-endian timestamp encodings are written byte-by-byte since Kotlin has no zero-cost byte-order wrapper.
ByteWriter is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and used with writeBytes/writeUInt8/writeUInt24/writeUInt32/writeUInt32Le/data.
The stride(from:to:by:) split loop is reproduced with an equivalent while loop stepping by maximumSize.

The file is now a set of Model extension functions: togglePhotoShoot, setPhotoShootInterval, activatePhotoShoot, handlePhotoTaken plus the file-private start and stop (the old startPhotoShoot/stopPhotoShoot are gone).
photoShootEnabled is a MutableStateFlow in the port, so it is read and written through .value.
photoShoot.photoTaken keeps its MutableStateFlow form (.value) as in the previous Kotlin file; photoShoot.active and photoShoot.nextPhotoTime are written as plain properties.
The two timers moved from Model into the photoShoot object: photoShoot.timer and photoShoot.flashTimer.
start() now uses a single-shot timer and records photoShoot.nextPhotoTime; ContinuousClock.now + .seconds(interval) is translated with the shim's advanced(bySeconds = interval).
stop() clears photoShoot.photoTaken, photoShoot.nextPhotoTime and photoShoot.active.
setQuickButton(type:isOn:) keeps its Swift labels and uses SettingsQuickButtonType.photoShoot, imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
activatePhotoShoot combines the two Swift guard clauses into a single early return.
RtmpUserControlMessage subclasses RtmpMessage(RtmpMessageType.user) through a Kotlin primary constructor; the two Swift initializers map to the primary constructor plus one secondary constructor.
Swift's nested `Event: UInt8` becomes a nested `enum class Event(val rawValue: UByte)` with a companion `fromRawValue`, replacing `Event(rawValue:)`.
The overridden `encoded` property keeps the lazy getter/setter semantics: the getter returns the stored payload when non-empty, otherwise it builds it from `event` and `value` and stores it.
`Data` maps to `ByteArray`; `value.bigEndian.data` is produced by explicit big-endian shift/mask conversion, and the setter parses the tail big-endian.
Where Swift used the inherited `length`, this port reads `super.encoded.size` to avoid re-entering the overridden getter (which has side effects).
`Int32` maps to `Int`; `Int32(data:...).bigEndian` is reproduced by reading the trailing bytes big-endian, capped at the 4-byte value width.

Swift `throw "..."` (a thrown String) has no Kotlin counterpart, so the file declares DjiMessageError whose toString() is the message, following the DataChannelError/SrtError convention; it is not an unsupported API.
`CrcSwift.computeCrc8/16` are called with the unsigned literal arguments from the shim (0xEEu, 0x31u, 0x496Cu, 0x1021u) exactly like the Swift call.
ByteReader methods do not throw in Kotlin, so every `try reader.readX()` became a plain call and the parsed value is compared directly.
`writer.data` is used verbatim as in Swift for the header and body CRC computations and for the returned bytes.
`value.utf8Data` / `url.utf8Data` map to `String.toByteArray()` (UTF-8), and the UInt8 truncation of the length is `(size and 0xFF).toByte()`.
`payload.hexString()` has no ported counterpart in the glossary, so a file-private lowercase-hex ByteArray.hexString() is defined in this file.
`DjiMessage` is a non-final Swift class, so it is an `open class` with `open` members; `init(data:)` is a secondary constructor delegating to the primary one.
The Swift local `let data = data.subdata(...)` shadow is renamed payloadData to avoid shadowing the constructor parameter.
ChatProvider no longer takes maximumNumberOfMessages; the class has no primary constructor parameter and uses the global maximumNumberOfChatMessages from com.moblin.android.various.model.
Updated appendMessage now drops the oldest paused post once the paused queue exceeds 2 * maximumNumberOfChatMessages - 1, then appends.
update() in the paused branch now reports the full pausedPosts count instead of count - 1.
pause() takes no redLine argument and starts with an empty pausedPosts queue.

Swift's Deque<Action> maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque and popFirst() to removeFirstOrNull().

Task { } becomes mainScope.launch { } on a private file-level CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main); the Model receiver is captured in a local `model` because the launch lambda rebinds `this` to the CoroutineScope.
The private Action enum becomes a private sealed class with Add/Next/Previous/Status data classes and Play/Pause data objects; the switch becomes an exhaustive when.
MusicAddResult becomes a sealed class with Added(song) and the SongNotFound data object, so callers write MusicAddResult.Added(...).
logger.debug maps to Log.d with the tag "ModelMusic"; String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() from package com.moblin.android and error.localizedDescription to e.message ?: e.toString().
makeErrorToast(title = , subTitle = ) is assumed to exist on Model in package com.moblin.android.various.model, as used by the Swift original.
apple_only: MusicKit MusicAuthorization.request()
MusicKit MusicCatalogResourceRequest / MusicCatalogSearchRequest (Song lookup by URL id and search by term)
MusicKit ApplicationMusicPlayer (queue assignment/insertion, play, pause, prepareToPlay, skipToNextEntry, skipToPreviousEntry, state.playbackStatus, isPreparedToPlay)
MusicKit Song and MusicItemID types (findSong result type kept as placeholder Any?)

notes: @MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent; the function is a plain top-level function and callers are responsible for main-thread dispatch.
Swift's count(where:) becomes Kotlin's count { } on the pairs list.
Swift's clamped(to: 1...pages) becomes coerceIn(1, pages) on the Int page property.
Int arithmetic is widened with toDouble() because Swift's Double(...) conversion is implicit in Kotlin's stricter typing.
Behavior when the number of non-empty pages is 0 matches Swift: the clamped range is empty, so the call fails the same way; no extra guard was added.
quickButtons.pairs.isEmpty is assumed to be a Boolean property on QuickButtonPair in com.moblin.android.various.model.

Swift's `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on `Model` in the same package. A Kotlin file cannot add interface conformances, so `Model` must declare `: SpeechToTextDelegate, TranslatorDelegate` (or their Kotlin equivalents); the same-package extension functions then act as the interface implementations.

All Model members touched here must be visible outside Model's own file (at least `internal`): `speechToText`, `speechToTextLatestPosition`, `speechToTextLatestText`, `speechToTextAlertMatchOffset`, `speechToTextTextAligners`, `textEffects`, `browserEffects`, `enabledAlertsEffects`, `widgetsInCurrentScene(onlyEnabled:)`, `makeErrorToast(title:)`, `playAlert(alert:)`.
The `#available(iOS 26.0, *)` guards around the Translation framework are dropped: on Android the ported `Translator` runs unconditionally on the TranslationManager shim.
Swift counts Characters; `text.indexOf(string, startIndex, ignoreCase)` plus `string.length` are used instead, so offsets in the alert matcher are UTF-16 code units.
`Set(widget.widget.text.subtitles.map(\.identifier))` becomes `map { it.identifier }.toSet()` over nullable identifiers with an explicit null check inside the loop.
Assumes the widget model exposes `WidgetType.text` / `WidgetType.alerts` / `WidgetType.browser` and the alert enum case is `Alert.SpeechToTextString(id)` in package com.moblin.android.various.model.
`Translator.translators` is assumed to be a mutable list exposed by Translator's companion object (`clear()` / `add()`).
Swift Testing ValidateSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
isValidUrl and the other validators live in the same package com.moblin.android.common.various, so no imports are needed for them.
#expect(x == nil) maps to assertNull(x) and #expect(x != nil) maps to assertNotNull(x).
The allowedSchemes argument is passed positionally as listOf("srt") so the call does not depend on the Kotlin parameter name.
No suite-level setup exists in the Swift source, so no @Before method is generated.
Swift's private serial DispatchQueue is a top-level single-thread executor dispatcher; write()/flush() launch coroutines on the coroutine scope built from it so ordering is preserved.
The fileManager property was dropped: every FileManager operation maps directly to java.io.File (listFiles, deleteRecursively, createNewFile, length).
URLs are translated to java.io.File because every use is a filesystem path operation (appendingPathComponent, pathComponents, lastPathComponent, fileSize).
FileHandle is replaced by java.io.FileOutputStream opened in append mode, so seekToEnd() is unnecessary; synchronize() maps to FileDescriptor.sync() through the fd property.
contentsOfDirectory(.skipsHiddenFiles) is emulated by listFiles() plus an isHidden filter; non-Log_ entries are deleted recursively like removeItem(at:).
sorted by lastPathComponent becomes sortedBy { it.name }; maximumLogFileSizeBytes is a Long because it is not wire-format/byte-parsing code.
createAndGetDirectory and formatFilenameDateAndTimeIsoish are called positionally as in the Swift source (createAndGetDirectory("Logs")).
LogsStorage is no longer marked @unchecked Sendable; Kotlin shares the class through a confined single-thread dispatcher.
Added activeLiveChatId to YouTubeApiListVideoStreamingDetails with a null default so synthesized Codable decoding stays optional.
Added insertLiveChatBan between listChannels and doGet, keeping the Swift map insertion order (liveChatId, bannedUserDetails, then type/banDurationSeconds).
The Swift [String: Any] snippet body became a kotlinx.serialization buildJsonObject tree, which is what serialize(JsonElement) accepts.
A nil duration produces "type": "permanent"; a non-nil duration adds "type": "temporary" and "banDurationSeconds".
NetworkResponse<Void> maps to NetworkResponse<Unit> as in deleteLiveBroadcast, so success is NetworkResponse.Success(Unit).
Adds the shoutout-create event models, delegate method, subscription type and handler exactly where the Swift diff places them.

Swift Testing struct AudioUnitSuite becomes a JUnit 4 test class, one @Test function per @Test func.
withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer indirection is dropped: the Kotlin helpers take the array plus an explicit count, so tests pass (samples, samples.size) or (samples, 0) for the empty cases.

Int16.min / Int16.max map to Short.MIN_VALUE / Short.MAX_VALUE in shortArrayOf.

The types and helpers under test (AudioUnit, TalkbackPlayer, AudioMeasurement, AudioUnitAttachParams, makeChannelMap, audioFormat, calcAudioLevelPeak*) live in the same package, so no imports are needed for them.

Byte literals with the high bit set keep the explicit `.toByte()` conversion already used in this file.
No new imports were needed; JUnit 4, kotlin.test and Robolectric setup are unchanged.
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; helper functions stay private top-level in this file.
DriftTracker calls are written positionally (DriftTracker(""), addMedia(media, fillLevel), setDrift(value), update(media, ...)) because the Kotlin signatures live in DriftTracker.kt.
createTracker() and drive() keep their Swift names and default nullable audio/video lambda parameters.

The Swift tuple array of (media, closure) pairs becomes a listOf(media to fn) destructured in the for loop, with a `?: continue` guard replacing `guard let`.
DriftTrackerMediaState is not referenced by this file, so it is not imported.
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; each @Test becomes org.junit.Test fun and the struct becomes a plain class.
The private measurement builders keep the exact little-endian wire bytes: 0x02 + UInt16 + UInt16, 0x01 + UInt32 + UInt16 and 0x03 + UInt32 + UInt16 + UInt16 + UInt16.

Wheel revolutions stay unsigned (UInt, UInt.MAX_VALUE for Swift .max) because UInt32.max does not fit an Int; the 16-bit crank wheels and event times use Int with explicit and 0xFF masks inside the helper.
Swift UInt16 overflow 65000 &+ 1024 is written as (65000 + 1024) and 0xFFFF so the helper receives the same wrapped event time 488.
#require(speed) becomes requireNotNull(speed) before calling isEqual(actual, expected, epsilon).
handleMeasurement is called with the declared parameter name value and returns Pair<Double?, Int?> destructured into (speed, cadence).
#expect(throws: (any Error).self) becomes assertFailsWith<Exception>, because the Kotlin translation of the device throws an unchecked exception for a truncated measurement.
No test depends on locale or time zone, so no @Config qualifiers or TimeZone default are needed.
Swift Testing #expect(throws: "msg") { } is translated to kotlin.test assertFailsWith<Exception> plus an equality check on the thrown Throwable's message.
The Swift functions are `throws`; Kotlin has no checked exceptions so the calls are plain (no try/catch needed on the success paths).
@testable import Moblin is dropped because the types under test live in the same package com.moblin.android.media.rtspclient.
Test method names, order and string literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift source.
No suite-level init existed in Swift, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
If the ported error type wraps the text (e.g. prefixes the class name), the assertEquals on error.message must be adjusted to match the ported error's message/description.
Suite struct becomes a JUnit 4 class; kotlin.test assertions replace #expect.
appendTwitchRaidChannel is called with a List of SettingsStreamTwitchRaidChannel and returns the new list, matching the Swift value-semantics helper.
Local `var channels` uses immutable List plus reassignment, mirroring the Swift `var` array.
