Optional first/last uses firstOrNull()/lastOrNull() so the nil-comparison in test 3 ports directly.
maximumNumberOfTwitchRaidChannels and appendTwitchRaidChannel are imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
String interpolation of the loop index produces the same byte-identical channel ids/names as Swift.

The hand-written Codable (encode(to:) / init(from:)) is translated into a custom KSerializer; the wire format keeps the eight flat Swift coding keys via the private SettingsSelfieStickShape surrogate.

@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow backing fields (_enabled, _function, _functionData) exposed as public StateFlow, per the port's convention; mutation happens through the backing flows inside the class.
Swift's init() maps onto the Kotlin primary constructor's default arguments (enabled = false, function = switchScene, functionData = SettingsControllerFunctionData()).
Assumes SettingsControllerFunctionData exposes mutable properties sceneId, widgetId, gimbalPresetId, gimbalMotion, macroId and streamDeckLayoutId with the Swift defaults.
Assumes SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion expose a String rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue(String) returning a nullable enum, so persisted raw values stay byte-identical.
UUIDs are stored as strings; a malformed or missing string decodes to null instead of throwing, matching the Swift decoder's fault tolerance.
The nested CodingKeys enum is kept only for side-by-side parity; the actual keys live in SettingsSelfieStickShape's @SerialName values.
Missing keys fall back to the same defaults as the Swift decoder: enabled=false, function=.switchScene, gimbalMotion=.kapow, ids=nil.
Swift Testing suite RistSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class RistSuite with kotlin.test assertions.
The Swift struct has no init, so no @Before setUp() is emitted.

The second Swift argument .hostPort(host: .init("1.2.3.4"), port: .imap) is an NWEndpoint; since Android has no NWEndpoint, it is passed as RistRemotePeer("1.2.3.4", 143), 143 being NWEndpoint.Port.imap.
Assertion argument order follows the contract: assertEquals(expected, actual).
Expected URL strings are kept byte-identical, including the appended weight=1 query item.
If the ported makeRistMoblinkBondingUrl takes (url: String, host: String, port: Int) rather than a RistRemotePeer, only the third test call needs adjusting.
The Swift tuple return of parse() is translated as Pair<Boolean, HttpConnectRequest?>; tests destructure it with (done, result).
Top-level setup is not needed, so no @Before method is generated.
The destination comparison assumes the ported parser exposes Connection.Endpoint.HostPort(host, port) for the Swift .hostPort(host:port:) endpoint case.
The suite therefore imports nothing from the glossary packages because the test lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.network.
Swift's .utf8Data extension becomes Kotlin's String.encodeToByteArray().
Swift's destructuring reassignment in connectParserSplitAcrossChunks is rewritten with two mutable locals because Kotlin has no multiple assignment.
assertNotEquals and assertFailsWith are not required by this suite, so those imports are omitted.

Added the two new tests notificationActionSurvivesEncodeAndDecode and notificationActionDefaultsWhenMissingFromSettings after ifActionDefaultsWhenMissingFromSettings, matching the Swift diff position.

The new tests refer to SettingsMacrosActionFunction.NOTIFICATION and SettingsMacrosAction.notificationMessage, which the Swift change introduces; the SettingsMacros port must expose those two members for these tests to compile.
Swift .notification maps to the Kotlin enum entry NOTIFICATION following the UpperCamelCase to UPPER_SNAKE convention used by every other case in this enum.
decode/encode still go through kotlinx Json.decodeFromString/encodeToString with the Swift property names, as in the unchanged tests.
Data("{}".utf8) becomes the string literal "{}" passed to Json.decodeFromString, as in the existing default-value tests.
No other line of the file was touched; imports, formatting and declaration order are byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
No iOS API is used in the added code, so there is no TODO marker.

HttpResponseParser.parse() returning the Swift tuple (done, data) is translated as Pair<Boolean, ByteArray?>; each call is destructured, and the second parse in a test uses done2/data2 because Kotlin has no destructuring reassignment.
Byte arrays are compared with assertContentEquals rather than assertEquals because Kotlin ByteArray equality is reference based, unlike Swift Data.
String.utf8Data becomes Kotlin String.encodeToByteArray(), Data() becomes ByteArray(0), and Data.count becomes ByteArray.size.
Data slices body[0 ..< 5] and body[5...] become ByteArray.copyOfRange(0, 5) and copyOfRange(5, body.size).
The AVFoundation import is dropped because it was unused in this suite.
The class is a JUnit 4 test class using kotlin.test assertions; @Test comes from org.junit.Test and there is no setUp because the Swift struct has no init.
#expect(data == nil) is written as assertNull(data).
Assumes HttpResponseParser exposes append(data: ByteArray) and parse(): Pair<Boolean, ByteArray?>.

The hand-written Codable conformance is translated with kotlinx.serialization surrogate classes plus custom KSerializers, keeping the flat CodingKeys (id, key, function, sceneId, widgetId, gimbalPresetId, gimbalMotion, macroId, streamDeckLayoutId).
@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow fields (private _name, public name) exposed through public var accessors so the values stay mutable for decoding and UI edits.
ObservableObject and Identifiable have no Kotlin counterpart; the id property is kept as a plain property.
UUIDs are persisted as strings via UUID.toString()/UUID.fromString(), matching JSONEncoder's treatment of UUID.
Enum raw values are persisted as strings through rawValue.toString() and resolved by scanning the enum entries, so the code does not depend on the raw value's static type.
Missing keys fall back to exactly the same defaults as the Swift container.decode helper: new UUID, empty string, unused, kapow and nulls.
With the default Json configuration (encodeDefaults = false) surrogate fields equal to their defaults are omitted when writing, but decoding always restores them.
SettingsKeyboardKeyData and SettingsKeyboardData are private file-local serialization helpers, not part of the Swift API.
Swift Testing struct RtmpStreamInfoSuite became a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
#expect(a == b) was rewritten as assertEquals(b, a), i.e. the Swift right-hand side is the expected value.
info.bitrateStats.mutate { $0.add(...) } is kept as info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(...) }, assuming the ported stats holder exposes value and mutate (e.g. a MutableStateFlow wrapper).
RTMP acknowledgement sequence numbers are wire format, so onAck takes UInt and its literals carry the u suffix (UInt32 -> UInt, Int32.max -> Int.MAX_VALUE).

Counter fields (totalBytes, latestSpeed, rttMs, packetsInFlight) are asserted as Int, matching the untouched Int usage in the Swift suite.
The async onAckUpdatesRtt test is wrapped in runBlocking and calls the suspend sleep(milliSeconds:) helper from com.moblin.android.common.various positionally.
Assertions come from kotlin.test, the @Test annotation from org.junit.
Swift Testing @Test methods became JUnit 4 @Test functions with kotlin.test assertions (kotlin.test.Test aliases org.junit.Test on the JVM).
#expect(a == b) -> assertEquals(b, a); boolean expectations -> assertTrue/assertFalse, keeping the original order of cases.

Swift's try #require(URL(string:)) has no Kotlin equivalent: java.net.URI parses the same ws/wss strings and throws URISyntaxException on malformed input, which fails the test just like #require returning nil would.
The isLoopback extension is not listed in the glossary, so this file assumes NetworkUtils.kt declares URI.isLoopback() in this same package; no import is needed for a same-package extension.
Dollar signs inside expected/input string literals are escaped as \$ so Kotlin does not treat them as string templates (e.g. "a's\$b 6" and "#\$%^").
The empty Swift tuple array [] maps to emptyList(), whose element type is inferred from the makeUrl parameter type List<Pair<String, String>>.
makeUrl parameters are passed as Kotlin pairs, e.g. listOf("foo" to "bar").
The Swift suite had no init/setUp, so no @Before method is required.
JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions, matching the Swift Testing suite one-to-one.
#expect(optional/boolean) maps to assertTrue, #expect(==) maps to assertEquals with expected first and actual second.
Subtitles lives in this same package, so no import is needed for the type under test.
The Swift multiline string literals using a trailing backslash line continuation were flattened into single Kotlin string literals, preserving the trailing space before each continuation.
Subtitles(languageIdentifier: nil) becomes Subtitles(null).
updateSubtitles(position:text:) becomes updateSubtitles(position, text) as a positional call.
There is no Swift init in the suite, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
Expected line arrays keep the exact byte content, including the intentionally truncated final chunks.

CMTime has no Android counterpart in this port, so every CMTime becomes a Long number of microseconds; a private helper cmTime(value, timescale) in this file reproduces the Swift CMTime(value:timescale:) expressions.
CMTime(seconds:) values are converted with truncation: 0.02 s -> 20000L and 1/71 s -> 1_000_000L / 71 (14084 us, which formats back to 1/71).
CMTime.invalid is represented by the private sentinel invalidExposure = Long.MIN_VALUE and CMTime.zero by 0L; these must match the sentinels used by the implementation in this package.

Assumed signatures of the types under test: factorToExposure(List<Long>, Double): Long, factorFromExposure(List<Long>, Long): Double, exposureFactorStep(List<Long>): Double, formatExposure(Long): String.
Swift Testing struct + @Test func became a JUnit 4 class with org.junit.Test methods and kotlin.test assertions; assertEquals(expected, actual) keeps the Swift operand order.
#expect(a == b) became assertEquals(b, a) so the literal under test stays the expected value, including the empty-string cases in exposureIsFormattedAsFractionOfSecond.
Because exposures are integer microseconds, 1/60 s is 16666 us; the round-trip test still compares against exact list elements so it is unaffected.
The suite has no init/setup, so no @Before method was generated; test data helpers (cmTime, invalidExposure) live as private top-level declarations in this file.
UIGraphicsImageRenderer + CALayer.render(in:) are translated to android.graphics.Bitmap + Canvas + PNG compression with Bitmap.CompressFormat.PNG.

UIColor.white becomes android.graphics.Color.WHITE so ChatLineTextStyle keeps its Int color.

Assumes the ported ChatLineUiView is an android.view.View with a no-argument constructor and size(availableWidth: Float) returning android.util.Size.
Added the two new tests as @Test methods at the end of UtilsSuite, matching the Swift declaration order.
sortedBySearchPrefix lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.utils, so no new import is needed.
The closure { $0 } becomes the trailing lambda { it }.
List literals keep their Swift element order, including the case-sensitive ordering asserted in the first test.
No locale/time-zone dependency, so no assumeTrue guard is added.
All pre-existing lines were kept byte-identical.

JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; the two @Test(arguments: [24, 25, 30, 50, 60]) cases become loops over the same values inside a single @Test method, with the fps included in failure messages.
CMTime maps to Long microseconds, so presentationTimeStamp(frameNumber, fps) returns frameNumber * 1_000_000 / fps (frameNumber/fps seconds).

CMTime.invalid for the decode timestamp is modelled by the file-local sentinel invalidTimeStamp = Long.MIN_VALUE; if MpegTsTimecodeGenerator uses another sentinel (e.g. -1L or a nullable Long?) this constant is the only place to change.

setReference(now:presentationTimeStamp:) kept the Swift units (seconds for 'now' and seconds for the reference timestamp, as required by referenceIsPresentationTimeStampBaseNotTheFirstFrame), so its second argument is written as a bare numeric literal that fits Double/Long/Int.
MpegTsTimecode.clock is java.time.Instant; the private Instant.timeIntervalSince1970 extension restores the Swift accessor (epochSecond + nano/1e9) used all over this suite.

Double.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy:) is Kotlin's % operator on Double.
Hand-written Codable encode/init(from:) become @Serializable classes; Swift coding keys equal the Kotlin property names except assistant -> "client" and streamer -> "server", which use @SerialName.

@Published/ObservableObject/Identifiable are not reproduced: properties stay plain mutable vars so kotlinx.serialization can still persist them. Wrap the whole SettingsRemoteControl object in a StateFlow at the settings-store level if observation is needed.
java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx serializer, so file-private UUID and nullable-UUID serializers are declared at the bottom of the file and used via @Serializable(with = ...).
port: UInt16 became Int; SettingsRemoteControlWeb.port defaults to DefaultTcpPorts.remoteControlWeb (assumed Int, like the rest of the network ports).
kotlinx.serialization uses the property default when a JSON key is missing, so SettingsRemoteControlServerRelay.enabled keeps Swift's in-memory default true rather than the decoder fallback of false.
Same for hasMigratedAssistant = true: a decoded payload that explicitly contains false still runs the assistant -> streamers migration in the init block, a payload without the key does not.
The migration block shadows the streamer property with a local val, exactly like the Swift init(from:); getSelectedStreamerName() uses firstOrNull.
BufferedVideoSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; #expect(a == b) is translated to assertEquals(b, a).
createVideoSampleBuffer returns a com.moblin.android.media.MediaSample instead of a CVPixelBuffer-backed CMSampleBuffer: 1x1 BGRA (4 bytes of data), format = null, key frame = false.
CMTime(seconds: x) maps to presentationTimeUs = (x * 1_000_000).toLong() as the MediaSample carries microseconds.
The Swift precondition checks on CVPixelBufferCreate / CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateForImageBuffer are dropped because no pixel buffer is allocated in the port.
BufferedVideo constructor is called with the same labelled arguments; cameraId: .init() was translated to java.util.UUID.randomUUID(), assuming the port keeps a UUID camera id.
updateSampleBuffer(_:) is assumed to still take seconds as a Double, matching the Swift call site updateSampleBuffer(1.5).
processor: nil becomes processor = null.
The helpers stay private top-level functions in the same file as required for test data helpers.
RtmpChunkType is assumed to be a Kotlin enum class with entries ZERO/ONE/TWO/THREE, a UByte rawValue and a companion fromRawValue; RtmpMessageType is assumed to use fromRawValue(UByte) as well.

ByteReader is expected to expose position: Int (var), bytesAvailable: Int, readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16Le(): UShort, readUInt24(): UInt, readUInt32(): UInt, readUInt32Le(): UInt and a throwing readBytes(count: Int): ByteArray.
messageHeaderSize() is kept as a function call on RtmpChunkType, mirroring the Swift declaration.

RtmpChunkStream in Swift is a struct copied in and out of the dictionary; in Kotlin it is a data class held by reference, so mutations apply to the stored instance. The observable behaviour is identical because every re-entry re-reads the same bytes from the same offset.
Swift's UInt32 timestamps map to Kotlin UInt, chunk stream ids to UShort, in line with the wire-format rule.
Swift's &+ / &+= wrapping arithmetic is preserved implicitly: Kotlin unsigned operators are implemented over signed Int arithmetic and wrap on overflow.
data.subdata(in:) becomes ByteArray.copyOfRange(offset, size); try! becomes a plain call to a throwing ByteReader method.
The private file-level types RtmpBasicHeader and RtmpChunkStream stay private to this file, as in the Swift source.
DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload lost payload1/payload2 and the oa5 flag; its fields now follow the Swift order rtmpUrl, resolution, fps, bitrateKbps.
encode() in both streaming payloads now builds a body ByteWriter and prefixes a length-prefixed header byte 0x00 / 0x01.
DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload2 dropped the header property, its two header constants and the header constructor parameter.
ByteWriter.writeUInt8 takes a UByte, so the literal header bytes are written as 0x00.toUByte() and 0x01.toUByte().
UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: count) stays data.size.toUShort() as in the current Kotlin file.
The hand-written "/" -> "\/" JSON escaping used for the Codable payload was kept.
@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow backing fields plus public read-only StateFlow, as required by the porting rules.

kotlinx.serialization cannot serialize StateFlow fields, so SettingsMoblinkStreamer and SettingsMoblinkRelay use hand-written nested KSerializer objects that read/write the backing flows and always emit every key like Swift's encode(to:).
Swift's custom container.decode(_:_:_:isValid:) fallback is reproduced inside the custom deserializers: a missing key (or a url that fails isValidWebSocketUrl) yields the Swift default value.

CodingKeys server/client of SettingsMoblink do not match its property names, so @SerialName maps streamer->server and relay->client; the nested serializers use the Swift key names directly as descriptor element names.
The Swift UInt16 port is translated to Int because DefaultTcpPorts.moblinkStreamer and the rest of the ported code treat ports as Int; this file is not wire-format code.
SettingsMoblink itself stays a plain @Serializable class since it has no published properties; its nested types are resolved through their @Serializable(with = ...) serializers.
The explicit Swift init() initializers are implicit no-arg constructors in Kotlin; Swift's required init(from:) becomes the nested serialize/deserialize pair.
Swift Testing struct suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from:) becomes Json.decodeFromString<T>(string) with a Json instance configured with ignoreUnknownKeys = true to mirror Swift's default tolerance of extra keys.
Swift raw string #"..."# maps to a Kotlin triple-quoted raw string; the payloads contain no '$' so no escaping is needed.
`throws` test methods become plain @Test methods; decode failures propagate and fail the test as JUnit would.
SettingsMoblinkRelay lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.settings, so no import is required.
CheermotesSuite is a plain JUnit 4 class; the Swift @MainActor annotation and the throws clauses have no Kotlin counterpart and were dropped.
The Cheermotes.getUrlAndBits(word:) signature is unresolved in this file; it is assumed to return Pair<java.net.URI, Int>? based on the Swift URL return value.
URL.absoluteString maps to URI.toString() and URL.lastPathComponent maps to uri.path.substringAfterLast("/") since java.net.URI has no lastPathComponent.
#require(...) maps to kotlin.test.assertNotNull, which returns the non-null value, so destructuring with val (url, bits) keeps working.
Nil comparisons from #expect(... == nil) map to kotlin.test.assertNull.
Twitch API model properties keep their Swift snake_case names (min_bits, static_) to match the ported model declarations.
makeCheermotes takes a Map<String, List<Int>>; linkedMapOf is used where a test builds more than one prefix so iteration order stays deterministic.
Assertion argument order follows kotlin.test.assertEquals(expected, actual), so the literal side of the Swift comparison is passed first.
String.Index cursor arithmetic is translated to Int UTF-16 offsets; identical for the ASCII format templates this file parses.

Foundation's Measurement unit types UnitSpeed, UnitTemperature and UnitLength do not exist on Android and are declared locally in this file with the same symbol strings, so symbol()/toSystem()/toString() behave exactly as on iOS.
@MainActor is dropped; TextFormatLoader is a plain class driven from the caller's scope.
String(localized:) is translated to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
Failable enum initializers (init?(_:)) become companion functions fromString(value).
CaseIterable is exposed as companion property allCases backed by the enum entries.
Swift regex literals are translated to Kotlin Regex objects and prefix-matched with find(input, 0) plus a range.first == 0 check.
The Swift custom toString() on the unit enums is translated as override fun toString(): String.
Parameterized `@Test(arguments:)` cases became `@Test fun` bodies that loop over `intArrayOf` rows, because JUnit 4 cannot parameterize individual methods with different data sets in one class.
`Issue.record(...)` followed by `return` is translated to kotlin.test `fail(...)`, which throws and therefore stops the test.

Assumed the failable Swift initializers `HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode(reader:)`, `HevcNalUnit(data:offset:)` and `AvcNalUnit(data:offset:)` were ported as throwing constructors, so `try #require(...)` becomes a direct constructor call; if the port returns nullables instead, an explicit null check must be added here.

Assumed sealed payload case names keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitPayload.prefixSeiNut`, `HevcNalUnitSeiPayload.timeCode`, `AvcNalUnitPayload.sei`, `AvcNalUnitSeiPayload.pictureTiming`) with an associated-value property of the same name, and that enum entries keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitType.prefixSeiNut`, `AvcNalUnitType.sei`).
Wire-format integer mapping applied: `hours`/`minutes`/`seconds` are `UByte` and `frame` is `UInt`, so assertions convert the `Int` loop values with `toUByte()`/`toUInt()`.

`clock(...)` takes and returns `java.time.Instant`; the hevc `calendar` global is not used because the test must build the clock in UTC, matching the production `makeClock()` value asserted with `epochSecond % 86400`.
`Data` comparisons use `assertContentEquals` since Kotlin `ByteArray` equality is identity based, and `assertNotEquals`/`assertTrue` were not needed.
Byte literals above 0x7F keep their exact values and are written with `.toByte()` where Kotlin requires it.
The Swift file-private enum `CatPrinterCommandId` is renamed to `CatPrinterCommandsCommandId` so its .class file cannot collide with the private enum of the same name in CatPrinterCommandsMxw01.kt.
`logger.info(...)` became `Log.i("CatPrinterCommand", ...)`; the tag is this file's command type name, as on iOS.

`init?(data:)` became `operator fun invoke(data:)` returning `CatPrinterCommand?`; the do/catch that returned nil is `runCatching { unpack(data) }.getOrNull()` and the thrown Swift strings are IllegalStateException.
Image rows are UByteArray (`[[UInt8]]` -> `List<UByteArray>`), matching catPrinterEncodeImageRow and catPrinterPackPrintImageCommandsMxw01.
Data literals became byteArrayOf with `.toByte()` on values >= 0x80 so the bytes stay identical.
`reader.readUInt8() == 0x51` uses `0x51.toUByte()` because ByteReader returns UByte and bare hex literals are Int.
The case values SetEnergy/FeedPaper keep UShort and SetQuality keeps UByte, written through ByteWriter.writeUInt16Le/writeUInt8.
DrawRow and Lattice are data classes holding arrays, so their generated equals/hashCode compare references; no code in this file compares two commands by value.
Swift Testing's @Test(arguments:) has no JUnit 4 equivalent here, so bool(), decodeIntNotRepresentable() and the other parameterised cases run as one @Test that loops over the argument list.
Swift's `func null()` and `func object()` are hard keywords in Kotlin and had to be declared with backticks so the method names stay identical.
A private top-level `bytes(vararg Int)` helper was added so every Data([...]) byte literal stays byte-identical while producing a ByteArray; Data comparisons use kotlin.test.assertContentEquals.
Assumes Amf0Type is a sealed class with PascalCase subclasses (Number, Bool, String, Object, TypedObject, Null, Undefined, EcmaArray, StrictArray, Date) and that each payload is exposed as `value`.
Assumes AsValue is a sealed class with String/Number/Bool/EcmaArray subclasses and that AsObject is a Map<String, AsValue> (dictionary literals become mapOf).
Assumes AmfError is a sealed Throwable hierarchy with NotNumber and TooDeep objects, so assertFailsWith<AmfError.NotNumber> / <AmfError.TooDeep> is used for #expect(throws:).
RtmpCommandName is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.message and used through RtmpCommandName.fromRawValue(...) / RtmpCommandName.Result per the enum mapping convention.
Swift Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 15) becomes Instant.ofEpochSecond(15); ecmaArray.get(key:) becomes get(...) and swiftArray decoding yields a List<AsValue>.
Added shoutoutCreates list, delegate override twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate and the shoutoutCreate test, matching the Swift diff.
The delegate implements the override for twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate like the other TwitchEventSubDelegate callbacks.
Expectations use assertEquals/assertNull with kotlin.test as in the rest of the file, JUnit 4 via RobolectricTestRunner.
Swift URL file paths become java.io.File; Date becomes java.time.Instant (Date(timeInterval:since:) -> plusSeconds).
Recording's failable init?(recording:) is translated as a companion factory `create(recording:)` returning Recording?, with a private constructor taking the mutable fields.
The candidate-filename loop mutates a temporary Recording, exactly mirroring how Swift's init assigns filename and resolves recordingPath inside url().
createAndGetDirectory and formatFilenameDateAndTime are called positionally to avoid depending on their Kotlin parameter names.
final class RecordingsStorage becomes a plain Kotlin class (final by default).
Security-scoped bookmark resolution (URL(resolvingBookmarkData:)) has no Android equivalent and is replaced with TODO in loadRecordingPath().

encode() re-implements Apple's JSONEncoder output (keys sorted alphabetically, `"key" : value` separators, two-space pretty printing, '/' escaped as '\/') on top of kotlinx.serialization, so every expectation literal from the Swift suite is kept byte-identical.
Swift `try`/`throws` disappear: encode() returns String and never throws; the generic reified signature also serves the two non-request encode calls.

kotlinx.serialization prints Double(1.0) as '1.0' where Apple prints '1', so every literal whose expected JSON shows an integer (10, 30, 90, 250, 4200, 22, 17, 3...) was kept as an Int argument; decimals stay Double.

Foundation Measurement / UnitTemperature / UnitSpeed are replaced by the port's Measurement, UnitTemperature and UnitSpeed types in com.moblin.android.various, with celsius and metersPerSecond kept so the wire shape (unit.converter.coefficient/constant + symbol) is unchanged.
WeatherKit WeatherCondition.clear has no Android counterpart and is passed as its raw value "clear" (the string the Swift encoder produced).

Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) -> Instant.ofEpochSecond(...) and .now -> Instant.now(); note the expectation `"date" : 745043166` is Apple's 2001 reference-date encoding, which the port's serializer must keep to stay wire compatible.

Names for the sealed request cases were inferred from the Swift enum (RemoteControlRequest.SetGimbalTracking/SetGimbalMovement/AnimateGimbal/SaveGimbalPreset/SendMessage, motion RemoteControlRequest.GimbalMotion.Kapow), as were RunningMetrics and the nullable gForce accessors.
Json is configured with encodeDefaults = true (all stored properties are always encoded) and explicitNulls = false (nil Optionals are omitted, matching Swift's encodeIfPresent).
httpGet is assumed to be a suspend function returning Pair<ByteArray, NetworkResponse> that throws on transport errors, mirroring the iOS (Data, HTTPURLResponse) tuple plus thrown errors.
Emote is constructed with a String url (URL is only stored), so makeUrl(emote:) validates the string with java.net.URI and returns the string.
Dictionary merging with `{ $1 }` becomes MutableMap.putAll, which also keeps the newer value on duplicate keys; on failure nothing is merged because the fetch completes before putAll runs.
Swift's `throw "Not successful"` (String error) becomes throw Exception(...) because Kotlin can only throw Throwable.
The channel URL interpolates platform.rawValue, since the ported EmotesPlatform keeps the Swift raw value used by the BTTV API path.
JSONDecoder's tolerance for unknown keys is kept with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }; optional CodingKeys map to nullable properties defaulting to null.
logger.info -> Log.i with the file-level tag "Bttv"; String(localized:) -> localized().
BttvEmote/BttvChannel remain private top-level @Serializable data classes and are decoded with explicit serializers.
Only SettingsRistServerStream.virtualDestinationPort default, its decode default and SettingsRistServer.makeUniqueVirtualDestinationPort changed as described by the diff.
Swift UInt16 virtualDestinationPort stays a Kotlin Int (ports are Int throughout this file), so the new Swift default 2 becomes Published(2) and 2u in the decode call.
makeUniqueVirtualDestinationPort now starts at 2 and steps by 2 in both Swift and Kotlin.
Every other line is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin translation.
@Published properties are translated to private MutableStateFlow fields exposed as read-only StateFlow; id stays a plain var because it is not @Published in Swift.

Codable's hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) become a KSerializer implemented by each class's companion object (referenced with @Serializable(with = <Class>.Companion::class)); the CodingKeys enum is replaced by a private @Serializable surrogate whose property names match the Swift coding keys one-to-one.
java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so ids are written to the wire as their canonical string form and parsed back with UUID.fromString.

The surrogate properties carry the same defaults as the Swift container.decode(_:_:_:) fallbacks, so missing keys decode to id = random UUID, name = "", enabled = false, printChat = false, faxMeowSound = true, printSnapshots = true.
Swift's empty init() {} maps to the implicit no-arg constructor, so both classes still have one.
SettingsCatPrinter.baseName lives in the companion object because Kotlin has no static stored properties.
Named conformance assumes Named in com.moblin.android.various.utils declares name as StateFlow<String>, matching the @Published mapping used for this port.
Both classes serialize through their companion KSerializer and therefore never use a compiler-generated serializer.
FfzImages/FfzEmote translated to private @Serializable data classes with @SerialName("1x"/"2x"/"4x") matching the Swift coding keys.
Assumed the glossary function httpGet(url) is a suspend function returning Pair<ByteArray, NetworkResponse>; if the real port signature differs, only fetchEmotes must be adjusted.
response.isNotFound / response.isSuccessful are kept as NetworkResponse members.
Swift's thrown String replaced with Exception(" Not successful") so the surrounding try/catch behaves the same.
URL(string:) validation replaced with java.net.URI parsing; makeUrl returns String? and the value is passed straight to Emote(url = ...).
String(localized:) -> localized(...); logger.info -> android.util.Log.i with tag "Ffz".
EmotesPlatform does not exist in the glossary list given but is stated to live in this same package, so no import is needed; interpolation $platform mirrors \(platform).
message stays a local var and the return is the Kotlin Pair emotes to message.
Swift enum cases map to a Kotlin enum class; entry names are kept lowercase and byte-identical so persisted raw values keep working.
Codable without explicit raw values is synthesized as the case name, so rawValue is the case name and no @Serializable annotation is required for kotlinx.serialization defaults.
CaseIterable maps to the Kotlin 2.x enum `entries` property, exposed for callers through the companion `allCases()`.
Codable decoding of an unknown case returns nil in Swift; `fromRawValue` returns a nullable Platform for the same behaviour.
String(localized: "...") becomes the shared top-level `localized` function imported from com.moblin.android.
imageName() returns the same asset identifiers; on Android these resolve against drawables of the same lowercase-ish name when consumed by the UI layer.
No state is stored, so the enum has no mutable members and is thread-safe.
None of the glossary types are referenced by this file, so no cross-package imports besides `localized` are needed.
Added the new SettingsDjiDeviceModel entry osmoPocket4Pro with raw value "osmoPocket4Pro" right after osmoPocket4.
Added osmoPocket4Pro branches to hasImageStabilization (false), hasNewProtocol (true) and hasVideoCodec (true).
Added the new hasFps() function after hasVideoCodec(); osmoPocket3/4/4Pro return true, every other model false.
hasVideoCodec already returned true for osmoPocket4 in the existing port, so only the osmoPocket4Pro branch was added there.
Enum raw values stay byte-identical for persisted JSON (osmoPocket4Pro).

httpGet is the shared helper from com.moblin.android.common.various; it is called positionally as httpGet(url) and assumed to return a destructurable (data: ByteArray, response) pair whose response exposes isSuccessful, isNotFound and statusCode.
Swift threw plain String errors; each is now an IllegalStateException carrying the identical message ("Not successful", "Emotes missing", "Emotes list empty").
Swift's Dictionary.merging(other) { $1 } maps to Map.plus (emotes + other), which is also right-hand-wins and returns a new immutable map.

The private Codable structs become private @Serializable data classes with @SerialName for static_name and emote_set; a shared Json instance sets ignoreUnknownKeys = true to match JSONDecoder's default.
Decoding uses the ByteArray's decodeToString() plus the reified kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString extension.
URL values are only stored/passed to the HTTP helper, so they are plain String per the port mapping (no java.net.URI parsing needed).
URL(string:) guards that can never fail on Android were dropped; makeEmote still returns null exactly when there is no .webp file.
logger.info becomes Log.i with the file-level TAG "Seventv"; the platform path segment uses EmotesPlatform.rawValue, matching the Swift enum interpolation.
@MainActor on the Swift class is represented by a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) owned by the class; the polling loop runs in that scope.
Swift `Task<Void, any Error>?` becomes a nullable kotlinx.coroutines.Job, and `Task.isCancelled` becomes the coroutine scope's `!isActive` check inside the launched loop.
httpGet from com.moblin.android.common.various is assumed to return an okhttp3.Response; the body bytes are read and decoded to a String before kotlinx.serialization parsing (URLSession -> OkHttp).
JSONDecoder().decode(_:from:) is replaced by kotlinx.serialization: the struct becomes an @Serializable data class with the same stored property name currentSumViewer.
PlatformStatus.unknown / .live(viewerCount:) from com.moblin.android.various.model are used as PlatformStatus.Unknown and PlatformStatus.Live(viewerCount = ...) (sealed-class style).
URL(string:) cannot fail for an interpolated Kotlin String, so the Swift `guard let url` early return is dropped; the URL stays a plain String.
sleep(seconds: delay) from com.moblin.android.common.various is called with the Int second count; the Swift `delay = 5` then `delay = 60` cadence is preserved.

The caught exception is intentionally broad (Exception), matching the Swift catch-all; a CancellationException raised by sleep will therefore set the status to unknown before the isActive check breaks the loop.
Added the new guard calling isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed() right after the existing filter checks in isTextToSpeechEnabledForMessage, matching the Swift insertion point.

Added Model.isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed() and Model.stopTextToSpeechIfOutputNotAllowed() between isTextToSpeechEnabledForMessage and the private isTextToSpeechEnabledForAnyAlertWidget, keeping Swift declaration order.
The Swift guard in stopTextToSpeechIfOutputNotAllowed is written as an early-return if with the negated condition (!textToSpeechEnabled || isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed()).
The new functions reference database.chat.textToSpeechBluetoothSpeakerOnly and isBluetoothAudioOutput, which are translated verbatim from the Swift source.
@Published is not mapped to MutableStateFlow here: the hand-written Codable and the Named(name: String) conformance require plain, directly serializable properties, so observation is left to callers.

SettingsGimbal keeps the identical flat wire format (shutter*/flip* keys) through the private SettingsGimbalData DTO and SettingsGimbalSerializer, because kotlinx.serialization cannot inline a nested object into its parent.
Missing keys fall back to the same defaults as the Swift decoder: zoomSpeedDefault, true, true, .record, .switchScene, .kapow, empty preset list and null ids.
UUID is persisted as its string form via the private UuidStringSerializer (kotlinx.serialization has no built-in java.util.UUID serializer); decoding uses UUID.fromString like Swift's decoder.
SettingsGimbalPreset.baseName uses localized("My preset") from package com.moblin.android.
Enum entries are referenced with the Swift case names (record, switchScene, kapow) as declared by SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion.
Identifiable is dropped; id stays a plain UUID property with a fresh UUID default.
SettingsGimbal is annotated @Serializable(with = SettingsGimbalSerializer::class); callers may also use SettingsGimbalSerializer directly.
ObservableObject/@Published is modelled as plain properties inside @Serializable classes (these types are Codable, so StateFlow backing would break kotlinx.serialization).
The hand-written Swift encoders/decoders become @Serializable classes; Swift's fallback decode values become Kotlin property default values, so absent keys fall back identically.
Swift UUID is mapped to java.util.UUID and serialized as a string.
Swift UInt32 bitrate is a config value, not wire bytes, so it is mapped to Int; goProDeviceBitrates is List<Int>.
Enum raw values are preserved byte-identically with @SerialName; CaseIterable becomes the Kotlin enum entries property.
SettingsGoProLens.toString() replaces the Swift display-name helper and overrides Any.toString().
state and autoRestartStreamTimer are not in the Swift CodingKeys, so they are marked @Transient.
Swift switch over rtmpUrlType is exhaustive (only server/custom), so the Kotlin when has no else branch.
MediaPlayer now takes a third constructor parameter colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange and stores it in a private property declared after filename.
Added open fun setPixelFormatType(colorRange) right after deactivate(), assigning this@MediaPlayer.colorRange on mediaPlayerQueue.
loadVideoTrackCompletion now uses colorRange.pixelFormatType() instead of the Moblin pixelFormatType global for kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey.
Imported com.moblin.android.various.settings.SettingsStreamColorRange.
The unused kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA import is kept byte-identical since the diff does not touch imports.
All other lines, including the AutoCloseable close() and lease handling, are unchanged.

ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to kotlin.time.TimeSource.Monotonic.ValueTimeMark: '.now' becomes TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow() and 'time.duration(to: .now) > .seconds(5)' becomes 'time.elapsedNow() > 5.seconds'.
CyclingSource keeps the Swift case names (watch, cyclingPower, cyclingSpeedCadence) and the raw values 0/1/2, and gains the usual companion fromRawValue(rawValue).

Swift's 'extension Model: WorkoutDeviceDelegate' cannot be expressed by Kotlin extension functions, so the delegate callbacks stay as top-level extension functions with identical names; Model must declare WorkoutDeviceDelegate and forward its overrides to these functions (or the delegate must be assigned through an adapter).

Assumed Model members used here: workoutDevices (MutableMap<UUID, WorkoutDevice>), currentWorkoutDeviceSettings, statusTopRight.workoutDeviceState, heartRates / runningMetrics keyed by lowercased device name, cyclingPower / cyclingCadence / cyclingSpeed, latestCyclingPower / latestCyclingCadence and addWorkoutHeartRate / addWorkoutCyclingPower / addWorkoutCyclingCadence.
The Swift 'guard let device = ...' shadowing of the parameter is renamed to deviceSettings because Kotlin forbids shadowing a parameter name.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch, with mainScope a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) declared in this file.
Iterating workoutDevices.values is copied with toList() before calling stop() so that mutating the map inside the loop matches Swift's value-semantics iteration.
WorkoutDeviceState entries are referenced by their Swift names (.disconnected, .connected) and the unused first parameter of the two cycling delegate callbacks is kept as a named 'device' parameter.
`@MainActor` on the Swift class has no Kotlin equivalent; access must be confined to the main dispatcher by callers.
`@Published currentSwitcherId` is exposed as a `StateFlow`; the backing `MutableStateFlow` is `internal` so the `Model` extension functions in this file can write to it.
`ContinuousClock.Instant` is mapped to `java.time.Instant`; `switchTime`, `now` parameters and `.now` all use it.
`IndexSet` is mapped to `Set<Int>`; offsets are removed in descending order so earlier removals do not shift later indices.
`popLast()` maps to `removeLastOrNull()`, `removeAll()` maps to `clear()`, and `[UUID]` becomes `MutableList<UUID>`.
`logger.info(...)` becomes `Log.i("Model", ...)`; the tag is the enclosing type name.
`autoSceneSwitcher.currentSwitcherId` is a StateFlow, so reads from the extensions go through the internal backing flow's `.value`.
The remote control state call uses the app's `RemoteControlState`/`RemoteControlAutoSceneSwitcher` types, imported from this same package.
ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to monotonic nanoseconds from System.nanoTime() and ContinuousClock.Duration to Long nanoseconds (1_000_000_000L per second).
Deque<SrtDataPacket> becomes kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque and OrderedSet<UInt32> becomes LinkedHashSet<UInt> (insertion order, first()/remove() emulate removeFirst()).

Data/UnsafeRawBufferPointer buffers become ByteArray; the in-place writes done through withUnsafeMutableBytes are performed by the private ByteArray.writeUInt32(value, offset) extension declared in this file.
ByteReader/ByteWriter are assumed to expose readUInt16(): UShort, readUInt32(): UInt, readBytes(count): ByteArray, writeUInt16(UShort), writeUInt32(UInt), writeBytes(ByteArray) and data: ByteArray.
Atomic<SrtPerformanceData> is assumed to provide value and mutate { }, and SrtPerformanceData is created with its no-argument constructor in place of Swift's .zero.
delegate lost its weak semantics: SrtSenderDelegate is held as a plain nullable reference and must be cleared by the owner.
srtlaClientQueue.async { } became srtlaClientQueue.launch { }, so srtlaClientQueue must be a CoroutineScope; SimpleTimer.startSingleShot is called with the timeout in seconds as Double.
Swift's thrown String errors are translated as a private SrtSenderException type, and logger.info maps to Log.i with tag "SrtSender".
Added the import for spokenEmoteNames from com.moblin.android, keeping the import list alphabetical.
Added the spokenEmoteNames expectation to emoteInTheMiddle and consecutiveEmotes, translated as assertEquals(expected, actual) with kotlin.test.
ContinuousClock.Instant and ContinuousClock.Duration are mapped to Long nanoseconds obtained from System.nanoTime(); `.advanced(by:)` becomes plain addition.

The UInt32 bitrate surface (init targetBitrate, setTargetBitrate, getCurrentBitrate, delegate callback) is mapped to Int following the project convention, while the internal 64-bit bitrate stays Long.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i using the class name as the log tag.
logAdaptiveAcion is inherited from AdaptiveBitrate (same package) and is called with the named argument actionTaken.

AdaptiveBitrateSettings field types are assumed to be Int for counts (packetsInFlight, rttDiffHighAllowedSpike) and Long for bitrate-shaped values; minimumBitrate is Long because the Swift code compares it to an Int64.
Swift multiline strings with backslash continuations are collapsed into single-line interpolated strings.
defaultSrtLatency is wrapped with toDouble() so the elvis result matches the Double type of StreamStats.latency.
stats.mbpsSendRate is force-unwrapped with !!, stats.latency and stats.relaxed keep the Swift optional fallbacks via ?:.
Swift Testing async throws tests become @Test fun ...() = runTest { } so the suspend AdaptiveBitrate calls run inside a coroutine.
Deque<UInt32> from swift-collections maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<Int> with addLast/last/isEmpty.
Bitrate values (targetBitrate, transport bitrate, delegate callback) are translated as Int rather than UInt, since they are encoder bitrates, not wire-format data.
Int64 transport bitrate and the makeStats parameter become Long; the Swift Int literals 5_000_000 / 1_000_000 are typed as Long where required.
The Handler class and its AdaptiveBitrateDelegate conformance (a Swift extension in the same file) are merged into one Kotlin class with override.
makeStats and update stay file-private top-level functions, matching the Swift private helpers, and update is a suspend function because it calls sleep.
Named arguments are kept (targetBitrate, delegate, settings, stats, bitrate, milliSeconds) so the call sites read identically to the Swift source.
Test types live in the same Kotlin package, so no imports are needed for AdaptiveBitrateSrtBelabox, StreamStats, AdaptiveBitrateDelegate or adaptiveBitrateBelaboxSettings.

The @Test(arguments:) suite became a JUnit 4 Parameterized class: the timestamp argument is a constructor property named `value`, and JUnit runs the other two tests once per argument set (Swift Testing ran them once).
ntpUnixEpochSeconds stays a top-level private value of type ULong so the 64-bit NTP shifts and mask literals (0xFFFF_FFFF, 0x8000_0000) remain byte-identical.
decodeNtpTimestamp is assumed to take the wire-format ULong (parameter label `v`) and to return Double? seconds; assertNotNull is used in place of try #require to unwrap it.
#expect(decodeNtpTimestamp(v: value) == nil) became assertNull; #expect(timestamp == 0) became assertEquals(0.0, timestamp) because timestamp is a Double.

isEqual is imported from com.moblin.android and called positionally for the first two arguments with the Swift label `epsilon` kept as a named argument; adjust the call if the ported signature differs.
The Swift `throws` on decodeNtpTimestampAtUnixEpoch was dropped: Kotlin assertions do not need a throws clause.
WebrtcIngestClient, VideoCodec, TrackTimestamper and WebrtcIngestClientDelegate are not referenced by this suite, so no imports for them were added.
CMSampleBuffer is replaced by MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media; presentation times are converted from seconds to microseconds.
Swift `===` identity checks map to kotlin.test.assertSame because BufferedAudio hands back the same MediaSample instances that were appended.
expectSequence takes the timestamp as a parameter and returns the advanced value, because Kotlin has no Swift-style `inout` parameter.

createSampleBuffer builds a silent MediaSample directly, since CMSampleBuffer.createSilent has no Android counterpart; the format comes from MediaFormat.createAudioFormat(MIMETYPE_AUDIO_RAW, 48000, 1) and 1024 frames of 16-bit mono are represented by a zero-filled ByteArray.
DriftTracker.setDrift(drift:) keeps the Swift argument label as the Kotlin parameter name; adjust it if the ported signature uses a different name.
cameraId uses UUID.randomUUID() for the Swift `.init()` default UUID.
JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; the suite has no init block, so no @Before setUp method is generated.
Suite becomes a plain JUnit 4 class (class GoProBleProtocolSuite) with @Test methods in the same order; assertions use kotlin.test.
ByteArray has no value equality, so list/byte comparisons use assertContentEquals instead of assertEquals.
Byte literals >= 0x80 must be written with .toByte() in Kotlin (0xBC, 0x85, 0x80); the byte values themselves are unchanged.
Swift Data.prefix(2) becomes ByteArray.copyOfRange(0, 2) and Data((0..<64).map(UInt8.init)) becomes ByteArray(64) { it.toByte() }.
ByteArray.hexString() is assumed to be the ported Moblin extension that exists elsewhere in the project; it is not declared in this file.
The Swift throws/#require in packetizesAndAccumulatesLongMessage is unnecessary in Kotlin, so the last packet is taken directly with packets.last().

response.result == .resultSuccess is translated against the ported constant goProResponseSuccessStatus, and the protobuf serializedBytes initializer becomes OpenGopro_ResponseGetApEntries.parseFrom(...).

The Swift diff is empty, so the Kotlin file is returned unchanged.

makeChatPostTextSegments is called with the named argument text, matching the Swift helper's parameter label.

ModelMock folds the Swift extension into its class declaration by implementing SrtSenderDelegate directly.
MessageQueue<Void> becomes MessageQueue<Unit>; put is called synchronously from the delegate callbacks while get stays suspend, matching the sync SrtSenderDelegate surface.
The Swift Testing suite becomes a JUnit 4 class; connectDisconnect is a @Test method whose body runs in runBlocking because the model waits are suspend.

Everything else in the file, including the Android-only runMainTest and MainLooperDrainRule hooks, is left byte-identical.
Applied the Swift diff: added colorRange = SettingsStreamColorRange.full to the MpegTsReader constructor call, at the same position as in Swift.
Added the import for SettingsStreamColorRange from com.moblin.android.settings, the package holding Moblin's settings types (Moblin/Various/Settings/**).
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin translation.
Model is declared in the same package (com.moblin.android.various.model), so this Swift extension becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model with no extra import for Model itself.
Only SoopChat and SoopPlatformStatus are imported, from com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.soop.

resetChat(), setTextToSpeechStreamerMentions(), isRemoteControlChatAndEvents(platform:) and updateChatMoreThanOneChatConfigured() are member functions of Model declared in other files and are called unchanged.
Function order matches the Swift source so both files can be read side by side.
@MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent: the class owns a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob()) and all state changes stay on the main dispatcher.
Task<Void, any Error>? becomes Job?; stop() cancels the Job exactly like task?.cancel().
Task.isCancelled becomes the kotlinx.coroutines CoroutineScope.isActive check inside the launched coroutine.
sleep(seconds:) from com.moblin.android.common.various is assumed to be a suspend function taking Double, so the local delay is kept as Double (1.0 then 30.0).

PlatformStatus is assumed to be a sealed class in com.moblin.android.various.model with Unknown, Offline and Live(viewerCount: Int) variants matching the Swift cases .unknown, .offline and .live(viewerCount:).
The thrown error from getKickChannelInfo is caught as Exception, matching Swift's untyped catch which sets .unknown.
The C-style while true loop and the delay escalation from 1 to 30 seconds are preserved unchanged.
The type returned by getKickChannelInfo is used only through inference, so no import for it is required.
Swift's `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on `Model` in this same package, keeping names and order identical.

`ContinuousClock.Instant` is mapped to `kotlin.time.TimeSource.Monotonic.ValueTimeMark` and `ContinuousClock.now` to `TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow()`; the type must match `Variables.timestamp` in com.moblin.android.various.
`Date` becomes `java.time.Instant` (`Date.now` -> `Instant.now()`).
`"\(Int(slopePercent))%"` becomes `"${slopePercent.toInt()}%"`; Kotlin `toInt()` truncates toward zero exactly like Swift's `Int(_:)` for Double.
`Variables(...)` is built with named arguments, so the Kotlin data class parameter names must match the Swift memberwise initializer labels.
`systemMonitor.format()` is imported as an extension function from com.moblin.android.common.various.
`getSystemMonitor()` and `getBrowserTitle()` remain file-private extension functions, matching Swift's private extension members.
`loadTextFormat(...)` is invoked positionally to avoid depending on an unverified parameter name.
Swift Testing struct TextEffectSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions, run under Robolectric so the app context, resources and locale are available.

The two `.enabled(if: Locale.current.identifier == "en_SE")` guards are replaced by @Config(qualifiers = "en-rSE") plus TimeZone/Locale defaults set in @Before (Europe/Stockholm, en-SE), so the time and date tests run unconditionally with the same values as on iOS.
The suite is @MainActor in Swift, but the formatter under test is pure string/number formatting, so tests stay plain @Test; only the locale and time zone need to be pinned.
WeatherCondition is not part of the port (Variables.condition is a String?), so `.clear` / `.rain` are passed as the lowercase condition strings "clear" / "rain".
TextFormatLoader().load(format:) is called through the kept top-level function loadTextFormat(format = ...), which is what the port declares for the same loader logic.

createVariables mirrors the Swift helper parameter order and fills every Variables field with the same value, with timestamp = ContinuousClock.now.nanoseconds and date = Instant.ofEpochSecond(1_723_350_366).
Added the new spokenEmoteNames import from com.moblin.android and the three new assertions plus the emoteNameMayContainColons test from the Swift diff.

Only the changed tests and the new test were touched; all other lines stay byte-identical.

The suite's production API changed: interpolate3d now takes a (Int, Int, Int) -> SIMD3 sampler instead of a List<SIMD3>, makeLutCube(dimension, sampler) is new, and lutEffectConvertCube returns a (dimension, cubeData) pair. Signatures were inferred from the Swift call sites because the dependency listing still shows the previous list-based overloads.

sampler(lut, dimension) returns a Kotlin function value (Int, Int, Int) -> SIMD3 indexing lut[(blue * dimension + green) * dimension + red].

LutEffectSuite.lutEffectConvertCube is assumed to return Pair<Float, ByteArray> (Swift's Int(dimension) proves the dimension is not Int) and makeLutCube is assumed to return Pair<Int, ByteArray>; adjust if the production declarations differ.

renderBigPngLutWithMetalPetal is left out as instructed; the newly added renderCubeLutWithMetalPetal is left out as well because it also renders with MetalPetal/GL and cannot run under Robolectric, so both live in the hand-written instrumented LutEffectRenderSuite.
Byte comparisons of cube data keep the existing wrapper of ByteBuffer.wrap(data).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer().
The Swift diff only adds #expect(spokenEmoteNames(...)) assertions, so the Kotlin file adds the matching assertEquals calls plus the spokenEmoteNames import.
Import com.moblin.android.spokenEmoteNames was inserted in alphabetical order between makeEmotes and texts.
Every other line, including the Robolectric runner, helpers and existing assertions, is unchanged byte for byte.
WeatherKit has no Android counterpart, so Variables.condition is treated as a String and conditionToEmoji matches the Swift WeatherCondition case names.
Foundation MeasurementFormatter is replaced by android.icu NumberFormatter + MeasureUnit + Precision; the "system" unit choice uses the locale country (US/LR/MM = imperial).
DateFormatter and Date.FormatStyle are replaced by java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter bound to ZoneId.systemDefault().
ContinuousClock.Instant is modelled as Long nanoseconds: a duration between instants is (end - now) / 1_000_000_000.0.
Variables.temperature and Variables.feelsLikeTemperature are assumed to be Double degrees Celsius because Measurement<UnitTemperature> has nothing equivalent on Android.
Icon names (checkmark.square, mic.slash) and emoji plain-text values are kept byte-identical so rendering stays the same.

Moblin.format / Moblin.formatPace map to the top-level format() / formatPace() of com.moblin.android.common.various; Duration.formatWithSeconds() and TextFormatSpeedUnit.toSystem() are assumed to live in the packages shown by the glossary.
Emitted lines keep a reference to the mutable parts list, so parts is always replaced by a fresh list right after a line is appended (same value semantics as the Swift array).
WiFiAware is Apple-only in Swift; here it is replaced by the port's counterpart types in com.moblin.android.media.wifiaware (Sender, Receiver, WiFiAwareSender, WiFiAwareReceiver).

logger.info(...) maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name "Model" as tag.
#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) and @available(iOS 26, *) are compile-time/availability guards with no Android equivalent and are dropped.
The Swift private extension methods stay as private top-level extension functions on Model, in the same order as the Swift file.
The tested helper was renamed from metalPetalLayerPosition to layoutCenter, matching the current EffectUtils.kt declaration.
Test methods renamed to layoutCenterCorners, layoutCenterCenters and layoutCenterMatchesCoreImage.
SettingsWidgetLayout is a data class with val fields in this port, so the Swift `layout.size = 50` writes became `layout = layout.copy(size = 50.0)`.

The five new tests (layoutScaleFitsInsideLayoutSize, widgetShapePlacement, widgetShapePlacementNoResize, widgetShapePlacementRotatedWithBorder, widgetShapeApplySettings) were added at the end of the class in Swift order.

WidgetShape and ShapeEffectSettings are called with positional or named arguments exactly as the Kotlin signatures expose them; WidgetShape, ShapeEffectSettings, layoutScale and layoutCenter all live in com.moblin.android.videoeffects, so no new imports were needed.
The hand-written assertPosition(expected, actual) helper is reused for every CGPoint equality check, including the new placement.center assertions.
ShapeEffectSettings.cornerRadius is a Float, so the Swift 0.5 literal is written 0.5f.
The new tests mutate WidgetShape in place (borderWidth, apply), matching the data class with var fields used by the port's shape types.

Network.framework (NWListener/NWConnection/NWProtocolWebSocket) has no Android counterpart, so the transport is implemented with java.net.ServerSocket/java.net.Socket plus a hand-written WebSocket upgrade handshake and RFC 6455 text/close framing (client frames are unmasked, server frames are written unmasked).

MessageQueue<T> from com.moblin.android is used with the assumed suspend API put(value) / get(): T; if the real class exposes a non-suspending put, the enclosing functions can stay suspend without change.
Swift `throw "some string"` becomes a private ObsMockException(message) since Kotlin can only throw Throwable.
The mock's url() returns a String ("ws://127.0.0.1:port") rather than a URL/URI, since the value is only built and handed to a client.
deinit { listener.cancel() } is dropped; Kotlin has no destructors, so the ServerSocket/coroutine scope is only released when the mock is garbage collected or the socket is closed via disconnect().
@MainActor / MainActor.assumeIsolated / Sendable conformances are dropped; the class runs on ordinary coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.
logger.info(...) is mapped to android.util.Log.i with tag "ObsWebSocketServerMock"; unit tests on the JVM need unitTests.returnDefaultValues or Robolectric for Log not to throw.
jsonString uses kotlinx.serialization and recursively sorts object keys to match Swift's .sortedKeys option.

AVAudioConverter has no Android counterpart; the conversion engine is android.media.MediaCodec and the pull based convert(to:error:withInputFrom:) becomes dequeueInputBuffer/queueInputBuffer plus dequeueOutputBuffer.
AudioStreamBasicDescription and AVAudioFormat are both represented by android.media.MediaFormat (KEY_SAMPLE_RATE, KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT, KEY_CHANNEL_MASK), which is what MediaCodec uses natively.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer maps to MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media; the CMSampleBuffer.withAudioBufferList wrapper is replaced by reading MediaSample.data.
The DispatchQueue lockQueue is a CoroutineDispatcher, and every lockQueue.async block becomes a launch on a CoroutineScope bound to that dispatcher.
The port's Atomic is assumed to expose a settable value, so bitrate.mutate { $0 = x } is written as bitrate.value = x.

setBitrate stays an extension function on the converter but only clamps and tracks the value, because Android audio encoders cannot change their bitrate after configure; the value takes effect on the next converter creation.

makeChannelLayout has no channel layout object on Android, so the discrete in order layout tag becomes a MediaFormat channel mask with the low channel bits set; both statics are consolidated into one companion object placed where makeAudioFormat appears in the Swift file.
As in the Swift source, setInputSourceFormat never assigns inSourceFormat, so that field is only cleared by stopRunningInternal; this behaviour is kept identical.
URL properties become String paths; mediaStorage.makePath returns java.io.File, so .path is taken and checkResourceIsReachable becomes File.exists().
Deque -> kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque; getPlayer passes a copy so the player keeps Swift's value semantics when AlertsEffectGifImages consumes frames.
DispatchQueue.global().async -> a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); DispatchQueue.main.async -> a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) -> Bundle.url; Data(contentsOf:) -> File(url).readBytes(); FileManager.createFile -> File.writeBytes.
Int16(bitPattern: reader.readUInt16Le()) -> sample.toShort(), and the throwing read is wrapped in runCatching.
path.appendingPathExtension("wav") -> "$path.wav", since the stored value is already a plain path string.
AlertsEffectMedia is a non-final Swift class, so it becomes open class with open getPlayer/update and private helpers.
SettingsWidgetAlertsAlertMediaType is assumed to have the entries gifAndSound and video.
Added the torch entry to ChatBotMainArgument right after music, as in the Swift diff.
Declared ChatBotTorchArgument between ChatBotTeslaMediaArgument and ChatBotMessage, matching the Swift declaration order.
Everything else, including the hand-written FuzzyMatchingSwift port and the private constructor/invoke factory, is unchanged.
formatLog takes List<LogEntry> instead of Swift's Deque<LogEntry>: kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque would not accept the MutableList held by Model.log.
formatLog returns the written file's absolute path as String (URL -> String) and writes to context.cacheDir instead of FileManager temporaryDirectory, so Model must expose a context.
The temporary file name uses epoch millis ("Moblin-log-<millis>.txt") because Swift's Date() description contains characters that are awkward in Android file paths.

The extension functions assume Model exposes mutable collections/properties named log, fileLog, logId, logsStorage, logger, database, remoteControlLog and context; Kotlin extension functions cannot reach private members, so these must be internal or public in Model.kt.
logger.handler is assigned a lambda `{ message -> debugLog(message) }` because a bound callable reference to a private file-level extension function is not expressible as a plain (String) -> Unit.
DispatchQueue.main.async is dispatched on a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).
formatDate(.now) became formatDate(Instant.now()) following the Date -> java.time.Instant mapping.
log.map { $0.message }.joined(separator: "\n") became joinToString(separator = "\n") { it.message }.
JUnit 4 with kotlin.test assertions replaces Swift Testing; the suite class name and all test method names are kept identical, and there is no suite init so no @Before is emitted.
makeRtmpUri(url:) and makeRtmpStreamKey(url:) are top-level functions from com.moblin.android.common.various and are called positionally.
RtmpConnection(name:queue:) loses the DispatchQueue argument; the Kotlin port creates the connection with the name only (queue becomes a dispatcher inside the class).
callCompletions is treated as a MutableMap<Int, (List<AsValue>) -> Unit>; the captured local var arguments is reassigned inside the lambda, which Kotlin allows.
Data slicing uses ByteArray.copyOfRange(from, to); the expected buffer equality is checked with contentEquals because ByteArray has no structural equals in Kotlin.
commandType is passed as RtmpChunkType.amf0Command - the Swift RtmpMessageType enum is represented by RtmpChunkType in this port, confirm the entry name.
The AMF result payload is built with AsObject(mutableMapOf("code" to AsValue.String(...))); confirm the AsObject/AsValue constructors in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.amf.
makeConnectResultChunkData stays a private helper in the same file and returns a ByteArray produced by RtmpChunk.encode().
CGFloat is mapped to Double (HSV and chroma math), Float stays Float as in Swift's MTIColor/SIMD2 APIs.
DispatchQueue.main.async -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch, and asyncAfter(0.25) -> launch + delay(250), because no mainScope global is declared for this package.
DispatchQueue.global().async -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch.

processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope, so its .async blocks become .launch; the nonisolated(unsafe) let and the shadowing local val of the same name are kept as a plain local val with this@RemoveBackgroundEffect at the assignment.
CIColorCubeWithColorSpace.cubeData is a ByteArray, so the Swift [Float] cube is packed with ByteBuffer in native (little-endian) order, count * 4 bytes, as Data(bytes:count:) did.
Swift's switch-expression returning a tuple (red, green, blue) becomes a `when` returning Triple, with `default:` as `else` (Int(sector) -> sector.toInt(), same truncation).
filterMetalPetal.inputBackgroundImage = .transparent -> MTIImage.transparent; both `?? image` fallbacks kept.
The three private file-level structs become private data classes with their Swift names and member order.

RecorderTester's deinit that removed the temp file has no Kotlin equivalent; the tester registers its path in the file-private recorderSuiteTempFiles list and RecorderSuite.@After deletes every registered file.
DispatchSemaphore(value: 0) is java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch(1); wait(timeout: .now() + 10) is await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS).
CMTime is Long microseconds: videoFrameDuration is 1_000_000L / 30, CMTime(seconds:) becomes the file-private helper cmTime(seconds) and .seconds becomes / 1_000_000.0.

URL paths are plain String paths backed by java.io.File; FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent is File(System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir"), name) and attributesOfItem/.size is File.length() after File.exists().
Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval:) stays Thread.sleep(ms) so record() remains blocking exactly like the Swift helper.
The AVAssetReaderTrackOutput settings use the shim keys AVLinearPCM*, kAudioFormatLinearPCM and MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_AAC for Int(kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC).
sampleBuffer.withAudioBufferList + mData assumingMemoryBound(to: Int16.self) is ByteBuffer.wrap(sampleBuffer.data).order(LITTLE_ENDIAN).asShortBuffer() with samples.put/get.
The async tests run through runMainTest { } and loadTrackDuration/loadToneTime/loadVideoFullRange are suspend functions.

XMLCoder does not exist on Android: decoding uses javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory plus small org.w3c.dom helpers, encoding uses a hand-built string with an XmlNode.toXml(root) serializer (kept so Open and Auth keep their DynamicNodeEncoding attribute/element split).

URLSessionWebSocketTask is replaced by an OkHttp WebSocket; the callback-based listener pushes incoming text into a kotlinx Channel of unlimited capacity that receiveMessages() suspends on, and channel closure makes the receive throw so the reconnect loop still runs.
The @MainActor class keeps a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus a Job; Task.isCancelled becomes coroutineContext.isActive, and sleep(seconds: 5) becomes delay(5000).
The hard-coded ws://192.168.50.72:5443/ws socket created in the Swift init is dropped, because the OkHttp socket is only created in setupConnection() from the real url property.
The Swift inout Int parameter of makeChatPostTextSegments is assumed to be intArrayOf(0) (a one-element IntArray) in the Kotlin port; adjust if that helper used a different convention.
model.appendChatMessage is called with named arguments matching the Swift labels, and the chat platform case is assumed to be ChatPlatform.openStreamingPlatform from com.moblin.android.various.model.
private top-level Swift structs become file-private (private) top-level Kotlin declarations in the same file, preserving declaration order.
The XML message is wrapped in <container> before parsing because XMLCoder matches the outer root's child element, exactly as in the Swift original.
The Swift tuple (displayName, segments, isAction) inside Delegate is replaced by a private DelegateMessage data class so messages is a MutableList<DelegateMessage>.
@MainActor is dropped; TwitchChat delegate callbacks are assumed to be invoked synchronously inside webSocketClientReceiveMessage, so the test can assert right after the call.
Swift multi-line string literals with trailing-backslash line continuations are rewritten as Kotlin string concatenation so the IRC wire text stays byte-identical.
try? X becomes runCatching { X }.getOrNull(); try #require(x) becomes a direct x.first() access with kotlin.test assertions.
#expect(a == nil) uses assertNull, #expect(!x) uses assertFalse, #expect(a == b) uses assertEquals(expected = b, actual = a).
URL.absoluteString comparisons become plain String comparisons: ChatMessageEmote.url and ChatPostUrl.still are treated as String URLs in the Android port.
twitchEmoteIds builds the path with java.net.URI and splits/filters empty components to match Swift String.split(omittingEmptySubsequences: true) semantics.
TwitchChatCommand cases are assumed to be PascalCase (PrivateMessage, UserNotice, ClearMsg, ClearChat, Ping) and userBadges/sourceChannelIcon are assumed String-based.

This is SwiftProtobuf generated code: the message model is translated to plain Kotlin classes, and the runtime encode/decode plumbing (SwiftProtobuf.Decoder / SwiftProtobuf.Visitor) has no counterpart in this port's stack, so those two methods keep their names but take Any parameters and are TODO().
UnknownStorage is represented as ByteArray, and equality uses contentEquals/contentHashCode.
Protobuf field presence is preserved exactly: nullable private backing field, computed property falling back to the proto default, a hasX property and a clearX() function.
The Swift enum init() (which selects .resultUnknown) cannot be an enum constructor in Kotlin, so it becomes the companion function defaultValue().
The bytecode-encoded _protobuf_nameMap is translated into an explicit Map of enum/proto name to field number, keeping the same property name.
static func == is expressed as equals()/hashCode() overrides since Kotlin has no static operator.
Sendable conformance has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
SwiftProtobuf.ProtobufAPIVersionCheck is kept as private marker interfaces plus a private object, since Kotlin has no nested typealias.
The emote regex now captures the emote name: Regex("""\\[emote:(\\d+):([^\\]]+)\\]""").

The chat segment for an emote now carries the name from the second capture group, so ChatPostUrl was replaced by ChatPostEmote(moving, still, name); the ChatPostUrl import was swapped for the ChatPostEmote import at the same position.
Only the regex group, the emote segment construction and the Pusher app key changed; every other line is byte-identical.
The Pusher websocket app key is now 34bf7a0ff419a2a775b9.
Swift's inout Int counter stays AtomicInteger in Kotlin.
DispatchQueue is replaced by a CoroutineDispatcher constructor parameter plus an internal CoroutineScope; queue.async -> scope.launch and queue.asyncAfter -> scope.launch { delay(...) }.

AVFoundation types are mapped as follows: AVAudioFormat and CMFormatDescription -> android.media.MediaFormat, AVAudioCompressedBuffer -> ByteArray, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample, so presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0.
MediaSample has no decode timestamp, so calcVideoCompositionTime returns 0 and the video sample path uses presentationTimeUs where the Swift code preferred decodeTimeStamp when it was valid.

Because AVAudioCompressedBuffer carries no AudioStreamBasicDescription, the audio codec is remembered in the new audioMime field set by audioEncoderOutputFormatInternal and checked with the literal "audio/opus".

The delegate overrides assume the port's AudioEncoderDelegate/VideoEncoderDelegate take (MediaFormat), (ByteArray, Long) and (VideoEncoder, MediaFormat)/(VideoEncoder, MediaSample, Long); adjust if the codec files chose other Android types.
RtmpConnection, RtmpChunk, RtmpChunkType, RtmpStreamInfo and RtmpStreamStats live in this same package, so they are used without imports; processorPipelineQueue is treated as a CoroutineScope.
SimpleTimer is built from the coroutine dispatcher and startSingleShot is called with a Double timeout in seconds (20.0), matching the Swift API.
info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(bytesTransferred = length) } is kept as-is, assuming RtmpStreamStats exposes the same mutate helper as the Swift version.

The Swift diff switches the channel-info request from URLSession.shared to the shared httpUrlSession(); the Android file previously held its own OkHttpClient for this, so that client field is dropped and getChannelInfo now calls httpUrlSession().
Removed the now-unused okhttp3.OkHttpClient import and added the import for com.moblin.android.various.network.httpUrlSession.
The OkHttp-based WebSocket, message channel, coroutine loop and everything else are unchanged, since the diff only touches the HTTP request line.

Every Codable class becomes an @Serializable kotlinx.serialization class; Swift optional properties get a Kotlin default of null so they are omitted from JSON exactly like the synthesized encodeIfPresent, while non-optional properties stay constructor parameters without defaults and are always encoded (and required when decoding).

The Swift encoder used .sortedKeys plus .withoutEscapingSlashes; toString() re-sorts every JsonObject key alphabetically (kotlinx.serialization has no sortedKeys option) and kotlinx does not escape '/' by default, so the output matches.
Swift throws String values as errors; in Kotlin those become Exception(message) with the identical message text, since String can no longer implement Throwable.
UInt32 bitrate and UInt16 port are wire-format values and map to UInt/UShort as required by the unsigned-type rule.
MoblinSettingsRemoteControlServerRelay conformed to ObservableObject but declares no @Published property here, so it translates to a plain serializable class without StateFlow.

MoblinSettingsRemoteControl keeps the Swift declaration order (assistant, streamer, password), which means the non-default 'password' parameter follows defaulted ones; callers must use named arguments.
fromString decodes with ignoreUnknownKeys = true because Swift's JSONDecoder silently skips keys that are not part of the model, while kotlinx.serialization throws by default.
fromString/toString both throw SerializationException on malformed JSON, replacing Swift's EncodingError/DecodingError.
libdatachannel's C API has no Android/JNI binding, so RtcTrack and PeerConnection keep their exact signatures but every native call site is TODO().
whipQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher; whipQueue.async maps to whipScope.launch and whipQueue.sync maps to runBlocking(whipQueue).
WhipStreamDelegate.whipStreamPerform now takes an OkHttp Request/Response with a (ByteArray?, Response?, Throwable?) completion instead of URLRequest/URLResponse/Error.
The encoder-delegate overrides were written against ByteArray, MediaFormat and MediaSample with Long microsecond timestamps; align them with the audio/video codec packages.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer is reduced to a ByteArray and its packet descriptions are dropped, matching Android's one-access-unit-per-buffer codec output.
DataChannelConnectionState and DataChannelGatheringState only exist in the Swift DataChannel module, so they are declared here with a fromValue(rawInt) companion.
Enum entries for SettingsStreamCodec (H264AVC/H265HEVC), SettingsStreamAudioCodec (OPUS/AAC) and the MpegTsVideoConfigAvc/Hevc create(format) factory are inferred.
logger.info/debug are replaced with Log.i/Log.d using the tag WhipStream.
Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on Model in the same package, keeping the original member names and order.

Kotlin has no retroactive protocol conformance: Model must declare `: BlackSharkCoolerDeviceDelegate` so that `delegate = this` compiles, and forward its two interface callbacks to these extension functions.
BlackSharkLib.CoolingState has no counterpart in the Android port, so blackSharkCoolerDeviceStatus receives phoneTemperature and heatsinkTemperature (Double) directly instead of the status object.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch using a file-private `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)`.
`device.bluetoothPeripheralId!` is translated to an early return on the nullable id (`?: return`) so it can be reused for the map key and the start call.
disableBlackSharkCoolerDevice keys the map by `device.id` exactly like the Swift source, not by bluetoothPeripheralId.
blackSharkCoolerDevices is expected to be a MutableMap<String, BlackSharkCoolerDevice> on Model, matching the Swift dictionary usage.

DockKit is Apple-only: every DockAccessory/DockAccessoryManager interaction (state observation, system tracking, orientation, animation, angular velocity, accessory events) is replaced by TODO("no Android counterpart for DockKit").
The Swift #if canImport(DockKit) / #else variants collapse into one Kotlin class whose public signatures match the stub branch; isConnected() still mirrors 'accessory != null'.
Spatial.Vector3D has no Android type, so a local data class Vector3D(x, y, z) is declared in this file; it is used only in gimbal signatures.
DockAccessory is kept untyped as Any? because its members do not exist in Kotlin; the private observer methods take Any for the same reason.
Fire-and-forget Task { } bodies become gimbalScope.launch { }, a private file-level CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) standing in for @MainActor + Task.
