setOrientation/getCurrentOrientation are suspend functions; their '!tracking' guards and the nil result while tracking is enabled are preserved.

handleAccessoryEventCameraShutter/Flip/Zoom are fully translated against Model.database.gimbal, Model.handleControllerFunction and Model.setZoomX (Float conversions added because the Kotlin settings types are unknown).
Those camera event handlers stay unreachable until an Android gimbal backend feeds handleAccessoryEvent, which is itself a TODO.
apple_only: DockKit (DockAccessoryManager, DockAccessory, DockAccessory.StateChange, DockAccessory.AccessoryEvent, DockAccessory.Animation): no Android counterpart, replaced with TODO

notes: Emoji now carries shortcuts and a name() function; both are translated: shortcuts is List<String>? and name() trims ':' from the first shortcut.
The two emoji segment appends now use ChatPostEmote(moving, still, name) instead of ChatPostUrl, matching the new Swift call; the ChatPostUrl import was replaced with ChatPostEmote.
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin revision, including the OkHttp fetch/upload helpers and the coroutine loop.
Swift's trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: ":")) maps to Kotlin String.trim(':'), which trims the same leading/trailing ':' characters.
URL(string:) string-to-URL conversion drops away because emoji thumbnails are already String paths in Kotlin.
run.emoji?.name() is evaluated only when the emoji URL is non-null, as in Swift.

Hand-written Codable encode(to:)/init(from:) with CodingKeys is translated to @Serializable classes with @SerialName per key; every property keeps the same default the Swift decoder used for a missing key.

@Published / ObservableObject is not mapped to MutableStateFlow here because these model objects are persisted with kotlinx.serialization (StateFlow fields cannot be serialized); the properties stay plain mutable vars and are observed by the Compose settings layer.
UInt32 bitrate is mapped to Int and Int32 to Int since no wire-format/byte-parsing code is involved.

kotlinx.serialization has no built-in serializer for java.util.UUID, so a top-level UuidSerializer (KSerializer<UUID>, encoded as a string exactly like Swift's Codable UUID) was added and applied to every id property.
DeepLinkCreatorStreamAudio.bitrateFloat is not encoded in Swift and was derived from bitrate in init(from:), so it is a @Transient computed property here.
DeepLinkCreatorStream.baseName is a static let, translated to a companion object property built with localized("My stream").
[T] arrays are MutableList because the settings objects are mutated; .init() becomes ClassName().
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart; the id property is kept and the class only declares the Named interface (from com.moblin.android.various.utils).
Incremental change: only the new ProcessorDelegate method streamPhotoTaken() was added to ModelMock, right after streamNoTorch(), matching the Swift position.
streamPhotoTaken is declared with `override`, so the app-side ProcessorDelegate interface is expected to declare it as well.
All other lines, imports and declaration order are byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.

Kotlin extensions cannot add interface conformance, so the GoProDeviceDelegate implementation of Model is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model must declare GoProDeviceDelegate in its own file and this function is the body used for it.
IndexSet is replaced by Set<Int>; the settings list is trimmed in descending index order so the remaining indices stay valid.
Swift switch expressions over RtmpUrlType and GoProDeviceState become Kotlin when expressions with uppercase enum entries (SERVER/CUSTOM, CONNECTING/STREAMING/WIFI_SETUP_FAILED/FAILED).
String(localized:) becomes the top-level localized() from package com.moblin.android.
The weak self/weak device captures of the Swift closures are dropped; the lambdas run on the calling coroutine scope and capture the extension receiver directly.
autoRestartStreamTimer is expected to expose startSingleShot(timeout: Double, onFire: () -> Unit) and stop(), matching the Swift timer wrapper.
NetworkInterfaceType, IpType and IpType.formatAddress are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, hence no import is written for them.
Model members used but not declared here (goProDevices, database, getRtmpStream, makeToast, makeErrorToast) must already exist on Model.
iOS 18 availability guards are dropped; the Gimbal APIs are assumed always available in the Android port.
Apple's Spatial framework has no Android counterpart, so a local Vector3D data class is declared in this file; verify it matches the port's Gimbal.setMovement/setOrientation parameter types.
Task { } and DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter use a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main); the 0.3s deadline becomes delay(300) and defer becomes try/finally.
Deque.popFirst()/append() map to MutableList.removeFirstOrNull()/add() on Model.moveToGimbalPresetQueue.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() function from package com.moblin.android.
error.localizedDescription maps to Throwable.message.
setQuickButton uses SettingsQuickButtonType.gimbalTracking, inferred from the Swift `.gimbalTracking` case; confirm that enum exists in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
makeErrorToast, setZoomX, setQuickButton and remoteControlStateChanged are Model members declared in other files and are called with the same argument labels as in Swift.
Model extension members became top-level extension functions on Model in the same package; cleanWizardUrl, createStreamFromWizardCustomUrl and createStreamFromWizardUrl remain file-private helpers.
WizardPlatform, WizardNetworkSetup and WizardCustomProtocol are Kotlin enum classes that keep the Swift case names and order.
URLComponents is replaced with java.net.URI and URLEncoder; validity of the parsed URL is expressed with runCatching(...).getOrNull().
Faithful to the Swift optional chaining: the SRT streamid is only set when the URL already contains a query string, so a URL without '?' is returned unchanged.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
SettingsStream(name = ...) as well as the named arguments of makeErrorToast, setCurrentStream, sceneUpdated and the keychain helpers assume the ported signatures keep the Swift argument labels.
database.streams.add(stream) replaces Swift Array.append.
DefaultTcpPorts.mobcamStream from com.moblin.android.various.network is used to build the mobcam URL.
Swift `extension Model` members become top-level extension functions on Model in com.moblin.android.various.model; the private helpers stay `private` so they are only visible inside this file.

Swift `extension Model: DjiDeviceDelegate` cannot add interface conformance in Kotlin, so `djiDeviceStreamingState` is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model itself must declare `DjiDeviceDelegate` and the matching override in its own file for `djiDevice.delegate = this` to compile and for callbacks to arrive.
The `[weak self, weak device]` timer closures are plain Kotlin captures; on Android the ViewModel/Model lifetime is handled by the owning CoroutineScope, so no WeakReference is used.

`statusOther.ipStatuses` filtering compares `interfaceType`/`ipType` with their `.name` strings ("wifi"/"ipv4") because those enum types are not declared in this file's glossary and cannot be imported.
`device.autoRestartStreamTimer` is assumed to expose `startSingleShot(timeout) { }` and `stop()`; that timer type is declared with SettingsDjiDevice in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift `IndexSet` offsets become `Set<Int>` and the removal is done over descending indices so that `removeAt` positions stay valid, mirroring SwiftUI's `remove(atOffsets:)`.
The `switch` over `rtmpUrlType` becomes an exhaustive `when`; the `switch` over `DjiDeviceState` keeps an `else -> {}` branch for the remaining states.
`String(localized:)` maps to the top-level `localized()` from com.moblin.android, which is imported explicitly.
Generated SwiftProtobuf file: every Swift enum became an enum class with rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue; the message structs became mutable Kotlin classes.
Swift's computed storage/`has...`/`clear...` triplets (protobuf field presence) are kept verbatim as backing nullable fields `_x`, a property with default, a `hasX` Boolean and a `clearX()` function.
`SwiftProtobuf._NameMap(bytecode:)` was decoded by hand into a plain `Map<Int, String>` (`protoMessageName` / `_protobuf_nameMap`) since the runtime no longer exists.
`SwiftProtobuf.UnknownStorage` has no Android counterpart; `unknownFields` is represented as a `ByteArray` (empty by default) and compared with contentEquals.
`decodeMessage(decoder:)` and `traverse(visitor:)` need the SwiftProtobuf runtime (Decoder/Visitor) and are stubbed with TODO; they are the only unsupported items in this file.
The Swift `fileprivate struct _GeneratedWithProtocGenSwiftVersion` version probe is kept as a private class with nested `_2`; Kotlin cannot declare a `Version` typealias inside a class.
`SwiftProtobuf.Internal.areAllInitialized(self.entries)` became `entries.all { it.isInitialized }`.
Only `==` is written in Swift; `equals`/`hashCode` were added (with a private `byteArraysEqual` helper) so the Kotlin classes behave as value objects.

The YouTubeLiveChat call site stays `YouTubeLiveChat(model = this, videoId = videoId, settings = stream.value.chat)`: the current Kotlin YouTubeLiveChat takes a Model, not a delegate, so the Android behaviour is kept even though Swift now passes `delegate: self`.

The new Swift `extension Model: YouTubeLiveChatDelegate` is materialised as the private class ModelYouTubeLiveChatDelegate, because Kotlin cannot add an interface to Model from another file - the same pattern the file already uses for YouTubeApiDelegate.
The three delegate methods are added as top-level Model extension functions at the end of the file, keeping the Swift declaration order.
Added imports for ChatHighlight and ChatPostSegment, which the new appendChatMessage call needs.
`timestampTime: .now` becomes java.time.Instant.now(), matching the Instant used by ChatPost.timestampTime and the rest of this file.
`userBadges: []` becomes emptyList() and `segments: [ChatPostSegment]` becomes List<ChatPostSegment>.
No Swift API in this file is Apple-only; nothing was replaced by TODO().
Only the constructor label and the added delegate extension changed; every other line is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
Async Swift tests become @Test fun ... = runBlocking<Unit> { ... }; if ObsWebSocket marshals work onto Dispatchers.Main this source set also needs Dispatchers.setMain.
CompletionResult is a private sealed shim replacing Swift's Result<Value, String> so the failure value stays a String message.

Mock/helper members are called with the names and labels of the Swift originals: receiveRequest, receiveRequestBatch, respond(request, data=/errorCode=/comment=/results=), sendEvent(type=, intent=, data=), send(text=/op=), ObsMockResult.Success/Failure, ObsMockRequest(type=, id=, data=), ObsMockRequestBatch(id=, requests=).
ObsWebSocket's async initializer is invoked as the constructor ObsWebSocket(url, password, delegate) and ObsWebSocketServerMock(password).

getMediaSourcesSettingsBatch is assumed to deliver settings objects exposing input/isLocalFile, which are mapped to Pair<String, Boolean> for the completion; if the ported callback already yields Pair the map collapses to a pass-through.
areEqual is assumed to take List<Float> values and a Float epsilon.
For Completion<Unit> the onSuccess() extension is invoked from a lambda because completion::onSuccess would be ambiguous with the member function.
assertContentEquals is used for the ByteArray screenshot comparison instead of assertEquals.
Added the new VideoSources class between CameraShow and CameraState, with @Published properties as MutableStateFlow<List<Camera>> and all() reading them via .value.
The old public listCameras(position:) became the private listBuiltinCameras(position:); its hand-written Kotlin body (DeviceType.entries.toList()) is kept.
updateCameraLists() and listCameras(excludeBuiltin:) were removed, replaced by updateVideoSources()/updateDeviceVideoSources().

Declarations were reordered to match Swift: colorSpaceUpdated..shouldShowCameraPreview, then updateVideoSources, updateDeviceVideoSources, listBuiltinCameras, listExternalCameras, isBackCamera, isFrontCamera.
isBackCamera/isFrontCamera/getCameraPositionName/getExternalCameraName/isExternalCameraConnected now read videoSources.back/front/external (via .value).
The Model.videoSources property is assumed declared in Model.kt; this file only references it.
VideoSources is not a settings class, so its arrays stay MutableStateFlow with List values, written with .value =.
Swift's POSIX getaddrinfo/addrinfo/getnameinfo block is replaced with java.net.InetAddress.getAllByName, which is the supported Android resolver path.

DnsLookupFamily keeps its Swift lowercase case name and order; toCFamily() maps to android.system.OsConstants AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_UNSPEC and is retained for API parity although the lookup itself filters with Inet4Address/Inet6Address.
The Swift 'unspec' family matched every returned address; the Kotlin translation keeps that behaviour by not filtering in that branch.
The returned value is the first matching hostAddress string, matching Swift's addresses.first, or null when the lookup fails or yields no matching family.
Logger calls map to android.util.Log.i with the file-level tag "DnsLookup".
Swift's import Network is unnecessary on Android and is dropped; no Network.framework API from this file survives the port.
CryptoKit Insecure.MD5 is replaced by java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") over the UTF-8 bytes.
Swift Data maps to ByteArray; String.utf8Data is replaced by Kotlin's stdlib String.encodeToByteArray().
Data.base64EncodedString(options: .lineLength64Characters) maps to java.util.Base64.getMimeEncoder(64, LF), which is available from Android API 26.
The three Swift overloads become three Kotlin top-level functions with the same names and order; the String/ByteArray overloads stay unambiguous.
The java.util.Base64 MIME encoder pads with '=' and wraps at 64 characters, matching the Swift line-length option; callers that need an unwrapped token should strip the line breaks.
No Moblin-internal extension (utf8Data) is imported or redeclared, so this file has no dependency on other Moblin files.
MD5 is cryptographically broken but is kept unchanged because the HaishinKit protocol path depends on those exact digests.
No permission handling is needed for digest calculation.

CBytePerfMon is a libsrt C struct with no Kotlin binding in this port, so a mirror data class named CBytePerfMon is declared in this file with the same field names and C types (int32_t -> Int, double -> Double); SrtNative is expected to populate it.
The Swift memberwise init is the Kotlin primary constructor; the init(mon:) becomes a secondary constructor so both call shapes stay identical.
static let zero maps to val zero in the companion object.
Int32 in Swift maps to Int in Kotlin; Double stays Double.
The Swift mon.pktRecvNAKTotal is exposed as pktRecvNakTotal to match the existing Swift property spelling.
No native (JNI) symbols are called in this file, so no System.loadLibrary call is needed here.
Kotlin data class equality, hashCode and toString are generated, which the Swift struct got for free.
Moblin keeps these counters as plain values, so no state flow or observable wrapper is required.

NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent comes from the NetworkExtension shim (platform/networkextension/NEHotspotNetwork.kt): WifiInfo from the ConnectivityManager transport info on Android 12 and later, WifiManager before that, and null without WiFi or location permission, like iOS.
fetchCurrentWiFiSsid keeps the same callback shape: a top-level function taking (String?) -> Unit, so callers do not change.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch on a private file-level CoroutineScope on Dispatchers.Main.
The macCatalyst CoreWLAN dynamic-lookup helper is preserved as a private function of the same name returning null.
No types are declared by this file, only top-level functions, so declared_types is empty.
BluetoothScanner is an ObservableObject but not a settings class, so @Published discoveredPeripherals became MutableStateFlow<List<CBPeripheral>>; views collect it with collectAsState().
The Swift class is non-final, so it is declared open class with open val discoveredPeripherals and open funs.
private var centralManager uses CBCentralManager.holder(), so assigning null releases the manager and closes its connections exactly like ARC.
The Swift extension that conforms to CBCentralManagerDelegate is folded into the class header, and the delegate methods use override because the shim interface provides default bodies.
CBCentralManager(delegate: self, queue: .main) maps to CBCentralManager(delegate = this, queue = null): the main queue is the default.
discoveredPeripherals.append(peripheral) becomes a value assignment on the flow (value = value + peripheral), and the duplicate check reads .value.
The delegate methods are declared with all four parameter names even though the Swift code ignores advertisementData and rssi.
CMMotionManager, CMAccelerometerData and OperationQueue.main come from the CoreMotion shim (platform/coremotion/CoreMotion.kt), so the constructor keeps the Swift parameter motionManager.
startAccelerometerUpdates(to: .main) becomes startAccelerometerUpdates(to = OperationQueue.main); the handler runs on the main thread, paced to the 0.1 s accelerometerUpdateInterval.
data.acceleration is a CMAcceleration in g on iOS axes with gravity included, so the magnitude is about 1 at rest, as on iOS.
guard let data, error == nil else { return } becomes an early return@startAccelerometerUpdates.
GForce is a @Serializable data class; its property names match the Swift coding keys exactly, so no @SerialName is needed.
getLatest() keeps the Swift optional return type GForce? even though the Swift implementation always returns a value.
NSObject is dropped; ObservableObject with @Published array becomes MutableStateFlow<List<GoProDiscoveredDevice>> per the scanner rule, so readers use discoveredDevices.collectAsState().
centralManager is a stored optional CBCentralManager backed by CBCentralManager.holder(); assigning null releases it like ARC (scan stops, no more delegate calls).
The Swift extension conformance is merged into the class header, so both delegate methods are override fun of CBCentralManagerDelegate.
CBCentralManager(delegate:self, queue:.main) uses queue = null because .main, DispatchQueue.main and nil all map to the main queue in the shim.

goProControlServiceId is not declared in this file: it is expected as a top-level CBUUID val in package com.moblin.android.integrations.gopro (GoProDevice.kt); no import is needed since it is the same package.
String(localized: "Unknown") becomes localized("Unknown") from com.moblin.android.
discoveredDevices.append(.init(...)) becomes a value reassignment with a new list plus a GoProDiscoveredDevice, and the duplicate check uses any { it.peripheral.identifier == peripheral.identifier }.
The whole class stays main-actor-less: the shim delivers every central delegate call on the queue given to the manager (here the main queue), in order.
NWPathMonitor is replaced with ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback, so a Context parameter was added to the constructor because Android needs it.
NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart and is replaced by a local InterfaceType enum keeping the same case names (cellular, wifi, wiredEthernet, other).
The DispatchQueue queue parameter is kept as a CoroutineDispatcher to preserve the public API shape but is not used by the Android connectivity callback.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and was dropped.
Collections.Deque is replaced with kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque.
pathUpdateHandler is mapped to onCapabilitiesChanged; since only the default network is observed, .other is used when the network exposes none of the wifi/cellular/ethernet transports.
The `if self.cellular` guard is expressed as `this@NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.cellular` inside the anonymous NetworkCallback.
The registration is never unregistered because the Swift file exposes no cancel path; the owner must call unregisterNetworkCallback if needed.

`@Published var discoveredPeripherals` became `open val discoveredPeripherals = MutableStateFlow<List<CBPeripheral>>(emptyList())`, read with collectAsState and mutated with `.value = ...` so it stays observable.
The `CBCentralManagerDelegate` extension was folded into the class header with `override fun`s, as the shim's delegate methods use those names.
`.main` as the central manager queue maps to `queue = null` (the shim then delivers callbacks on the main thread).
`centralManager` is held with `by CBCentralManager.holder()` so assigning null releases the old manager like ARC, closing its scan.
`localName.wholeMatch(of: /S[0-9a-f]{16}C/)` is `Regex("S[0-9a-f]{16}C").matches(localName)`, an entire-string match.
`discoveredPeripherals.contains(where:)` uses the shim's `==` on `CBPeripheral`, which compares identifiers; appending rebuilds the list (`+ peripheral`) because a StateFlow holds an immutable list.
`static let shared` became `companion object { val shared by lazy { ... } }`, read as `TeslaVehicleScanner.shared`.

CoreBluetooth ids stay CBUUID, as required for BLE device protocol files: workoutDeviceHeartRateServiceId and workoutDeviceHeartRateMeasurementCharacteristicId are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = ...).
HeartRateMeasurement keeps its Swift shape as a file-private class with a secondary constructor taking the value bytes, since a data class cannot hold the parsing init.
Swift throws/try disappear: ByteReader's readUInt8/readUInt16Le are non-throwing in Kotlin, so handleMeasurement is a plain function and the init needs no try.
UShort is used for the 16-bit heart-rate field because this is BLE wire parsing; Int(measurement.heartRate) becomes measurement.heartRate.toInt().
UInt16(reader.readUInt8()) is a widening conversion, written readUInt8().toUShort().
flags.isBitSet(index:) comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and takes the UByte flags of the measurement byte.
Data parameters become ByteArray and the class is open because the Swift class is non-final, so its members are open too.
The private top-level format-index constant stays private in this file.

Swift's throwing `init(value:)` on the file-private struct becomes the companion factory `CyclingSpeedCadenceMeasurement.parse(value)`; ByteReader throws naturally, so Kotlin needs no `throws` clause.
The 32-bit wheel-revolution delta is widened to Long so the `+ 4294967296` wraparound cannot overflow Kotlin's Int.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and is imported explicitly.
`ContinuousClock.now` and `ContinuousClock.Instant` come from com.moblin.android.platform.core; the 3-second guard uses `3.seconds` from kotlin.time.
UInt/UShort values are value-preserving converted with `toLong()`/`toInt()` and never reinterpreted as bytes.
`measurementCharacteristic` is stored but only tested by `isAnyCharacteristicDiscovered()`, exactly as in Swift.
The class stays `open` with `open` members because the Swift class is not final; all stored state stays `private`.
Average calculator and crank cadence come from the same Kotlin package, so no imports are needed for them.
ByteReader's Kotlin methods do not throw, so the Swift `throws` on RscMeasurement's init and on handleMeasurement is dropped; callers that wrap the call in try still compile.
The throwing Swift init of RscMeasurement became `RscMeasurement.create(value)` on a private data class, because a Kotlin constructor cannot parse with several statements.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` is the extension from com.moblin.android.common.various, imported and called with the named argument as on the shim contract.
`lastRscUpdateTime.duration(to: now).seconds` becomes `duration(to = now).toDouble(DurationUnit.SECONDS)` from com.moblin.android.platform.core.ContinuousClock.
WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics is a synthesized-Codable struct, so it is an @Serializable data class with the Swift property names and null defaults so absent JSON keys decode like Swift.
WorkoutDeviceRunning is a non-final Swift class, so it becomes an open class with open members and private backing properties.
The two CoreBluetooth UUID constants are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = "..."), matching the shim constructor.
The two flag indices stay file-private constants with their Swift names.
A Context is now a constructor parameter because ConnectivityManager cannot be obtained without one; pass the application context.
NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback with a main-Looper Handler, so callbacks arrive on the main thread like the Swift @MainActor code.
NWInterface.InterfaceType became the local InterfaceType enum, mapped from NetworkCapabilities transports (wifi/cellular/ethernet, otherwise other).
The ifaddrs walk is replaced by ConnectivityManager.allNetworks for the interface list and java.net.NetworkInterface.getByName(name).inetAddresses for the addresses.
IPv6 scope suffixes such as %wlan0 are stripped from hostAddress before the address is reported.
start() needs ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE on the manifest; the permission request stays in the Activity layer.
Swift's init only installed monitor.pathUpdateHandler; that handler is now the NetworkCallback overrides, so init just builds the callback object.
Swift URL is stored only, so pushUrl/stopUrl are plain String fields built from baseUrl and pushKey.
The failable init? becomes a regular primary constructor because there is no URL parsing failure path once URL is a String; call sites get a non-null RealtimeIrl.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, speed -> speed, altitude -> altitude, timestamp.timeIntervalSince1970 -> location.time / 1000.0.
The POST body is built as a plain JSON string like the Swift version; content type application/json is set via OkHttp MediaType.
httpRequest is expected to take an okhttp3.Request; the JSON body is sent with toRequestBody().
stop() sends an empty POST body because OkHttp rejects a POST with a null body.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer.
Network.framework NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; reads happen on a Dispatchers.IO coroutine and writes are fire-and-forget coroutines, matching .idempotent send semantics.
ContinuousClock.Instant is represented as monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(); isActive compares the delta against removeTimeoutNanos.
The Swift connection.batch / receiveMessage batch-of-100 pattern becomes a single blocking InputStream.read loop; connectionReceiveBatchSize is kept but unused.
A private ByteArray.setUInt32Be extension is added locally because the common package only guarantees createSrtlaPacket, srtControlTypeSize and the packet parsers.
logger.info/debug map to Log.i/Log.d with tag SrtlaServerClientConnection.
SrtlaServerClientConnectionDelegate protocol becomes a Kotlin interface; AckPacket struct becomes a mutable class.
isSrtDataPacket, getSrtControlPacketType and getSrtSequenceNumber from the common package are used as ByteArray member extensions.
connection.cancel() maps to Socket.close(); stop() also cancels the receive coroutine.
Swift's `nonisolated(unsafe) let ... = CBUUID(string:)` globals become top-level vals calling the CBUUID shim with `string =`.

The private PowerMeasurement/PowerVector structs keep their throwing `init(value:)` as a Kotlin class whose `init` block parses through ByteReader; call sites stay `PowerMeasurement(value)` / `PowerVector(value)`.
`try` disappears: ByteReader's reads throw on their own, so the parsing code is a plain sequence of calls.
UInt8 flags use ByteReader.readUInt8() -> UByte; the direction mask is a private UByte val because a UByte literal cannot be a `const val`, and the shift goes through toInt() since UByte has no shr.
The private raw-value enum gets a `rawValue` property and a companion `fromRawValue` returning null for unknown values, matching the Swift failable `init?(rawValue:)`.
`isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various; WorkoutDeviceAverageCalculator/WorkoutDeviceCrankCadence are in this same package so they need no import.
Crank data is read with readUInt16Le (little-endian) exactly as in Swift, and the tuple result of handleMeasurement becomes Pair<Int, Int?>.
`now: .now` becomes ContinuousClock.now from com.moblin.android.platform.core.
CoreLocation maps to android.location: CLLocation -> Location, CLPlacemark -> Address, CLGeocoder -> android.location.Geocoder.
The class gains a Context constructor parameter because Geocoder needs one; every other member keeps its Swift name and signature.
@MainActor becomes a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main), and Task<Void, any Error> becomes kotlinx.coroutines.Job; the geocoding call is moved to Dispatchers.IO via withContext.
Task.isCancelled becomes isActive of the launch scope, so the polling loop still exits after cancellation.
sleep(seconds:) is assumed to be the suspend function sleep(seconds: Int) from com.moblin.android.common.various; the delay variable stays an Int number of seconds.
The do/catch around the sleep and geocode becomes runCatching { ... } so a failed lookup keeps the loop alive, exactly like the Swift catch.
Geocoder.getFromLocation is blocking, so it must not run on the main dispatcher.
Location.distanceTo returns Float while Swift returned CLLocationDistance (Double); the 1001/1000 literal fallback and threshold stay the same numbers.
The Swift `extension Model: CBCentralManagerDelegate` becomes a top-level extension function `fun Model.centralManagerDidUpdateState` in this package, since Model itself is declared in Model.kt.
`Model.bluetoothAllowed` is a `MutableStateFlow<Boolean>`, so the assignment writes `bluetoothAllowed.value = ...`.
`CBCentralManager.authorization == .allowedAlways` maps to `CBManagerAuthorization.allowedAlways` from the CoreBluetooth shim.
The `@MainActor` attribute is dropped; when a CBCentralManager is created it is given `delegate = { model.centralManagerDidUpdateState(it) }` and its queue, and that queue defines the thread.
`let bluetoothNotAllowedMessage` is a global String constant and becomes a top-level `const val`.
The unused `_: CBCentralManager` parameter is named `central` in Kotlin.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location, the same type the WeatherService shim accepts.
The Swift Task<Void, any Error>? loop becomes a Job launched from a main-dispatched CoroutineScope; Task.isCancelled is checked with the coroutine scope's isActive.
try await sleep(seconds: delay) is sleepSeconds(seconds = delay) from com.moblin.android.common.various.
weatherService.weather(for: location) is called with the backticked keyword parameter `for` exactly as the shim declares.
logger.debug is android.util.Log.d with "WeatherManager" as the tag.
The non-final Swift class keeps open members so subclasses can override, matching Swift.
The private stored properties stay private, so they are never marked open.

NetServiceBrowser and NetService are replaced by android.net.nsd NsdManager discovery and resolve listeners; the class now implements NsdManager.DiscoveryListener and NsdManager.ResolveListener instead of the two NetService delegate protocols.
MoblinkScanner now takes a Context as its first constructor parameter, needed to obtain NsdManager via Context.NSD_SERVICE.
moblinkBonjourDomain is unused: android.net.nsd has no domain parameter, discovery always runs in the local domain.
resolve(withTimeout: 5.0) has no counterpart; NsdManager has no resolve timeout and failures arrive in onResolveFailed, which stays empty like the Swift file's missing didNotResolve.
service.addresses is reduced to NsdServiceInfo.host, so at most one websocket url is appended per resolved service.
Discovered services are matched by serviceName because NsdServiceInfo equality is not reliable across API levels.

@MainActor is dropped; the delegate is notified from a mainScope coroutine on Dispatchers.Main. The weak delegate reference cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so it is stored strongly in a nullable property.
NsdManager allows only one outstanding resolve per listener; onServiceFound resolves directly with this listener, so overlapping resolves can report onResolveFailed.

libsrt is reached through an `internal object SrtNative` declared in this file: it loads libsrt in its init block and exposes `external fun srt_setsockopt` with the same name and argument order as the C API. Keep a single SrtNative per package and extend it with the other srt_* calls as later files need them.

SRT_SOCKOPT and SRT_TRANSTYPE numbers come from the libsrt C header and are declared here as file-private const vals (srt.h 1.5 numbering); verify them against the libsrt fork bundled in the NDK build, SRTO_SRTLAPATCHES in particular.
snddropdelay keeps the raw option number 32 of the Swift source, exposed as the named constant SRTO_SNDDROPDELAY.

URL/URLComponents/removingPercentEncoding are replaced by android.net.Uri.queryParameterNames + getQueryParameter, which already percent-decodes values; getQueryItems therefore takes a String, not a URI.
Enum entry names stay lowercase exactly as in Swift so that rawValue (the query-string key, e.g. "srtlaPatches") is byte-identical.
MemoryLayout.size(ofValue:) is reproduced with fixed widths: Int -> 4 bytes, Int64 -> 8 bytes, written in native byte order (Android is little-endian).
The Swift enumeration branch sized its buffer from the String value (16 bytes) instead of the SRT_TRANSTYPE; the Kotlin version writes the intended 4-byte Int32 value.
logger.info(...) becomes Log.i with the class name as tag.
observableObject without settings semantics: discoveredDevices is a MutableStateFlow<List<DjiDiscoveredDevice>>, mutated through .value as the BLE shim section requires
centralManager is stored with the CBCentralManager.holder() property delegate so assigning null releases the old manager like ARC
DjiDeviceScanner now implements CBCentralManagerDelegate in its class header because Swift's delegate extension moves into the type
NSObject and ObservableObject have no Kotlin counterpart and are dropped; no other supertype is needed
CBCentralManager(delegate: self, queue: DispatchQueue.main) becomes CBCentralManager(delegate = this, queue = null), since .main maps to a null queue
logger.info is translated to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag
the backslash-joined Swift multi-line log string is a single line here, with manufacturerData.hexString() from com.moblin.android.common.various
the struct DjiDiscoveredDevice becomes a data class with the same property names and order
Model, StatusTopRight, LocationManager and the settings/database types are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, so only RealtimeIrl and the Android/JDK types are imported.

CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, horizontalAccuracy -> accuracy, verticalAccuracy -> verticalAccuracyMeters, distance(from:) -> distanceTo() widened to Double.
The privacy-region loop assumes the region type exposes contains(latitude: Double, longitude: Double); the Swift version took a CLLocationCoordinate2D.
statusTopRight.location = location assumes StatusTopRight exposes a mutable location property (class with var), not an immutable data class.
ContinuousClock.Instant is replaced by monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(), so updateAverageSpeed takes now: Long and resetAverageSpeed stores System.nanoTime().
getLatestKnownLocation() returns Pair<Double, Double>? because Swift returns an optional tuple.
The Moblin LocationManager wrapper is used with the same call shape (status/stop/start/getLatestKnownLocation); the onUpdate callback is passed as a Kotlin lambda.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer; this file only starts/stops updates.

Kotlin cannot add protocol conformance from an extension, so Model's HttpProxyServerDelegate conformance is kept as the extension function httpProxyServerPortReady plus an anonymous adapter object assigned to HttpProxyServer.delegate.
NWEndpoint.hostPort is represented as java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", port) and NWEndpoint.Port as Int, so getHttpProxyServerEndpoint returns InetSocketAddress?.
Model must already declare httpProxyServer: HttpProxyServer?, httpProxyPort: Int? and database whose httpProxy exposes enabled, localNetwork and port.
setWebBrowserProxy() and setBrowserEffectsProxyServer() are resolved as Model members or extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.model.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus launch.
All functions are top-level extension functions on Model in this package, matching the Swift extension.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced by java.net.Socket / java.net.DatagramSocket running in coroutines on Dispatchers.IO; NWEndpoint host+port become String + Int.
The `weak var delegate` becomes a plain strong `var delegate` because Kotlin has no weak properties.
The original callback-driven receive chain is rebuilt as coroutine while-loops so a long stream does not grow the JVM stack.
Reading exactly N bytes is done with a loop over InputStream.read since Kotlin has no minimumIncompleteLength/maximumLength receive API.
stop() closes the sockets (to unblock the blocking reads) and then cancels the CoroutineScope.
ByteWriter (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util) is assumed to expose writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16(UShort), writeBytes(ByteArray) and the `data` property.
logger.debug/info map to Log.d/Log.i with the tag "RtspTransport".
rtspTransportDisconnected() is never invoked because the Swift transport never calls it either.

The file-private serial DispatchQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineScope(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor().asCoroutineDispatcher()); start/stop/setWheelCircumference keep hopping onto it with launch.
centralManager is stored through CBCentralManager.holder() so assigning null releases the previous manager and its connections exactly like ARC.
delegate stays a plain nullable var (Swift weak); no WeakReference is used.
The @MainActor global workoutDeviceScanner becomes a top-level val constructed from the four service ids.
WorkoutDevice implements CBCentralManagerDelegate (fun interface) and CBPeripheralDelegate in the class header; only the delegate methods the Swift file uses are overridden.
In peripheralDidDiscoverCharacteristicsFor the CBPeripheral parameter is named peripheralArg because the body uses the stored peripheral property.
Swift's try around the delegate calls is dropped (the Kotlin delegate methods and handleMeasurement do not throw); the do/catch around characteristic handling stays as try/catch.
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with tag "WorkoutDevice"; CBUUID interpolation uses uuidString.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced with java.net.Socket/ServerSocket on Dispatchers.IO; the callback-driven receive loops became blocking read loops inside coroutines.
NWEndpoint is replaced by a host String plus a port Int, so HttpConnectRequestParser.Result carries destinationHost/destinationPort instead of an NWEndpoint.

The file-level serial DispatchQueue is a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); Swift's serial execution guarantee is lost, so the shared `connections` list and `stopping` flag would need extra synchronization in production.
logger.info calls become android.util.Log.i with tag "HttpProxyServer".
HttpParser.getLine is assumed to return Pair<String, Int>? and HttpParser.data a ByteArray; both live in this same package so nothing is imported.
NWInterface/NWInterface.InterfaceType map to android.net.Network: NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.getType() returns Network? and markBad takes it.
NWListener state updates are collapsed into handleStateUpdate(error: Exception?), where null means the ready state and a non-null value the failed state.
The body byte range is stored before connectToDestination runs (Swift sets it after the async connect) so the tunneling socket can flush it.
The diff only swaps URLSession.shared for httpUrlSession() in the uploadTask branch, i.e. it makes the shared HTTP client explicit, which the Kotlin port already does.

httpCallUrlSession in Kotlin is a hand-written merge of the Swift body and no-body branches: it attaches the body to the OkHttp Request and always goes through httpRequest(), which itself uses httpUrlSession().
That hand-written form already matches the new Swift intent (both branches use the same session), so no Kotlin line changes.
Every other Kotlin line, import and declaration stays byte-identical to the previous revision.
Global `logger` becomes android.util.Log with tag "ObsWebSocket"; `logger.debugEnabled` maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG).

The untyped JSON envelope (op/d/eventType/...) is parsed with org.json (the Android counterpart of JSONSerialization); typed payloads use kotlinx.serialization with ignoreUnknownKeys = true so unknown keys are skipped like Swift's JSONDecoder.
Swift's `throw "some string"` became IllegalStateException("..."), and `try?` became runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(); `try { } catch {}` became runCatching { }.onSuccess { }.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent: delegate is a strongly referenced constructor property, so the caller must drop the ObsWebSocket instance to break the cycle.

@MainActor is emulated with a private mainScope (CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)) used only inside the WebSocketClientDelegate callbacks; all public methods must be called from the main dispatcher as before.
The UInt64 event-subscription bitmask is kept as ULong (wire format) and serialized by kotlinx.serialization's built-in unsigned serializer.

Assumed WebSocketClient API (from com.moblin.android.various.network): constructor WebSocketClient(url: String, loopback: Boolean), var delegate: WebSocketClientDelegate?, start(), stop(), send(string) -- verify against the Kotlin port of WebSocketClient.kt.

`URL` is stored as String and `url.isLoopback()` (not present in the glossary) is replaced by a private isLoopback(String) helper using java.net.URI; request bodies are pre-encoded with Json.encodeToString at the call site because Kotlin cannot encode an `any Encodable`.
pauseBetweenMessages default changed from 0.0 to 0.5.
Added isPausingBetweenMessages and a SimpleTimer on textToSpeechDispatchQueue that gates trySayNextMessage, mirroring AVSpeechUtterance.preUtteranceDelay removal.
skipCurrentMessageInternal now waits 0.5 s before the next message; sayFinished waits pauseBetweenMessages.
reset() also stops the pause timer via stopPauseBetweenMessages().
The Android-only delay that emulated preUtteranceDelay inside utterApple is removed because the pause is now scheduled centrally.
NLLanguageRecognizer has no Android port, so dominantLanguage/languageProbability stay as local stubs; the filter keeps its 0.7 threshold.
deleteByUserId keeps the previous Kotlin name for Swift delete(userId:).

WiFiAware (Wi-Fi Aware listener/connection) and Network.framework's declarative NetworkListener/NetworkConnection have no counterpart in this port, so listen() keeps its signature and its body is TODO("no Android counterpart for WiFiAware").
actor WiFiAwareReceiver -> plain class with suspend members; the Swift 'static let shared' singleton becomes 'val shared' in the companion object.
private struct Sender -> file-private data class Sender; Swift Task<Void, Never> -> kotlinx.coroutines.Job, cancelled with task.cancel().
NetworkConnection<UDP> has no Kotlin type equivalent here, so 'connection' is typed Any; the Android realization of the UDP data path would be a java.net.DatagramSocket driven on Dispatchers.IO.
The 'connections' array is exposed as a file-private MutableList<Sender> of the class; actor isolation must be provided by a Mutex if the list is later mutated concurrently.
Swift 'async throws' becomes a suspend function; errors surface as thrown exceptions rather than a checked error type.
The '#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)' compile guard and '@available(iOS 26, *)' annotations are dropped since they have no Kotlin meaning.
logger.info(...) lines disappear with the stubbed body; when the body is implemented use android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
apple_only: WiFiAware framework (Wi-Fi Aware listening, publishable/subscribable service pairing)
Network.framework declarative NetworkListener / NetworkConnection API

notes: NWListener/NWConnection (UDP) are replaced by one loopback DatagramSocket. The 'connection' is the remote InetSocketAddress of the first peer that sends a packet, and packets are sent back over that same socket so the local source port stays stable for the SRT peer.
onReady passes the port as Int because Android exposes ports as Int; UInt16 is only used for wire formats in this port.

srtlaClientQueue is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher/CoroutineContext, so the class builds CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + srtlaClientQueue). If it is declared as a CoroutineScope instead, replace this with srtlaClientQueue.launch { }.
NWListener.State is replaced by a private nested enum ListenerState(setup, ready, failed); setup is a no-op and every other failure maps to the same 'bad network state' error message as in Swift.
The receive loop drains incoming datagrams so the peer endpoint can be detected; the payload is discarded because the Swift file exposes no receive handler on its connection.
stop() closes the socket, which also unblocks the blocking DatagramSocket.receive; the scope itself is not cancelled so the listener can be started again.
DatagramSocket.send is blocking and therefore dispatched onto srtlaClientQueue from the non-suspend sendPacket().
All logging uses android.util.Log.i with tag LocalListener and the same message text as the Swift logger calls.
CoreBluetooth ids stay top-level CBUUID vals built with CBUUID(string = ...), and the UInt8 protocol ids stay top-level UByte vals.
Data becomes ByteArray: Data([a, b]) -> byteArrayOf(a.toByte(), b.toByte()), concatenation uses ByteArray.plus, and Data() -> ByteArray(0).
Byte parsing uses (x.toInt() and mask) then .toByte(), so the UInt8 masks and header shifts keep Swift's unsigned semantics.
Protobuf requests use the ported types with the same property names (result, phoneName, scanID, maxEntries, bypassEulaCheck, ...); Int32 maps to Int and UInt32 to UInt.
The file-private SwiftProtobuf.Message.encoded() extension becomes a file-private fun Message.encoded() using runCatching { serializedData() }.getOrNull() ?: ByteArray(0).
The two toProtobuf() extensions are kept, one file-private for SettingsGoProLaunchLiveStreamResolution and one public for SettingsGoProLens returning a nullable OpenGopro_EnumLens.
GoProBleMessageAccumulator keeps its switch as a when expression so headerLength is definitely assigned, and reset() reassigns payload to ByteArray(0).
The ScanEntry helpers test the flags with Int bitwise and against OpenGopro_EnumScanEntryFlags rawValue.
MoblinkStreamer gains a Context constructor parameter (first position) because the Bonjour advertisement now uses android.net.nsd.NsdManager; port/password/name keep the Swift names and order.
NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket plus a file-private WebSocketConnection that performs the RFC 6455 HTTP upgrade and frame coding on Dispatchers.IO.
NWConnection.start(queue:) has no equivalent and its call site was dropped: the Kotlin connection is usable as soon as the handshake helper returns it.
NWEndpoint is represented as host String + port Int, so MoblinkStreamerDelegate takes host/port instead of an endpoint object and Relay stores tunnelEndpointHost/tunnelEndpointPort.
moblinkBonjourDomain has no NsdManager counterpart, so only name/type/TXT attributes are registered.
@MainActor is modelled with CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main): all relay bookkeeping and delegate callbacks are dispatched there, so the mutable relay list needs no locks.
MainTimer, SimpleStringStorage(key:) and randomString() call sites assume the Kotlin ports kept the Swift labels; MainTimer intervals are passed as Double seconds per the TimeInterval mapping.

MoblinkRequest/MoblinkResponse/MoblinkMessageToRelay/MoblinkMessageToStreamer are matched with `is` checks and property names taken from the Swift case labels (id, result, data, apiVersion, authentication).
NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; connect, read and write run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO and all blocking calls stay off the caller thread.
NWProtocolTLS.Options is mapped to javax.net.ssl.SSLContext? (null keeps plain TCP); an RTMPS caller passes an SSLContext whose socket factory creates the SSLSocket.

The DispatchQueue constructor argument became a CoroutineDispatcher named queue, still used for the delayed close and the too-much-buffered disconnect; short latency trickles stay on the caller side otherwise.
NWConnection.viabilityUpdateHandler has no Android counterpart, so viabilityDidChange is kept intact but must be driven by the caller (e.g. a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback).
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart; it is modelled by the private sealed class RtmpSocketConnectionState (Ready/Failed/Cancelled) declared in this file and fed from connect().
weak var delegate cannot be expressed in Kotlin; delegate is a plain nullable property and the owner must clear it when the socket is released.
RtmpChunk.split, RtmpMessage.length, RtmpHandshake.sigSize, RtmpHandshake.createC0C1Packet/createC2Packet and RtmpConnectionCode.eventData() are assumed from the sibling files of the same package.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "RtmpSocket".
CLLocationManager, CLBackgroundActivitySession and the delegate protocol come from com.moblin.android.platform.corelocation; CLLocation is android.location.Location, imported as AndroidLocation.

LocationManager has no desiredAccuracy/distanceFilter: the accuracy choice selects the provider (ACCURACY_FINE for best and nearestTenMeters, ACCURACY_COARSE for hundredMeters) and the distance filter sets the private minDistance Float, both applied by the private startUpdatingLocation() once a location permission is granted.

The class implements android.location.LocationListener and CLLocationManagerDelegate: didFailWithError becomes onProviderDisabled, didUpdateLocations becomes onLocationChanged, and onProviderEnabled/onStatusChanged are kept as empty overrides for Android 10 and older.
@Published isDenied is a MutableStateFlow(false); format(speed:) from com.moblin.android.common.various is called as formatSpeed(location.speed.toDouble()).

start()'s manager.delegate / requestWhenInUseAuthorization calls go through the CLLocationManager authorization shim, whose locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization also restarts location updates when the user grants permission and onUpdate is set.
The iOS 17 availability check around CLBackgroundActivitySession is dropped because the shim always exists on Android.
Location takes the application Context in its constructor (Model passes AppDelegate.context).
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with the "Location" tag.

Network.framework's NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; the NWConnection.stateUpdateHandler/NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart, so handleStateUpdate now takes a String state description and is invoked as 'ready'/'failed: ...' when the loopback socket connects or fails.
All blocking socket reads (receive loop) and writes happen inside a CoroutineScope built from srtlaServerQueue, which is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher (kotlinx.coroutines).

SRT wire values keep unsigned Kotlin types per the port rules: the NakPacket sequence numbers, timestamps and socket ids are UInt and the control-packet type/bit values are UShort (i.e. isSrtSnAcked(sn, ackSn) is called with UInt arguments).

The srtla.common helpers are called in their Swift free-function form (isSrtDataPacket(packet), getSrtControlPacketType(packet), getSrtSequenceNumber(packet), processSrtNak(packet) { }); if the sibling file declared them as ByteArray extension functions the calls only need a receiver/argument swap.
packet.getUInt32Be(8)/getUInt32Be(12) is assumed to exist as a ByteArray extension in com.moblin.android.media.srtla.common; it is not listed in the glossary but is used by the Swift file.
srtPort is an Int (port numbers are not wire-format data), and the loopback connection is created with InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1").
ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to java.time.Instant, so duration comparisons use Duration.between(...) (millis for the 25 ms data flush, precise nanos for the 10 s client removal timeout).

NWConnection.batch/send(content:completion:) have no counterpart: the local SRT server socket is written through its OutputStream inside scope.launch, keeping Swift's 25 ms coalescing of data packets.
DispatchQueue(label:) becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher; every `async { }` becomes CoroutineScope(queue).launch { }.
centralManager uses `by CBCentralManager.holder()` so assigning null releases the manager and its connections exactly like ARC on iOS.
ProcessInfo.thermalState comes from com.moblin.android.platform.core; `@unknown default` becomes `else`.
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with the tag "BlackSharkCoolerDevice".
`weak var delegate` becomes a plain nullable var, since the port has no weak references; the delegate protocol stays an interface.
`[weak self]` inside the periodic cooling-stats timer is dropped, as for other platform callbacks.
Swift's locals named coolingPower/fanSpeed shadow the stored properties and are never written back; reads use explicit `this.` to preserve that behaviour.
CBUUID comparison stays inside `when` branch conditions built with CBUUID(data = ...), matching Swift's `case CBUUID(data:)` pattern.
Apple-only tier: every HealthKit-touching body is TODO("no Android counterpart for HealthKit"); properties keep null defaults so callers still compile.
Workout stays a file-private singleton reached through Workout.shared; the HealthKit delegate protocols become plain member functions keeping the same names and parameters.

Kotlin has no argument labels, so add(heartRate:), add(cyclingPower:) and add(cyclingCadence:) become addHeartRate, addCyclingPower and addCyclingCadence; the private add(type:unit:value:) keeps its name.
WatchProtocolWorkoutType is declared here as a placeholder enum (WALKING, RUNNING, CYCLING) because the watch protocol file is not in the glossary; delete this declaration once that file is ported.
HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutBuilder, HKSampleType, HKQuantityType and HKUnit become Any, Date becomes java.time.Instant, ContinuousClock.Instant also becomes java.time.Instant.
Workout.isActive() and the private types() helper keep real implementations because they use no Apple API; the #available(iOS 26.0) guards are dropped.
The nonisolated delegate callbacks are not dispatched to the main queue any more: coroutine dispatch belongs in the ported watch/health layer, not in these TODO stubs.
Calls to logger, String(localized:), makeErrorToast and setIsWorkout vanish with the TODO bodies, so no logging or localization import is needed.
apple_only: HealthKit (HKHealthStore, HKWorkoutConfiguration, HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutSessionDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutBuilder, HKLiveWorkoutBuilderDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutDataSource, HKQuantitySample, HKUnit, HKSampleType, HKWorkoutSessionState)
WatchConnectivity (source of the WatchProtocolWorkoutType workout kinds)
ContinuousClock.Instant and HKWorkoutSession state transitions used for sample rate limiting

notes: NWInterface has no android.net.Network equivalent for type/name/index, so a file-local MoblinkRelayInterface wrapper (network, name, index, type) carries the values read from ConnectivityManager.

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback registered with a cellular/ethernet NetworkRequest; MoblinkRelay.applicationContext must be assigned by the Activity layer before start() so the ConnectivityManager can be obtained.

The UDP tunnel uses java.net.DatagramSocket receive loops on moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO); NWListener/NWConnection state callbacks have no counterpart, so the listener-ready response and the waitingForCellular -> connected transitions are inlined in handleStartTunnel.
Android has no public API to bind a DatagramSocket to a specific android.net.Network, so the destination socket is created unbound; destinationInterface is only used to select and compare relays.
@MainActor is dropped; mainScope (Dispatchers.Main) and moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO) replace the dispatch queues. The delegate is held strongly because Kotlin has no weak references.
UUID.add(data:) is replaced by java.util.UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes over relayId + interface name (then name becomes 'name-index').

Assumed Kotlin APIs from the port: WebSocketClient(url[, cellular]), send(string), delegate; WebSocketClientDelegate.webSocketClientConnected/Disconnected/ReceiveMessage; MainTimer.startSingleShot(timeout, handler); SimpleStringStorage.get()/set(); Moblink* sealed subclasses and remoteControlHashPassword(challenge, salt, password).
MoblinkRelayState and RelayState keep their Swift raw values through a rawValue property plus a fromRawValue companion helper.

Swift now groups .osmoPocket4 and .osmoPocket4Pro: the Kotlin when branches in processSettingUpWifi and sendStartStreaming list both SettingsDjiDeviceModel.osmoPocket4 and SettingsDjiDeviceModel.osmoPocket4Pro.

SettingsDjiDeviceModel as currently declared in com.moblin.android.various.settings has no osmoPocket4Pro entry yet; it must be added (rawValue "osmoPocket4Pro") for this file to compile, and hasNewProtocol()/hasImageStabilization()/hasVideoCodec() should cover it like the other Pocket devices.

The header: argument was dropped from both DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload2 constructions in sendStartStreaming, matching the current Kotlin declaration of that payload, which has no header parameter.
The oa5: model.hasNewProtocol() argument was dropped from the DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload construction in the default branch; the DjiConfigureMessagePayload oa5 argument is unchanged.
Everything else in the Kotlin file, including the CBCentralManager.holder() property delegate and the log TAG calls, is untouched.
Actor -> class with a companion object holding `shared`; the connection table is a ConcurrentHashMap so it is safe from the launched tasks.
Task<Void, Never> -> Job from scope.launch; sleep(seconds: 5) -> delay(5_000); the sender/receiver closure bodies map onto coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

NWConnection over UDP -> java.net.DatagramSocket; send/receive build and fill DatagramPacket instances, and the peer address comes from remoteSocketAddress, so the socket handed over must already be connected to the peer.

WiFiAware (NetworkBrowser, NetworkConnection, WAPairedDevice) is only reachable through the private suspend helper browseWiFiAware, which is a TODO; on Android this is android.net.wifi.aware (attach/publish/subscribe + WifiAwareNetworkSpecifier) or NetLink ServiceDiscovery.
WAPairedDevice.ID -> String device id used as the map key.
The Swift `try?` around browser.run disappears: browseWiFiAware throws NotImplementedError until it is implemented, so the cleanup and 'Stop' logging after it do not run yet.
DatagramSocket.receive is blocking, so cancelling the receiver task only ends the loop once a packet arrives or the socket is closed.
Receiver keeps the same three stored properties in the same order, with senderTask/receiverTask as Job.
apple_only: WiFiAware NetworkBrowser / NetworkConnection over UDP (Network.framework on Wi-Fi Aware)

notes: DispatchQueue ristQueue became a single-thread coroutine dispatcher (ristDispatcher) plus a CoroutineScope (ristScope); ristQueue.sync { } blocks map to runBlocking(ristDispatcher) { }, ristQueue.async/named queues map to scope.launch.

The Rist C library has no ready JNI binding, so its types (RistPeer, RistSenderContext, RistSenderStats, RistStats, RistSenderContextDelegate) are declared in this file following the libsrt rule: the wrapper keeps the Swift method names and calls a private RistNative object with external fun declarations and System.loadLibrary("rist").
NWEndpoint is replaced by RistEndpoint(host, port); NWInterface.InterfaceType is replaced by an android.net.NetworkCapabilities transport constant (Int?).

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback; because a Context is required, the file exposes a top level var ristApplicationContext that the Activity layer must set before starting a bonding stream.
Swift weak references (weak let stream, weak let ristDelegate) became plain strong references; Java GC handles the resulting cycles.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart and became a close() method that stops the connecting timer; stopInternal also calls close() on removed peers.

MpegTsWriterDelegate and RistSenderContextDelegate overrides keep the Swift parameter names; the exact Kotlin delegate signatures come from the ported Moblin interfaces in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg and are assumed to match.
SimpleTimer(ristScope), Atomic<Long>(0L), processorPipelineQueue.launch { } and BondingConnection(name:, usage:, rtt:) use the signatures of the ported types listed in the glossary.

NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket: connect, receive and send run in coroutines on the file-private connectionScope (Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob); srtlaClientQueue is still what the two SimpleTimer instances are built with.

NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart, so `type` is an Int? holding android.net.NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* values (null means relay/any), and NWParameters.requiredInterface is applied by creating the socket through Network.socketFactory.
Because android.net.Network exposes no interface name, the typeString lookup uses interface?.toString() as the key into SrtlaNetworkInterfaces.names.
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart: a private top-level ConnectionState enum (ready/failed) stands in for the handleStateUpdate(to:) parameter.
ContinuousClock instants become System.nanoTime(); getKeepAliveTime() and rtt stay millisecond based like the Swift code.

The Data helpers used by this file (getUInt32Be, setUInt32Be, getInt64Be, setInt64Be, randomData) are not part of the glossary, so they are declared as private top-level ByteArray extensions here, implemented with ByteBuffer and SecureRandom.
logger.* maps to android.util.Log with tag RemoteConnection; the weak delegate becomes a strong reference, and deinit is translated as an override of finalize().

sizeFormatter (com.moblin.android.common.various) is assumed to expose format(bytes: Long): String for ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount:), and outgoing packets are written under synchronized(socket) so they cannot interleave.

srtlaClientQueue is a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher: DispatchQueue.async becomes srtlaClientScope.launch and DispatchQueue.sync becomes runBlocking(srtlaClientQueue) (never call those two sync-based getters from the srtla dispatcher itself).

NWPathMonitor/NWPath are replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback plus a Network->transport map; no Context is available in this layer, so the ConnectivityManager must be published through the new top-level var srtlaConnectivityManager by the Activity (TODO until then).

NWEndpoint parameters are flattened into host: String + port: Int (addMoblink/removeMoblink/startRemote) and NWInterface becomes android.net.Network with its NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* constant as the interface type.
UInt16 ports became Int, UInt32 sequence numbers became UInt, and ContinuousClock/Duration became System.nanoTime() nanoseconds compared against 15_000_000L.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart, so the 'srtla deinit' debug log is dropped.
weak let delegate becomes a plain nullable reference (private val delegate: SrtlaDelegate?) since Kotlin has no weak properties.

State is redeclared here as a file-private enum, matching the Swift private enum; SrtlaDelegate's conforming members were moved into the class body because Kotlin interfaces cannot be implemented by extensions.

Sibling APIs are assumed to keep their Swift names: RemoteConnection.networkInterface/type(Int?)/register/setPriority/score/getDataSentDelta/stop(reason), LocalListener.onReady/onError/sendPacket, SimpleTimer-startSingleShot/stop, BondingConnection(name, usage, rtt) and the enum cases SettingsDnsLookupStrategy.ipv4/ipv6/ipv4AndIpv6/system, DnsLookupFamily.ipv4/ipv6/unspec, SettingsStreamSrtImplementation.moblin/official.
Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket/Socket; the accept loop and each connection read loop run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

HttpServer.queue is modelled as a CoroutineDispatcher and the class exposes an internal scope so HttpServerConnection can share it; SimpleTimer is assumed to be constructible as SimpleTimer(queue: CoroutineDispatcher).
NWEndpoint.Port becomes Int (default 80); the NWListener.State failure branch became handleStateUpdate(failed: Boolean) driving the same 1 second retry through retryTimer.
sendFileAndClose takes a java.io.File and streams it in 512 KiB blocking chunks (iterative loop) instead of the recursive NWConnection completion chain.

HttpServerConnection is internal instead of fileprivate because it appears in HttpServerResponse's internal constructor; HttpServerResponse.connection is a plain nullable reference (Kotlin has no weak properties).
HttpParser, declared in the same package, is assumed to be an open class exposing data: ByteArray, append(data: ByteArray) and getLine(data: ByteArray, offset: Int): Pair<String, Int>?.
Data.advanced(by:)/prefix become ByteArray.copyOfRange/copyOf; utf8Data becomes String.toByteArray().
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with a file level TAG constant because Kotlin has no per-class logger.
@MainActor protocol becomes a plain interface; SDK callbacks (webSocket*) are hopped onto Dispatchers.Main through mainScope so delegate calls stay on the main thread.
Swift 'private weak let delegate' has no Kotlin equivalent; it is a strong nullable property. Callers must drop their delegate reference explicitly to avoid leaking.
URL -> String (stored only). URL.isLoopback() is not in the glossary, so it is re-implemented here as a private String extension using java.net.URI.

Sealed cases of RemoteControlMessageToStreamer / RemoteControlRequest / RemoteControlResponse / RemoteControlEvent / RemoteControlMessageToAssistant are assumed to be named after the Swift cases with a capital first letter (Hello, Request, GetStatus, Response, ...) and their properties after the Swift labels.
RemoteControlResult is treated as an enum class whose entries keep the Swift case names (ok, wrongPassword, error) because the raw values are persisted.
Data -> ByteArray, base64EncodedString() -> android.util.Base64.encodeToString(..., Base64.NO_WRAP); Data.utf8Data -> String.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).
String(localized:) -> localized() imported from com.moblin.android; logger -> android.util.Log with the file-level TAG.
UUID().uuidString -> UUID.randomUUID().toString() (lowercase, the wire value is still a valid UUID).
The two URLSession.shared call sites now use the shared OkHttp client helper httpUrlSession(), imported from com.moblin.android.various.network.

The hand-written private httpClient val (the old stand-in for URLSession.shared) is no longer referenced and was removed, together with its okhttp3.OkHttpClient and java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit imports.
Both requests still run inside withContext(Dispatchers.IO) and keep the same headers, body and status checks as before.

App Attest has no Android counterpart, so attestedKey/generateAssertion/isAppAttestSupported keep their existing TODO-free stubs (isAppAttestSupported() is false) and sendLive returns early, exactly as in the current port.
apple_only: DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateKey/attestKey/isSupported (App Attest) - attestedKey() and sendLive() bodies are TODO()
DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion - generateAssertion() body is TODO()

notes: Added the TwitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreateEvent import in the twitch import block, after TwitchEventSubChannelRaidEvent.
Added the empty override twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate right after twitchEventSubChannelModerate, matching the Swift extension order.
Everything else in the file is untouched, including the hand-written WebSocket server, socket helpers and the RemoteControlWebSocket class.
RemoteControlWebDelegate becomes a Kotlin interface; the Swift `weak` delegate is stored as a plain nullable property because Kotlin has no weak references for interfaces.

Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection is replaced with java.net.ServerSocket plus a hand-rolled RFC6455 WebSocket handshake and frame codec running on Dispatchers.IO; callbacks are dispatched back on a Dispatchers.Main scope.
NWListener.State update handling is reduced to a private `handleWebsocketStateUpdate(failed: Boolean)` helper that drives the same 1s retry timer.
UInt16 ports become Int (ServerSocket takes Int); string interpolation on the port value is preserved in config.mjs.
URL return of `remoteControlWebGetRecordingUrl` maps to java.net.URI; `[[String: String]]` recordings map to List<Map<String, String>>.
JSONSerialization is replaced with org.json.JSONArray and logger.info with android.util.Log.i using the class name as tag.
Sealed-class case names are assumed as RemoteControlRequest.*, RemoteControlResponse.*, RemoteControlMessageToAssistant.* and RemoteControlEvent.* (PascalCase, matching the Swift case labels).
@MainActor isolation is not reproduced; blocking socket work runs on Dispatchers.IO and UI-visible callbacks run on Dispatchers.Main.
Model is declared in the same package, so this file holds top-level extension functions on Model; the Swift file-private `thumbStickDeadZone` became a private top-level `const val`.

GameController has no Android counterpart: GCController is replaced by android.view.InputDevice and the per-button `pressedChangedHandler` / `valueChangedHandler` wiring is gone because the Activity delivers KeyEvent/MotionEvent instead.
`handleGameControllerButton` and `handleGameControllerThumbStick` were private in Swift and are left public on purpose so the Activity layer can forward key and motion events into them.
`button.sfSymbolsName` is replaced by an explicit `buttonId: String` parameter; the Activity is expected to map KeyEvent key codes to the same ids stored in SettingsGameControllerButton.name.
`String(localized:)` became the top-level `localized()` function imported from com.moblin.android.
`Gimbal.shared?.animate(motion:)` keeps the `shared` accessor shape; the iOS 18 availability check is dropped since it does not exist on Android.
The `[weak self]` capture in the gimbal preset long-press timer is dropped; Kotlin lambdas capture strongly, so the timer must be stopped/removed to avoid retaining the Model.
SettingsQuickButtonType is not in the glossary and is assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.settings; fix the import if the port placed it elsewhere.

The two Swift `extension GoProDevice: ...Delegate` blocks become the class header conformance to CBCentralManagerDelegate/CBPeripheralDelegate with `override fun` members kept in the same order at the end of the body, since Kotlin cannot extend conformance from an extension.
The Swift tuple array `pendingWrites: [(characteristic: CBCharacteristic, packet: Data)]` is a private nested data class PendingWrite.
`[weak self]` is dropped from every MainTimer closure, as required for the hand-written shims.
`try? X(serializedBytes:)` becomes `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()`; an empty Source returns early exactly like the Swift guard.
The private `state` property keeps its name together with the Swift-named `getState()` / `setState(state:)` methods; Kotlin generates getState/setState accessors for that property.
ByteArray sizes/slices: `message.count` -> `size`, `Data(message.dropFirst(2))` -> `message.copyOfRange(2, message.size)`.

Message header bytes are compared as `message[0].toUByte()`/`message[1].toUByte()` so the UByte action/feature ids stay unsigned; `bitrate` stays `UInt` because goProSetLiveStreamModeMessage takes a UInt.
@MainActor is dropped: these Model extensions run on the main dispatcher like the rest of Model.
The three WatchConnectivity entry points keep their names but their bodies are TODO(...) because the WatchProtocol* payload types have no Android counterpart; their parameters are typed Any.
The scoreboard configs stay file-private top-level vals; configs is declared after the individual configs so top-level initialisation order matches Swift.
Swift switch expressions on scoreboard.sport become when(...) with an else branch, and if/guard let becomes a null check, ?.let or an early return.
clamped(to:) maps to coerceIn, Array.popLast()/removeLast() map to MutableList.removeLastOrNull()/removeLast(), count is read through List.size.

modular.layout and modular.clock.direction are compared against SettingsWidgetScoreboardLayout and SettingsWidgetGenericScoreboardClockDirection taken from the glossary; verify these are the enums used by SettingsWidgetModularScoreboard.
scoreChanges elements are translated as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScoreIncrement.home/.away, and padel/generic score entries as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScore().

modular.home.textColor.toHex() is kept as a member call on the color type of com.moblin.android.common.various, and modular.clock.format() is imported as the top-level extension format() from that package.
TeslaVehicle implements CBCentralManagerDelegate and CBPeripheralDelegate directly; the two Swift extensions became override members at the end of the class body.
responseHandlers is keyed by address.hexString() because ByteArray keys compare by identity.
The P256 public key DER-header extension became a companion invoke operator plus a toBytes() extension in this file.
Deque<Job> is ArrayDeque<Job>: append -> addLast, popFirst -> removeFirstOrNull, removeAll -> clear.
Data.random(length:) -> randomBytes() from com.moblin.android.various.utils; Data.random(length:) for uuid addresses too.
@MainActor and @available(iOS 17) have no Kotlin counterpart, so the auto-reconnect option is set unconditionally.
protobuf .init() assignments name the generated message type explicitly (CarServer_*), as the Kotlin setters need a value.
Log.i/Log.d use the TeslaVehicle tag in place of logger.info/logger.debug.
Data extension becomes an extension function on ByteArray in package com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension.
Data.subdata(in:) maps to ByteArray.copyOfRange(fromIndex, toIndex), which also copies into a new array just like subdata.
The Swift `offset ..< offset + thisChunkSize` range is translated to copyOfRange(offset, offset + thisChunkSize) because Kotlin's end index is exclusive.
The returned type is List<ByteArray> instead of [Data].
The Data-returning branch for count < size returns listOf(this), preserving the Swift behaviour of returning the receiver itself.
Declares no Kotlin types, only the top-level extension function chunks.
The CoreMedia import is unused in the Swift body and therefore has no Kotlin import.
No iOS-only API needed a TODO in this file.

AVFoundation's AVFrameRateRange has no Android counterpart, so this file declares a plain data class AVFrameRateRange with minFrameRate/maxFrameRate (Double) in the same package; the extension keeps the Swift member name contains(frameRate:).
Swift's range pattern operator ~= on a ClosedRange is translated to Kotlin's in operator on a ClosedFloatingPointRange, which is the direct equivalent.
Float64 maps to Double and the parameter name is kept as frameRate so both codebases read side by side.
No other call sites of contains(frameRate:) exist inside this file; consumers import this package's declaration.
No hardware, AudioToolbox, or VideoToolbox API is touched here, so no TODO() markers were needed.
AVCaptureDevice.Format has no Android class; it is modelled here as the plain data class AVCaptureDeviceFormat with the same property name videoSupportedFrameRateRanges.
AVFrameRateRange is modelled as a data class with minFrameRate/maxFrameRate and a contains(frameRate:) member, matching AVFrameRateRange semantics (inclusive bounds).
isFrameRateSupported keeps its Swift name and signature and contains the full pure logic port; only the loop style is idiomatic Kotlin with an early return.

CameraX/camera2 exposes frame-rate ranges as Range<Int> (camera2 CONTROL_AE_AVAILABLE_TARGET_FPS_RANGES, high-speed video fps ranges); the call site maps those into AVFrameRateRange entries, so no camera2 import is needed in this file.
No hardware call, no coroutine and no permission handling appears in this file, so nothing became a TODO().
Frame rates stay Double (Swift Float64).
No iOS-only framework call was dropped, so unsupported is empty.
CVPixelBuffer already declares width, height, size and isPortrait() in com.moblin.android.platform.video, so those four Swift extension members are not redeclared here; call the existing members.
colorAttachments is a top-level extension property on CVPixelBuffer that reads the attachments with CVBufferCopyAttachment(this, key) from com.moblin.android.platform.video.

kCVImageBufferColorPrimaries_ITU_R_709_2, kCVImageBufferTransferFunction_ITU_R_709_2, kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_601_4, kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_709_2, kCVImageBufferColorPrimaries_ITU_R_2020 and kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_2020 are used from com.moblin.android.platform.video next to the three key constants it already declares; they must exist there.
The Apple string values of the attachment constants are kept byte-identical, as they travel with the pixel buffer attachments.
sdrYCbCrMatrix returns a String in Kotlin; CFString has no Kotlin counterpart.
The three attachment maps are top-level read-only Map<String, String> values, exactly like the Swift globals.
Nothing in this file needs a TODO: every API used (CVPixelBuffer members, CVBufferCopyAttachment, the CoreVideo key constants) is declared by the hand-written platform layer.
No Kotlin types are declared by this file; it holds one extension property and top-level values and functions.
CMFormatDescription maps to android.media.MediaFormat, so the three members become top-level extension functions on MediaFormat in this package.
atoms() returns the sample-description atom map; on Android the codec-private data lives in the csd-0 ByteBuffer, so it is returned keyed by avcC/hvcC according to the MIME type.
extensions() mirrors CMFormatDescriptionGetExtensions; MediaFormat can only enumerate its keys from API 29, so on API 26-28 the body is TODO().
numberOfAudioChannels() reads MediaFormat.KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT instead of AudioStreamBasicDescription.mChannelsPerFrame.
Channel count is Int in Kotlin (UInt32 is reserved for wire-format byte parsing).
ByteArray replaces NSData/CFData and Map replaces NSDictionary/CFDictionary.
