peerConnected reports the stream's id, camera() name and latencySeconds() through the new connected signature.
UInt16 virtual destination ports stay Int in Kotlin, as in the rest of the port.
This file exists only for macCatalyst; Android has no status-item bridge, so the helper entry points keep their signatures with TODO() bodies.
The MoblinMac plugin types MacStatusItem and MacStatusItemDelegate have no counterpart and no glossary entry, so minimal Kotlin interfaces are declared in this file.
macStatusItem is a stored Model property in Swift (extensions cannot store properties); here it is a top-level extension property on Model backed by a WeakHashMap.
makeMacStatusItemStatusTitle() is translated in full because it only joins localized strings.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
logger.info maps to Log.i with the tag "Model".
The Swift #else branch (empty stubs) is represented by the same three function names; their bodies are TODO because the macCatalyst plugin bundle cannot be loaded on Android.
apple_only: NSBundle.main.builtInPlugInsURL / Bundle(url:) / principalClass plugin bundle loading (MoblinMac.bundle)
macCatalyst NSStatusItem bridge (MacStatusItem helper object)
UIImage(named:)?.pngData() icon encoding
MacStatusItemDelegate conformance declared from an extension

notes: ThermalStateView is a SwiftUI struct: it becomes a @Composable function with the same name, an extra trailing Modifier parameter and thermalState kept first.
Image(systemName: "flame") with .font(.system(size: 11)) and .foregroundStyle(...) is the platform SystemImage composable with fontSize = 11.sp and tint = thermalState.color().
ProcessInfo.ThermalState comes from com.moblin.android.platform.core and keeps its Swift case names (nominal, fair, serious, critical).
thermalState.color() is the existing Kotlin extension fun ProcessInfo.ThermalState.color(): Color; it is imported from the same com.moblin.android.common.view package as this view.
compactAudioLevelColors returns Pair<Color, Color> because Kotlin has no tuples; callers use .first/.second (Swift callers destructure the tuple).
Image(systemName:) is resolved by the private helper compactAudioLevelIcon, mapping the SF Symbol speaker/mic names to Material Icons.Filled.VolumeUp/VolumeDown/VolumeOff/VolumeMute.
.foregroundStyle(foregroundColor) becomes the Icon tint parameter.
.font(smallFont) has no effect on a Material Icon, which is sized purely by Modifier.size(17.dp); it is therefore not applied.
.contentShape(Rectangle()) only widens the hit-test region and has no Compose counterpart; it is dropped (no gesture is attached in this file).
.padding(20) followed by .padding(-20) only expands the tap area in SwiftUI; Compose rejects negative padding, so both are dropped and the wrapped layout is unchanged.
clippingThresholdDb/redThresholdDb/yellowThresholdDb/zeroThresholdDb/defaultAudioLevel stay top-level Float vals in the same package so other files keep the same names.
The composable parameter backgroundColor intentionally shadows the package-level backgroundColor color, exactly as in the Swift struct.
Enum cases beforeIcon/afterIcon/hide became PascalCase entries BeforeIcon/AfterIcon/Hide; comparison kept identical.
The row is Compose Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp)) with vertical centering, matching HStack(spacing: 1).
Image(systemName: icon) uses a dynamic SF Symbol name, so there is no Material icon to substitute; the painter is TODO() and listed as unsupported.
.font(smallFont) applied to StreamOverlayTextView is passed as the child composable's style parameter; smallFont is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
color has default Color.White and iconBackgroundColor defaults to the imported top-level backgroundColor val from com.moblin.android.common.various.

Icon sizing chain maps to Modifier.size(17.dp, 17.dp).padding(horizontal = 2.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).background(iconBackgroundColor) so the background is clipped like Swift's .cornerRadius(5).
Swift's .contentShape(Rectangle()) plus .padding(-20) hit-area expansion has no Compose counterpart (negative padding is not supported); it is left as TODO().
enum case names differ in casing only, so the Swift and Kotlin sources can still be read side by side.

The four private enums with associated values (PublishMessage, SubscribeTopic, Message, MessageToMoblin, MessageToBrowser) became private sealed classes with hand-written JsonObject encode/decode that match Swift's synthesized Codable shape ({"caseName":{...}}, optional associated values omitted).
ChatPostSegment/ChatPostUrl are encoded by hand into id/text/url/bigGifUrl (url: {moving, still}) instead of relying on a serializer, because their Kotlin ports are not shown as @Serializable.
JSON is parsed and printed with codableJson; MessageToBrowser.toJson returns null when encoding fails, like Swift's try?.
moblinScript() calls loadStringResource("moblin", "js") from com.moblin.android.various.utils in place of Bundle.main url+Data.
NSObject, weak and @MainActor are dropped; the delegate is a plain nullable property.
DispatchQueue.main.async became CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch.
logger.info/debug became Log.i/Log.d with the tag "BrowserEffectServer".
The class implements WKScriptMessageHandler in its header (the Swift extension) and is open with open members because the Swift class is not final.
ChatLineContent gains `var font: SettingsFont = SettingsFont()` at the same position as the Swift property.
New private makeBaseFont(content, bold) builds the Typeface from content.font.family / content.font.name(), falling back to the design family and weight.
makeFont now calls makeBaseFont, then adds ITALIC and (bold && family != nil || italic) BOLD via Typeface.create(base, style), mirroring the SymbolicTraits logic.
makeLayout now sets basePaint.typeface from makeBaseFont(content = content) instead of the hard-coded default Typeface.
Typeface carries no size on Android, so the font size stays on the paint (textSize = content.fontSize), as in the rest of this port.
UIFont(name:size:) returning nil has no direct equivalent; Typeface.create(name, style) falls back to the default typeface instead, so the two branches of makeBaseFont both produce a Typeface.
SettingsFont is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; `family` and `name()` keep their Swift names.
No Apple framework API is newly introduced by this change.
CMTime is ported to Long microseconds: `.invalid` becomes the sentinel Long.MIN_VALUE and `.zero` becomes 0L.

AVAudioPCMBuffer is replaced by the new PcmBuffer type (ByteArray + frameLength) because the original does raw memcpy of int16/int32/float32 samples, interleaved or planar; ShortArray alone could not express all three sample formats.
The AVAudioFormat stored in `format` is replaced by the new PcmAudioFormat type which carries sampleRate, channels, isInterleaved and commonFormat plus derived bytesPerSample/bytesPerFrame.
AudioStreamBasicDescription/`kAudioFormatLinearPCM` become android.media.MediaFormat with KEY_PCM_ENCODING; the guard still returns null for non 16-bit linear PCM.
AudioEncoder.makeAudioFormat is expected to exist in this package and to return PcmAudioFormat? for a MediaFormat argument.
Swift `init?` becomes a companion `operator fun invoke` returning AudioEncoderRingBuffer?, with the primary constructor kept private.
`defer` inside createOutputBuffer is translated by capturing the tuple first, then resetting latestPresentationTimeStamp/outputIndex before returning.

Added the new top-level createColorProperties(colorAttachments) helper right after createDataRateLimits, translating the optional lookups with ?.let and NSMutableArray-style append calls.

The per-format constants kCVImageBufferColorPrimaries_ITU_R_2020, kCVImageBufferTransferFunction_ITU_R_2100_HLG and kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_2020 stay declared in this file because other files use them.

The Swift file is wrapped in #if targetEnvironment(macCatalyst); the whole capture pipeline is Apple-only, so the three ScreenCaptureKit call sites are TODO() while the rest of the structure (delegate, latency constant, sample-buffer rewriting) is translated.
SCStream has no Kotlin type, so the private 'stream' property is kept as an Any? placeholder.
makeContentFilter returned (SCContentFilter, SCDisplay); those types do not exist here, so it returns Pair<Any, Any> with a TODO body.
CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample; presentationTimeStamp (CMTime) -> presentationTimeUs (Long microseconds) and the 0.15 s latency becomes +150000 us.
sampleBuffer.imageBuffer != nil is mapped to MediaSample.data.isNotEmpty(), because MediaSample carries the pixels in data.
weak var delegate has no Kotlin equivalent; it is kept as a plain nullable reference (strong).
logger.info is translated to Log.i with tag "MacScreenCapture"; the start log cannot reproduce the SCStream width/height pixels, so it logs the filter/display/scale instead.
TODO() throws NotImplementedError (not an Exception), so startInternal/stopInternal short-circuit before the delegate callbacks run; the TS-adjustment callback logic is still fully translated.
apple_only: no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream.stopCapture
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCShareableContent

notes: CMSampleBuffer maps to MediaSample, so every presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 and CMTime is kept as Long microseconds (deltaLimit arithmetic unchanged).

CMSampleBuffer.numSamples has no MediaSample counterpart, so frameLength is TODO(); startOutput, makePresentationTimeStamp and the whole periodic output path depend on it being supplied by the platform capture side.
formatDescription.audioStreamBasicDescription?.mSampleRate maps to MediaSample.format (android.media.MediaFormat) + KEY_SAMPLE_RATE; sampleRate is only touched when a format is present, as in Swift.

CMSampleBuffer.replacePresentationTimeStamp is emulated by building a new MediaSample with the same data/isKeyFrame/format and the corrected presentationTimeUs (MediaSample is assumed to have those constructor parameters).
CMBlockBuffer data pointer zeroing becomes latest.data.fill(0) because MediaSample.data is a mutable ByteArray.
consumeBuffer's inout Int parameter becomes a returned Int (Kotlin has no inout); the call sites assign the result.

Assumes the ported SimpleTimer takes the queue in its constructor and exposes startPeriodic(interval, initial) { } and stop(), that DriftTrackerMedia's entry is Audio and DriftTracker.update/addMedia keep the Swift parameter order, and that currentPresentationTimeStamp() returns microseconds.
logger.info/debug become android.util.Log with tag "BufferedAudio"; logger.debugEnabled becomes Log.isLoggable(tag, Log.DEBUG).
Deque<CMSampleBuffer> became kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<MediaSample>; CMTime comparisons use presentationTimeUs and 'seconds' became presentationTimeSeconds (presentationTimeUs / 1e6).
The Swift 'weak let processor' is stored as a plain nullable reference because Kotlin has no weak stored properties; a WeakReference would have changed every call site.
deinit has no JVM counterpart, so it is exposed as close() and must be called by the owner when the BufferedVideo is discarded.
logger.debugEnabled maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG) and the stats.getStats() call stays inside that guard so its short-circuit side effects match Swift exactly.
Assumes DriftTrackerMedia.Video and BufferedStats.getStats() returning Pair<Int, Int>? so the Swift tuple destructuring still compiles; adjust if the sibling Kotlin files name these differently.
replacePresentationTimeStamp is provided as a file-private MediaSample extension using copy(); if the sibling file declares the same helper, delete this one.
The inout 'numberOfBuffersConsumed' parameter of consumeBuffer became a returned Int because Kotlin has no inout.
processor.delegate is reached with safe calls (processor?.delegate?.streamVideoBufferedVideoReady/Removed) to avoid depending on its nullability.
Added the colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange constructor parameter after softwareDecoding and forwarded it to WebrtcIngestClient, matching the Swift diff.
SettingsStreamColorRange is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.

The dependency declaration listed for WebrtcIngestClient does not yet show a colorRange parameter; the call follows the Swift change, so WebrtcIngestClient's constructor must expose colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange.
Everything else in the file (delegate interface, handleOffer, stop and the delegate overrides) is unchanged.

catPrinterDispatchQueue is a single-thread Executors dispatcher; every `DispatchQueue.async { }` became `CoroutineScope(catPrinterDispatchQueue).launch { }` and the same dispatcher is passed to SimpleTimer and to CBCentralManager through a wrapping CoroutineScope.
The stored central manager uses `by CBCentralManager.holder()`, so assigning null in reset() releases the manager and stops scanning like ARC on iOS.

CatPrinter.getState() is annotated @JvmName("currentState") because the private `state` property's generated getter would otherwise clash with it; CurrentJob.setState keeps @JvmName("updateState") as the existing port does.
Swift `throw "text"` became `throw CatPrinterError(message)`, a private exception whose toString() is the message, so the logged text matches the iOS log.

CFDataGetLength/CFDataGetBytePtr are gone: CGDataProvider.data already returns the ByteArray, so only the "Failed to get length" guard was dropped; bitsPerComponent/bitsPerPixel/dataProvider come from the CoreGraphics shims and the UInt8 comparisons use `and 0xFF`.
Deque<PrintJob> became MutableList with removeFirstOrNull(), and Data slices use copyOfRange(offset, min(offset + mtu, size)).
AtkinsonDithering takes MutableList<UByteArray> while FloydSteinbergDithering takes List<List<UByte>>, so pixels are converted with toList()/toUByteArray() when the floydSteinberg algorithm is used.
catPrinterEncodeImageRow takes a UByteArray row, matching the row type of catPrinterPackPrintImageCommands(image: List<UByteArray>).
startRunning now resets oldBitrateVideoSize to a zero Size, matching the new Swift line CMVideoDimensions(width: 0, height: 0).
CMVideoDimensions maps to android.util.Size in this port, so the reset is Size(0, 0), the same value used for the oldBitrateVideoSize field initialiser.
Everything else in the file is unchanged; the Android-specific launch/atomic/lockQueue handling and the Size-based adaptive resolution logic are preserved byte-identically.
No SwiftUI views are declared here; the file only provides data models and a formatter, so no @Composable functions were added.
Swift UInt64 usage/percentage values are mapped to Long, matching the Android side which does not use unsigned types for these counters.
The Swift tuple return of format(_:) becomes Triple<String, String, List<BondingPercentage>>; callers read .first/.second/.third.
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; BondingPercentage keeps its id property for LazyColumn keys.
RgbColor(red:green:blue:).color() is assumed to exist as a member call on RgbColor from com.moblin.android.common.various with Int red/green/blue arguments.
The file-private top-level `colors` array keeps its name and file-privacy; nothing outside this file can see it.
getNameColor uses indexOfFirst (-1 when absent) instead of Optional firstIndex, preserving the same colour selection order (Cellular, WiFi, then interface names offset by 2).
percentages is a MutableList so the last entry's usage can be normalised to 100 minus the sum of the earlier entries, exactly as in Swift.
RtmpServer gains the colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange property, constructor parameter and init assignment exactly as the Swift diff adds them.
colorRange is forwarded to RtmpServerClient in handleNewListenerConnection; RtmpServerClient's constructor must accept that fourth parameter.
Everything else, including the ServerSocket-based listener, SimpleTimer periodic work and Atomic<BitrateStats> usage, stays byte-identical to the previous Kotlin revision.
Swift positionPort .init(rawValue:) with a fallback is already handled by the port range check plus DefaultTcpPorts.rtmpServer fallback; unchanged.
Only the scopes list changed: 'moderator:manage:shoutouts' added after 'moderator:manage:announcements'.
All other declarations remain byte-identical to the previous Kotlin translation, including the hand-written WebView and Keychain platform code.
The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package, so the two files can be read side by side.
`database.appMode == .chatPhone` assumes the port keeps an enum `AppMode` in this package with a `chatPhone` entry; `AppMode` is not declared here and must already exist.
AVAudioPlayer is replaced with android.media.MediaPlayer: numberOfLoops = -1 becomes isLooping = true and play() becomes start().
The member `chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer` is assumed to be declared in the Model file as `var chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer: MediaPlayer? = null`.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) for the Alerts.bundle subdirectory has no direct Android equivalent, so only the asset resolution plus MediaPlayer construction is deferred with TODO().
`resetSelectedScene(changeScene: false)` is called with a Kotlin named argument; the parameter name must be `changeScene` in the Model file.
The long Swift switch lists every SettingsQuickButtonType case explicitly, all returning false, with `default` returning true; the Kotlin `when` mirrors this with `else -> true`.
No new types are declared by this file; it only adds extension functions to Model.
Only the `#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)` branch is translated; the empty `#else` extension is dropped and no other Android API replaces it.
Swift's nested `LiveActivityAttributes.ContentState` stays nested in Kotlin.

`Activity<LiveActivityAttributes>.activities` becomes `Activity.activities<LiveActivityAttributes>()`; the stored `liveActivity` property keeps its `Activity<LiveActivityAttributes>?` type and is assumed declared on Model.
`logger.info` becomes `android.util.Log.i` with the class name "Model" as tag.
`String(localized:)` becomes the top-level `localized()` from com.moblin.android.
`stopLiveActivity` replaces the dispatch semaphore over a global queue with `runBlocking { }` around `end`, as the shim prescribes.
`updateLiveActivity`'s `Task { await ... }` body is run with `runBlocking`; the shim's `update` never suspends and needs no main thread.
`functions.prefix(2)` becomes `functions.take(2)` and the state carries a `List<LiveActionFunction>` instead of a Swift Array.
Despite the ui tier, this file declares no SwiftUI views; it is a Model extension with control bar background image helpers, so no @Composable functions are produced.
UIImage is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap and UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing is replaced with android.graphics.Canvas plus android.graphics.Matrix.

URL.documentsDirectory has no equivalent without a Context: a top-level lateinit appContext must be assigned the application context at app startup, and controlBarBackgroundImagePath is derived from appContext.filesDir.
FileManager.removeItem is File.delete and Swift's try? becomes runCatching, matching the silent failure behaviour.
The crop factors (backgroundImageCropX/Y/Width/Height) and backgroundImageOpacity are treated as Float, since CGFloat maps to Float.
image.jpegData(compressionQuality: 0.9) becomes Bitmap.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, 90, ...).
BitmapFactory returns null on undecodable data, mirroring the optional returned by UIImage(data:).
Crop + scale rendering keeps the same order as Swift: scale by min(1, 1024 / max(width, height)) and translate by -x*scale, -y*scale.

`getRistStream(virtualDestinationPort:)` is deleted; `isRistStreamConnected(port: Int)` and the two id-based lookups stay unchanged.

`updateRistMics()` is a Model extension in the same package and is called directly from `updateRistVideoSourcesAndMics()`.
This file is a networking layer despite being flagged ui tier, so there are no Compose views; the translation is a plain Kotlin/Swift-parallel API client.

Everything else in the file is unchanged from the previous Kotlin translation, including the ModelRtspClientDelegate that replaces the Swift extension conformance to RtspClientDelegate.
Added the colorRange constructor parameter and passed it to SrtServerClient, matching the Swift diff.
Imported SettingsStreamColorRange from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
All other lines, including the existing Android-specific sockaddrIn/SrtError/mutate hooks, are unchanged.
Added the new colorRange constructor parameter between softwareDecoding and iceServers, matching the Swift init order.
Added the import for SettingsStreamColorRange from com.moblin.android.various.settings.

All other declarations, imports and bodies are unchanged from the current Kotlin file.
Added the new setPhotosImageQuality() call in Model.importSucceeded, right after setExternalCameraVideoRange() as in the Swift diff.
Everything else in the Kotlin file is unchanged, including the hand-written Context-taking clipboard and data-import helpers.

localized(...) keeps the same format strings, including the interpolated user name variants.

isSrtClientStreamConnected(id:) was removed from the Swift file and is removed from the Kotlin file as well.

`images: Deque<VideoImage>` (swift-collections) maps to `ArrayDeque<VideoImage>`; `images += newImages` becomes `images.addAll(newImages)` and `images.count` becomes `images.size`.
`AVAssetReaderTrackOutput.copyNextSampleBuffer()` blocks and stays on the reader's own (lock) queue, never on processorPipelineQueue.

`try? AVAssetReader(asset:)` becomes `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()`; the `guard let trackOutput` after construction is kept as a local nullable read.

Pixel buffer output settings use the Map<String, Any> form with the kCVPixelBuffer* keys from com.moblin.android.platform.video.
BeautyEffect is a final Swift class, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class; @unchecked Sendable is dropped.
framesPerFade keeps the Swift declaration order: the stored default 30f plus an init block that assigns 15f * (fps / 30f).
setSmoothnessSettings/setShapeSettings keep the processorPipelineQueue hop, written as processorPipelineQueue.launch { } since the scope is already a CoroutineScope.
VideoEffectDetectionsMode cases are referenced as the nested members VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Now(null) and VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Off, matching the sealed class declared in VideoEffect.kt.
In executeMetalPetal the Swift local `var image` shadows the parameter; Kotlin forbids that, so the running value is named `result` and the parameter keeps its name.

Adds the new colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange constructor property, placed after softwareDecoding and before targetLatency like the Swift source.
handleVideoFormatDescription now passes colorRange as the fourth argument of VideoDecoder, following the Swift diff that threads the color range into the video decoder.

The existing hand-written stop() cleanup, invalidPresentationTimeUs sentinel helpers, MediaSample/AVAudioConverter usage and log tags are kept byte-identical.

Dewarp360Filter and graphicsEpsilon are in the same package and need no import.

final class CameraManEffect : VideoEffect gets a primary constructor; moveVertically, speed and alwaysMove are private var constructor properties.
highQualityDownsampling is referenced from the ported VideoEffect base class exactly as in Swift; it is not part of the declaration excerpt given in the request.

VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so Swift's .seconds is divided by 1_000_000.0 at both call sites.
calcCropRegion keeps the stateful isStill / previousScale / previousIsRising logic; isStill.toggle() becomes isStill = !isStill.

CIFilter.colorMatrix() returns the CIColorMatrix shim, whose aVector is a CIVector and inputImage a CIImage?.

SIMD4<Float>(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75 becomes SIMD4(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75f using the platform.simd SIMD4 Number constructor and Float times operator.
simd_float4x4(columns: (...)) becomes simd_float4x4(columns = listOf(...)) with the four SIMD4 columns in Swift order.
SWIFT final class GrayScaleEffect: VideoEffect becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open VideoEffect, since a final Swift class has no open members.

PinchEffect is a final Swift class extending VideoEffect, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open class VideoEffect.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.async; translated to processorPipelineQueue.launch from kotlinx.coroutines.

pixellateCalcScale keeps Swift's Float arithmetic; 20/1920/5/1 literals become 20f/1920f/5f/1f and size.maximum() is a CGSize member returning Double, narrowed with toFloat().
