The Toggle/onChange body is untouched: the fixed-horizon write and model.sceneUpdated() call stay byte-identical.
@Published properties became private MutableStateFlow backing fields exposed as public StateFlow via asStateFlow().

Swift's hand-written Codable encode(to:)/init(from:) flatten functionData into top-level keys; reproduced with hand-written KSerializer objects (SettingsStreamDeckKeySerializer, SettingsStreamDeckLayoutSerializer, SettingsStreamDecksSerializer) attached via @Serializable(with = ...).
UUIDs are persisted as strings (UUID.toString() / UUID.fromString) because java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx serializer here.
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart; id is exposed as a plain java.util.UUID property instead.
SettingsStreamDeckLayout conforms to Named; assumed com.moblin.android.various.utils.Named declares 'val name: StateFlow<String>' so the flow-backed property can override it.
Assumes RgbColor, SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion are @Serializable in their own packages and expose .serializer().
SettingsControllerFunctionData is treated as a mutable class instantiated with SettingsControllerFunctionData().
toString() on SettingsStreamDeckModel is an override of Any.toString() to keep the Swift function name.
Picker with .pickerStyle(.inline) is rendered as a LazyColumn of clickable rows with a RadioButton, one per database.streams entry.
Assumes each stream exposes `id` (matching Model.currentStreamId) and `name`; adjust if the Kotlin settings model names them differently.
onChange(of: model.currentStreamId) is translated to LaunchedEffect(currentStreamId) with a first-composition guard, because LaunchedEffect also runs on entry while Swift onChange does not.
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) becomes delay(3000) inside the LaunchedEffect coroutine, which already runs on the main dispatcher.

Writing the picked stream requires Model.currentStreamId to be assignable from outside (e.g. a var backed by a MutableStateFlow); if the port exposes only a read-only StateFlow, route the write through the model's setter.
.navigationTitle("Switch stream") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
The Section footer text becomes a trailing item in the LazyColumn.
pickerStyle(.inline) and labelsHidden() have no direct Compose equivalent and are dropped.
Only the onChange callback changed: model.reattachCamera() is now model.attachCamera(); everything else stays byte-identical.
The CallbackSignatureStateManager, the Row/Switch layout and the database write are untouched.
The SwiftUI View body became a @Composable named TapScreenToFocusSettingsView taking the model and database objects as parameters.
@ObservedObject database reads database.tapToFocus via collectAsState() on its StateFlow.

The @Binding write $database.tapToFocus is expressed as database.tapToFocus.value = value, which assumes Database exposes tapToFocus as a MutableStateFlow; swap in the ported setter if Database only exposes a read-only StateFlow.
onChange(of: database.tapToFocus) became LaunchedEffect(tapToFocus), which also fires on first composition, so model.setAutoFocus() can run once at startup when the toggle is already off.
Toggle became a Row containing a Text label with weight(1f) and a Material 3 Switch, matching the platform settings-row layout.
The toggle title goes through the top-level localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
No navigation, sheet, alert or toolbar is used in this file.
scanner.discoveredPeripherals is a MutableStateFlow, read with collectAsState; the filtered/mapped InlinePickerItem list is rebuilt on each recomposition.
Swift localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("black shark") becomes contains("black shark", ignoreCase = true).
ProgressView() has no iOS shim, so the standard CircularProgressIndicator is used inside HCenter.
@State selectedId is never read in the Swift body; it stays as a required parameter so call sites keep working.
.navigationTitle("Device") is folded into Form(title = "Device"), which supplies the navigation stack.
The List wrapping the ForEach inside the Section is dropped; its rows are rows of the Section.
onAppear/onDisappear become a DisposableEffect(Unit) that starts and stops the BLE scan.
model.bluetoothAllowed is collected as state so the body recomposes when the Bluetooth permission changes.
layoutScale and the private layoutOffset helper are added; layoutPosition and move are rebuilt on top of layoutOffset.
metalPetalLayerPosition is renamed to layoutCenter (layoutPosition + half size) and its old body is dropped.
moveComposited, resizeMirrorMoveComposited and composited now take WidgetShape/WidgetShapePlacement from the same package instead of MetalPetalWidgetShape.

composited gained the resize parameter and reads placement.center/placement.size/placement.borderSize/placement.borderWidth; the border layer wraps cornerRadius/borderColor in MTICornerRadius/MTIColor.
shape.rotationRadians() is converted with .toFloat() and shape.borderColor components with .toFloat() for the Float MTIColor constructor, matching Swift's Float(...) casts.
move now uses alignment.mirrorPositionVertically() and alignment.mirrorPositionHorizontally() instead of the old isTop()/else branch logic.
resizeMirror computes a single layoutScale and scales by (mirror ? -scale : scale, scale).
Imports MTIColor and MTICornerRadius added; shape.placement and shape.cornerRadiusPixels are called positionally because WidgetShape lives in another file of this package.
Form/List become a single LazyColumn; the outer Section has no header so no header Text is emitted.
.navigationTitle("Streams") is rendered as a Material 3 Scaffold TopAppBar; remove the Scaffold if the caller already provides one.

deepLinkCreator.streams is collected with collectAsState() to replace @ObservedObject, and mutations assume DeepLinkCreator exposes it as a public MutableStateFlow<List<DeepLinkCreatorStream>> (assign via .value).
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart; long-press (combinedClickable) on a row opens an AlertDialog that deletes the stream.
onMove (List reordering) has no Compose equivalent without an extra library, so reordering is not implemented; onDelete behaviour is covered by the delete dialog.
CreateButtonView is used with a trailing lambda, matching a Composable that takes an onClick as its last parameter.
All user-facing strings go through localized() from package com.moblin.android.
makeUniqueName and DeepLinkCreatorStream.baseName are called positionally because their Kotlin parameter names are defined in other packages.
ThermalState replaces ProcessInfo.ThermalState with PowerManager thermal status constants (API 29 values, inlined ints); read the live value with PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus() on API 29+.
Enum entries are upper case in Kotlin (NOMINAL, FAIR, SERIOUS, CRITICAL); raw values 0-3 are persisted byte-identically via ThermalStateSerializer.

StreamingHistoryDatabase's @Published properties are public MutableStateFlow fields (totalTime, totalBytes, totalStreams, streams) so append() and migrateFromOlderVersions() keep the Swift member shapes; collect them from Compose.

The database itself is serialized through the private StreamingHistoryDatabaseSnapshot class because kotlinx.serialization cannot serialize MutableStateFlow; totalTime is stored as milliseconds and missing keys fall back to the Swift defaults.
UUID and Instant get explicit KSerializers (UuidSerializer, InstantSerializer) as kotlinx.serialization has no built-in ones in the default module.
UInt64 counters (totalBytes, totalStreams) and Int64 highestBitrate became Long; Int64.min stays Long.MIN_VALUE.
Swift's toString() became override fun toString(): String (it overrides Any.toString); fromString() keeps throwing behaviour by letting SerializationException propagate.
logger.info is android.util.Log.i with tag "StreamingHistory".

The Swift change replaces `@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` with `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin `model: Model = LocalModel.current` default is dropped and `model: Model` becomes a required parameter.
The now unused `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import is removed together with the default value.
The rest of the file is unchanged: Form title, the empty-state Text, the ForEach with onDelete and the ContextMenuDeleteButton wrapper all stay byte-identical.
deleteNetworkInterface keeps its Kotlin shape with a Model parameter, matching model.networkInterfaceNamesUpdated().
Swift struct ExportSettingsView: View becomes a @Composable function taking model, defaulted from LocalModel.
@State URL? becomes remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }; the URL is carried as a String file path.
.onAppear is translated to DisposableEffect(Unit) calling model.exportToFile, with an empty onDispose.
ShareLink(item:label:) maps to the platform ShareLink composable, which shares a file path String as the file.
ProgressView() becomes CircularProgressIndicator with 20.dp size, formPalette().secondaryLabel colour and 2.dp stroke, matching the port's convention.
The HCenter wrapper from com.moblin.android.view.utils replaces the SwiftUI HCenter.
The result of the export callback is read back through the state, exactly like the Swift closure assigning to url.
catPrinterScanner is a shared scanner, so discoveredPeripherals is collected with collectAsState and read inside the Form body.
model.bluetoothAllowed is treated as a MutableStateFlow on the Model port and collected; change to a plain read if the port exposes it as a Boolean.
ProgressView has no shim in com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui, so HCenter holds a CircularProgressIndicator sized to 20.dp with explicit color and stroke width.
The iOS List inside the Section is dropped: the mapped InlinePickerItems are rendered with forEach and key(item.id) directly as rows of the Section.
peripheral.identifier.uuidString becomes peripheral.identifier.toString(), and the missing name falls back to localized("Unknown").
onAppear/onDisappear start and stop the scan in a DisposableEffect(Unit) with onDispose, so the scan is stopped when the view leaves composition.
Form(title = "Device") carries the Swift .navigationTitle and provides the NavigationStack; no Scaffold or TopAppBar is emitted.
selectedId stays a required parameter although the Swift body never reads it, matching the Swift struct's memberwise initializer.
Private helper views HeaderCellView and CellView become private @Composable functions; extra files keep the same names.
UIImage/SwiftUI Rectangle().stroke overlay is drawn with Modifier.border(0.5.dp), and the Swift modifier order is reversed when building the Compose modifier chain.
.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5 * scale)) becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape((5 * scale).dp)).
.foregroundStyle(textColor) has no equivalent environment here, so textColor is passed explicitly to every cell composable.
.minimumScaleFactor(0.5) is implemented by ScorecardShrinkText, which lowers the font size in onTextLayout while hasVisualOverflow, down to half the base size.
ForEach over 0 ..< numberOfHoles becomes a plain for loop; ForEach(golf.players) becomes players.forEach with key(player.id).
The .background modifier applied to a ForEach groups the player rows inside one Column with that background, as SwiftUI does.
The scorecardFontSize text sizes are scaled by `scale` and passed to SwiftUIFonts.system so the rendered scoreboard image matches iOS.
Model and DjiDeviceScanner are treated as state holders, so bluetoothAllowed and discoveredDevices are read with collectAsState().
The Swift singleton `.shared` on DjiDeviceScanner is assumed to be a Kotlin `object`, hence the default value `DjiDeviceScanner = DjiDeviceScanner` on the parameter.
@Environment(\.dismiss) has no Compose counterpart, so the view takes an explicit `onDismiss: () -> Unit` callback.
The nested List/ForEach is flattened into the single outer LazyColumn so there is no nested vertical scrolling.
The Section footer Text becomes a trailing item of the LazyColumn.
onChange and selectedId stay parameters; selectedId is part of the caller contract but is not read by the body, exactly as in the Swift source.
.navigationTitle("Device") is rendered as the title of a Scaffold TopAppBar, hence the @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).
DjiDiscoveredDevice property accesses (peripheral.identifier.uuidString, peripheral.name) are kept name-for-name from Swift since the Kotlin model is not defined in this file.
SettingsSaveView is translated to a single @Composable function of the same name taking the Model as a parameter.
Swift's @State showSaved becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) } with delegate read/write.
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) becomes a LaunchedEffect(showSaved) that delays 3000 ms and resets the flag.
model.storeSettings() is invoked inside a rememberCoroutineScope().launch block so the call compiles whether or not the Kotlin port makes it a suspend function.
HCenter from com.moblin.android.view.utils is used as the Compose centering wrapper around the content.
Button label and Text content keep the exact Swift strings, including the emoji.
Swift `@EnvironmentObject var model` became `let model`, so the Kotlin parameter lost its `LocalModel.current` default and is now passed in explicitly.
The now-unused `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import was removed with the environment object.
The Swift `HCenter { Button(...) }` remains the platform `FormButton(centered = true)`, which is the hand-written Android equivalent; unchanged by this diff.
`confirmationDialog` stays the platform `ConfirmationDialog` with `titleVisibility = Visibility.visible` and a destructive action Button.

ControllerThumbStickView: @Binding function becomes a value parameter plus an onFunctionChange lambda; the SwiftUI Picker + Section + ForEach is rendered as a Row with an ExposedDropdownMenuBox and the section header is dropped.
SettingsControllerThumbStickFunction.allCases maps to the Kotlin enum 'entries' property.
function.toString() uses the Kotlin enum toString(); Swift's toString() extension returned a localized display name, so swap in a localized label helper if the UI must stay localized.

function.color() is assumed to be an extension function color() on SettingsControllerThumbStickFunction returning androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color, imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
NavigationLink is replaced by the onNavigate("Thumb stick") callback; the destination Form (with its navigationTitle) belongs to the navigation host, not this file.
name is a LocalizedStringKey in Swift, so it is passed through localized(); pass an already-localized plain String instead if callers resolve it themselves.
The Label's SF Symbol icon (a runtime image name) has no direct Compose ImageVector mapping, so the Icon slot is TODO.
The whole row is made clickable with Modifier.clickable to reproduce the NavigationLink tappable label.
SwiftUI Form/Section are rendered as a scrollable Column with a header Text, and .navigationTitle becomes a Scaffold TopAppBar title.
@ObservedObject database becomes a plain parameter; its StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().
Assumed the port exposes Database.streamButtonColor (hex String) and Database.streamButtonColorColor (Color) as MutableStateFlow fields, written through .value.
Assumed the util composables exist as RgbColorPickerView(title, color: Color, onChange: (String) -> Unit) and TextButtonView(text, onClick).
The color() converter used on the stored color value is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; adjust the import if the port defines the extension elsewhere.
String(localized:) calls map to localized() from package com.moblin.android.
The picker callback keeps the Swift behaviour of only updating streamButtonColor; streamButtonColorColor is refreshed only by Reset.

SettingsFilePickerView no longer injects its model from LocalModel: the Swift @EnvironmentObject became a plain `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin parameter drops its LocalModel.current default and is passed in explicitly.
The sheet call site already passed the model, so it is unchanged.
LocalModel is still imported because ImportSettingsView keeps it as its own default model.
The SwiftUI Section wrapper has no Compose counterpart here, so its single child (TextEditNavigationView) is emitted directly at the top level of the composable.
@ObservedObject anamorphicLens is a parameter whose published `scale` is read with collectAsState(); the handler writes back through the same MutableStateFlow with `.value =`.
Private View methods updateWidget, changeScale and submitScale became private top-level functions so the composable keeps the SwiftUI name and signature shape.
The Swift `valueFormat: { "\($0)x" }` closure maps to the `valueFormat` lambda parameter of TextEditNavigationView and appends the literal 'x'.
Double(String) returning nil maps to String.toDoubleOrNull(); the three guard error strings keep the exact localized keys 'Not a number', 'Too small', 'Too big'.
String(localized:) calls become the shared localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
widget.setSettings(settings: anamorphicLens.clone()) keeps the clone/setSettings pattern from the Swift source.
Swift changed `@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` to a plain `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin parameter loses its `LocalModel.current` default and is now always supplied by the caller.
The `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import is removed because nothing else in the file uses it; every other line stays byte-identical.
`httpProxy` is a settings class read directly (no collectAsState) and read through `collectAsState` here for `port`, `enabled` and `localNetwork`, which are MutableStateFlow properties.
`submitPort` keeps the hand-written 0..65535 range check via `toIntOrNull` (no Android `UInt16`), and still calls `model.makePortErrorToast(port = value)` on failure.
Both Toggles write the flow (`httpProxy.enabled.value = it`) from the onChange lambda so the value is observable.
The conditional `UrlsView` Section stays inside the Form at the same position as in Swift.
SwiftUI Section has no header here, so the Kotlin translation is a plain Column that the parent settings LazyColumn can host.
chatEmoteCombo.minimumCombo and chatEmoteCombo.resetAfter are treated as MutableStateFlow<Int> (the @Published mapping); the view reads them with collectAsState() and writes with .value.
@ObservedObject chatEmoteCombo becomes a plain parameter; no ViewModel wrapper is introduced.
Both Pickers become ExposedDropdownMenuBox rows via a private ComboPicker helper, keeping the option lists [2...10] and [3...10] identical to the Swift source.
.onChange(of:) maps to LaunchedEffect(value); unlike Swift it also runs once on first composition, which just reapplies the same settings.
setEffectSettings() is kept as a private top-level function with model, widget and chatEmoteCombo passed explicitly.
The call chain model.getChatEmoteComboEffect(widget.id)?.setSettings(chatEmoteCombo) is assumed to exist on the Android Model port in com.moblin.android.various.model.

NavigationLink wraps an inline Form destination, so the destination became a separate top-level composable DisconnectProtectionSettingsForm while DisconnectProtectionSettingsView keeps the label and calls onNavigate("Disconnect protection").
Picker with an optional UUID selection is rendered as an ExposedDropdownMenuBox row through the private SceneSelectionPicker composable.
Form and Section become a LazyColumn whose last item is the bodySmall Section footer Text.
navigationTitle("Disconnect protection") becomes the TopAppBar title of DisconnectProtectionSettingsForm.
SettingsScene is not in the glossary and is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; the collapsed picker text uses its name property.
database.scenes and disconnectProtection.liveSceneId/fallbackSceneId are read with collectAsState() and written through the MutableStateFlow .value property.
SceneNameView is reused unchanged inside the dropdown items, matching its use as the picker row content in Swift.
KeyboardSettingsView stays a single @Composable function taking the model objects it needs (Model, SettingsKeyboard); no @StateObject/collect wrapper class is needed.
The Form/List/Section hierarchy is flattened into one LazyColumn: the description Text, the key rows via items(), the create button and the footer help text are separate items, keyed by key.id.
.navigationTitle("Keyboard") became a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar (needs @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)).

The custom SwiftUI modifier .contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart; each row is wrapped in a Box with a long-press (pointerInput + detectTapGestures) that opens a Material 3 DropdownMenu with a Delete item.
List.onDelete (swipe to delete) is a SwiftUI List gesture with no stable Compose equivalent here, so deletion goes through the same long-press delete menu and mutates the list by filtering on key.id.

Mutation assumes SettingsKeyboard.keys is a public MutableStateFlow whose value is a list, so the view can edit it like the Swift @Published array (keyboard.keys.value = ...); if the settings model exposes an immutable StateFlow, route these through its own mutators instead.
The list value is always written back with .toMutableList() so the assignment compiles whether the backing value type is List or MutableList.
String(localized:) is mapped to localized(); it is used for the footer kind ("a key") and for the new Delete menu label. CreateButtonView is called with a trailing lambda for the append action.

WidgetEffectWizardSettingsView becomes a @Composable function with the same name; the @Binding presentingCreateWizard is a Boolean parameter plus an onChange lambda, and effect is passed in so its StateFlow properties can be read with collectAsState().
The Form/Section structure is rendered as a LazyColumn with a section header Text, an ExposedDropdownMenuBox for the Type picker and a TextButtonView row for Create.

Picker selection writes back through effect.type.value, i.e. SettingsVideoEffect.type is expected to be exposed as a MutableStateFlow; if the class only exposes a read-only StateFlow this call must be adjusted in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
SettingsVideoEffectType.allCases is mapped to the standard Kotlin enum property SettingsVideoEffectType.entries, and the Swift custom toString() is mapped to the enum's own toString().
widget.effects.append(effect) becomes widget.effects.add(effect), so SettingsWidget.effects is assumed to be a MutableList<SettingsVideoEffect>.
model.resetSelectedScene(changeScene: false) keeps its Swift signature as model.resetSelectedScene(changeScene = false).
The toolbar CloseToolbar is rendered as TopAppBar actions calling CloseToolbarButtonView { ... } with a trailing lambda that sets the presentation binding to false.
TopAppBar requires ExperimentalMaterial3Api, hence the @OptIn annotation on the composable.

Swift changed the model from @EnvironmentObject to a plain let property; the Kotlin signature already provides it as a parameter, and its LocalModel.current default keeps the parameter optional so existing callers keep working while new callers can pass model explicitly, as the Swift now does.
No other line of the Swift body changed, so the rest of the Kotlin file is kept byte-identical.
model.reloadLocation() is called only when stream.enabled, exactly as in Swift.
stream is a settings type read directly (no collectAsState), matching how the platform settings classes are observed.
TextEditNavigationView keeps its onChange = { isValidHttpUrl(it) } validation and the sensitive push key field.
`@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` becomes an explicit `model: Model` parameter; `let stream: SettingsStream` becomes `stream: SettingsStream`.
The SwiftUI `Form` with a single header-less `Section` is rendered as a `LazyColumn` holding the two rows.
Each `Toggle` used a custom `Binding(get:set:)`; the `Switch` reads `stream.rist.*` directly and writes the new value plus calls `model.reloadStreamIfEnabled(stream)` in `onCheckedChange`.
`.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isLive)` becomes `enabled = !(stream.enabled && model.isLive)` on the `Switch`.
`.navigationTitle("RIST")` is emitted as a Material 3 `TopAppBar` title inside a `Scaffold`; hoist it into the parent Scaffold if this screen is already hosted by one.
Recomposition relies on the parent observing the model/stream state, since the switch value is read straight from the `SettingsStream` object.
RemoveBackgroundEffectView keeps its name and becomes a @Composable function that receives model, widget, effect and the observed removeBackground settings object as parameters.
The SwiftUI Section with its header becomes a header Text followed by the two picker rows inside a Column.
The @ObservedObject settings object is passed in as a parameter; its StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().

Writes back to the settings object use .value on the published MutableStateFlow properties, which is how this port exposes @Published (MutableStateFlow is itself a StateFlow, so collectAsState() still works).
RgbColorPickerView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils and is called as (title, color, onChange) replacing the Swift color Binding plus trailing closure.
updateWidget mirrors the Swift private method and stays a local function inside the composable; it reads plain values from the settings flows and forwards them to setColorRange.
The Swift $removeBackground.fromColor / toColor bindings are modelled as the collected current value plus an onChange lambda that writes the new color back.
SegmentedPicker, SegmentedHPicker and SegmentedVPicker keep their generic type parameters T and Content with the same parameter order as the Swift initializers.
Swift's @Binding selectedItem becomes a value parameter plus an onChange callback, matching the tier rules.
@Namespace / matchedGeometryEffect has no Compose equivalent; the selected highlight is drawn directly with a Modifier.background on the selected cell instead.
Global layout constants (zoomSegmentWidth, segmentHeight, cameraButtonWidth, ...) are top-level vals in this package, matching the Swift globals one to one.
Color.gray and Color.black.opacity(0.4) become Color.Gray and Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.4f).
The pickerBorderColor/pickerBackgroundColor globals keep their Swift names as top-level Compose Color vals.

defaultSegmentedPickerSelectedColor.color() is translated as a TODO() because the Settings color helper is not available in this file's glossary; replace it with the real conversion once Settings is ported.
The ForEach with Divider separators becomes a Kotlin for loop emitting each item followed by a HorizontalDivider.
SwiftUI Section has no header here, so it becomes a plain Column.

Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox; the current value is shown in a read-only OutlinedTextField with MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable, and the empty tag (nil source widget) becomes a DropdownMenuItem with empty text.
Model was an @EnvironmentObject, so it is now a parameter and model.database is read with collectAsState().

The private SwiftUI helper methods (changeXY, changeWidthHeight, submitX/Y/Width/Height, sourceWidgetExists) become private top-level functions in the same package that take model and widget as parameters, since the View is a @Composable function.

keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation is passed as Compose KeyboardType.Number; if the ported TextEditNavigationView takes its own keyboard-type type or no keyboardType parameter, adjust those four call sites.
SettingsWidgetType.browser is assumed to be the Kotlin enum case name for the Swift .browser case.
Mutating widget.crop does not itself trigger recomposition; the UI refreshes because resetSelectedScene(changeScene = false) updates Model state.
Applied the diff: the Chat destination now passes model = model into WatchChatSettingsView; the rest of the file is unchanged.
model keeps its Android default Model = LocalModel.current so existing callers of WatchSettingsView keep compiling; the explicit argument from the Swift init now overrides it.
watch.chat still drives the hand-written conversion into com.moblin.android.view.settings.watch.chat.WatchSettingsChat, which is the type WatchChatSettingsView expects.
No imports, declaration order or formatting changed elsewhere.
@ObservedObject debugOverlay becomes a parameter whose debugLines StateFlow is read with collectAsState().
ForEach over debugLines with id: \.self becomes a plain forEach loop; keys are not required in Compose.
The VStack spacing of 1 maps to Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp) on the Column.
smallFont from com.moblin.android.common.various is reused as the Text style parameter.
Color(white: 0, opacity: 0.75) becomes Color(0f, 0f, 0f, 0.75f).
The conditional rendering of the whole view is a plain if around the Column.
SwiftUI Form/Section become a scrollable Column; this Section has no header so no header Text is emitted.
Toggle with a get/set Binding becomes a Material 3 Switch with checked + onCheckedChange; the setter body is copied verbatim.
.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isLive) becomes the Switch enabled parameter with the negation.
.navigationTitle("RTMP") is not rendered here; the enclosing scaffold/TopAppBar owns the screen title in this port.
model is the @EnvironmentObject, so model.isLive is read as a StateFlow via collectAsState() (assumes Model exposes isLive as StateFlow<Boolean>).
stream.rtmp.adaptiveBitrateEnabled and stream.enabled are treated as directly mutable Kotlin properties, matching the Swift direct assignment.
model.reloadStreamIfEnabled(stream) is called after mutating the setting, preserving the original React-like side effect.
No nav-compose dependency is pulled in; the composable is a plain screen body.
SliderView becomes a @Composable taking value plus a onChange lambda and an onSubmit lambda, since Compose has no two-way @Binding parameter.
The Swift onEditingChanged begin/finish behaviour is reproduced with onValueChangeFinished, which Compose Slider calls when the user releases the thumb.
Slider range uses minimum..maximum with steps computed from (maximum - minimum) / step, rounded down to an Int as Compose expects.
The label width keeps the Swift name `width` and is applied with Modifier.width(width.dp).
format is a lambda parameter `(Float) -> String` exposed as FloatFunction-free plain Kotlin function type.
Slider is imported from androidx.compose.material3 and Text from androidx.compose.material3.
The EmptyView label of the Swift slider has no Compose counterpart and is dropped, which is behaviour preserving.
No iOS-only API is used, so there is nothing to replace with TODO().
UIImage is translated to androidx.compose.ui.graphics.ImageBitmap so the QR code can be drawn with Compose Image.
The View body became a single @Composable function QrCodeImageView(image, height); the @State isFullScreen flag is a remember { mutableStateOf(false) }.
HCenter is used from the same package com.moblin.android.view.utils and wraps the content horizontally centered.
.frame(maxHeight: height) maps to Modifier.heightIn(max = height.dp) because the Swift frame only caps the height.
.interpolation(.none) maps to filterQuality = FilterQuality.None so the QR code stays crisp when scaled.
.scaledToFit() maps to contentScale = ContentScale.Fit.
.onTapGesture maps to Modifier.clickable on the enclosing Column.
.fullScreenCover maps to a Dialog with DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false) whose content button dismisses the overlay.
SwiftUI @Binding value becomes a value parameter plus an onValueChange lambda; @State in the navigation wrapper is hoisted the same way so the caller owns the string.

@FocusState is replaced by a FocusRequester parameter (default remember { FocusRequester() }); MultiLineTextFieldDoneButtonView takes editingText plus an onEditingTextChange callback instead of a FocusState.Binding.
NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate(destinationName) callback, so no navigation-compose dependency is pulled in; the destination name used is 'MultiLineTextFieldBindingView'.
MultiLineTextFieldBindingView is declared internal instead of private so the navigation host in another file can render it as the destination.
The Swift .onDisappear submit logic is reproduced with DisposableEffect(Unit) { onDispose { ... } } using rememberUpdatedState of value/changed, since Compose has no onDisappear modifier.
Form/Section/footer become a LazyColumn whose first item is the text field and whose remaining items are the footer strings.
.navigationTitle(title) becomes a Material 3 Scaffold + TopAppBar wrapped around the binding view.
.disableAutocorrection(true) is translated to OutlinedTextField keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(autoCorrect = false) (deprecated in newer Compose but still valid).

SF Symbol names are runtime strings here, so a private helper sfSymbolToImageVector() maps common symbol names to the closest core Material icon (Icons.Default.*); unknown names fall back to Icons.Default.Info and the mapping table should be extended as new symbols appear.
Text("") used as a flexible divider is translated to Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)) inside the Row, which reproduces the right-alignment behaviour of the SwiftUI layouts.
LocalizedStringKey parameters become String parameters and Text(text) becomes Text(localized(text)) using the shared localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
iconWidth comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and is used as Modifier.width(iconWidth.dp); this assumes it is declared as Int or Float, not Double.
Row adds verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically to match SwiftUI's default HStack alignment.
The Swift views were structs with only stored properties but produce UI, so they stay @Composable functions instead of data classes.
No navigation, sheets or platform pickers in this file, so no navigation callback parameter is required.
No TODO() placeholders were needed; every view maps directly onto Compose.
@EnvironmentObject model becomes a parameter defaulted to LocalModel.current, @Environment(\.dismiss) becomes rememberDismiss().
@State var selectedId is never read in the Swift body, so it stays an unused String parameter (the parent supplies the current id, as in the Swift memberwise init).
model.bluetoothAllowed is read as a StateFlow and collected, like every @Published property of Model.
@ObservedObject scanner is the shared workoutDeviceScanner singleton; its discoveredPeripherals StateFlow is collected so the view recomposes.
onAppear/onDisappear become a single DisposableEffect(Unit) that starts and stops scanning.
The Swift List inside the Section is dropped: the ForEach rows are rows of the Section.
navigationTitle("Device") becomes Form(title = "Device"), which provides the NavigationStack.
ProgressView has no iOS shim in the platform layer, so the Compose CircularProgressIndicator replaces it.
UIViewRepresentable VideoPreviewItemView became a @Composable that hosts SharedUiViewContainerView inside AndroidView; updateUIView maps to the AndroidView update lambda calling attachSharedView().
SharedUiViewContainerView is called as SharedUiViewContainerView(context, previewView) in the AndroidView factory, assuming the Android port takes a Context plus the shared PreviewView.
Orientation and VideoPreviewProvider exposed @Published properties are StateFlow in the Kotlin port, so body reads use collectAsState() and the resulting Boolean/List values.
The Swift 'private func height()' helpers are kept as local functions inside the composables so names match the Swift source.
Frame/aspect ratio order was adapted to Compose measurement: Modifier.height(h).aspectRatio(16f/9f) yields the same fitted 16:9 size the SwiftUI frame(height:) produced.
.scrollIndicators(.hidden) has no Compose counterpart and was dropped because LazyRow draws no scrollbars.
.caption2 is rendered with fontSize 11.sp and .gray.opacity(0.5) with Color.Gray.copy(alpha = 0.5f).
ForEach over videoPreview.feeds became LazyRow items(); the empty-feeds Text became a leading item{} block, matching the Swift LazyHStack layout.
Form is rendered as a scrollable Column (verticalScroll) rather than a LazyColumn so that the nested ImportSettingsView form can be embedded without nesting scrolling containers.
navigationTitle is applied as the Material 3 TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold, since navigation-compose must not be pulled in from this file.
The section footer text is emitted as plain Text composables after ExportSettingsView; bold footer text uses FontWeight.Bold.
Every Text uses the localized(...) helper from package com.moblin.android.
The multiline Swift string literals are collapsed into single-line Kotlin strings, using the same wording.
ImportSettingsView and ExportSettingsView are reused from the same Kotlin package, so no extra imports are needed for them.
@ObservedObject parameters keep their names; their StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState() and written through .value (the ported settings classes expose MutableStateFlow).
SwiftUI Section becomes a header Text followed by its items inside the Column of the owning composable; Section footer becomes a trailing SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView call.
Picker -> Row with ExposedDropdownMenuBox + ExposedDropdownMenu + DropdownMenuItem; the composables are annotated with @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).

The NavigationLink to the inline 'Pars' Form is translated as a clickable Row that reports the destination through a new onNavigate callback (default {}), and the destination itself is kept in this file as WidgetScoreboardGolfParsView.
contextMenuDeleteButton and List.onDelete have no Compose counterpart, so per-player deletion is offered as a trailing Delete IconButton on each row.
onChange(of:) maps to LaunchedEffect(key), which therefore also runs on first composition, so currentHole is reset and updated() is called when the view first appears.
String(localized:) becomes localized(...) imported from com.moblin.android.
golf is unused in WidgetScoreboardGolfGeneralSettingsView, exactly as in the Swift source, and is kept for signature parity.
Added the new colorRange constructor parameter and forwarded it to MpegTsReader, matching the Swift change.
Added the SettingsStreamColorRange import from com.moblin.android.various.settings in alphabetical position.
Everything else, including the Android hand-written WeakReference server, packet buffer reuse, SrtNative calls and reader.stop(), is unchanged.
@State number/value become local MutableState seeded from the number/value parameters, named numberState/valueState to avoid clashing with those parameters.
@Binding parameters became a value parameter plus an onChange lambda: onNumberChange, onValueChange and onNumericInputChange.
onChange(of: number) is a LaunchedEffect gated by an 'initialised' flag so, unlike LaunchedEffect, it does not run on first composition as SwiftUI's onChange does not either.
TextField onEditingChanged(false) uses Modifier.onFocusChanged, and onSubmit uses KeyboardOptions/ImeAction.Done plus KeyboardActions(onDone).
SwiftUI Slider 'step' becomes Compose 'steps', computed as ((maximum - minimum) / step).toInt() - 1 and clamped at 0.

ValueEditCompactView takes SF Symbol names as runtime Strings, so they are mapped to the closest core Material icons (KeyboardArrowUp/KeyboardArrowDown) and the original name is kept as contentDescription.
.rotationEffect(.degrees(mirror ? 180 : 0)) becomes Modifier.graphicsLayer { rotationZ = ... }.
Divider maps to Material 3 HorizontalDivider; the .buttonStyle(.borderless) buttons render as TextButton.
Added the new colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange constructor parameter and private field, in the same position as the Swift init (settings, softwareDecoding, colorRange, delegate).
setupClient now forwards colorRange = colorRange to WhipServerClient, matching the added Swift argument.
Added the import of com.moblin.android.various.settings.SettingsStreamColorRange in alphabetical position among the other settings imports.
Everything else, including the main-thread onCompleted hops, HttpServer wiring and WhipServerClientDelegate overrides, is unchanged.

Inline NavigationLink destinations were extracted into separate composables (TeamViewDetail, WidgetScoreboardModularLayoutDetailView) and navigation is exposed through an onNavigate route-string callback, since navigation-compose must not be pulled in here.

The SettingsWidget* observable objects are treated as plain mutable holders and every onChange(of:) effect was folded into the corresponding mutation callback so nothing fires spuriously on first composition.
Section header views become a plain Text placed above their items, matching the Form/Section layout.
RgbColorPickerView and TextEditNavigationView signatures (title/value/color/onChange/onSubmit/valueFormat) were assumed from the glossary types in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
Compose Slider works in Float while the model keeps Double, so toFloat()/toDouble() conversions are applied to width and rowHeight.
SettingsWidgetGenericScoreboardClockDirection and SettingsWidgetScoreboardLayout are treated as Kotlin enum classes and iterated with .entries (the Kotlin counterpart of CaseIterable.allCases).
Navigation titles (navigationTitle) are not rendered in these composables; the hosting Scaffold/TopAppBar is expected to supply them.
localized(...) is imported from com.moblin.android and replaces String(localized:) per the mapping rules.
rtmpCameras() is replaced by updateRtmpVideoSources(), which assigns into the videoSources.rtmp MutableStateFlow with .value
updateRtmpVideoSourcesAndMics() calls updateRtmpVideoSources() plus the existing updateRtmpMics() from the mics file
Everything else in the file is unchanged from the previous translation
The diff only replaces URLSession.shared with httpUrlSession() for the POST offer and the DELETE request, which routes through Moblin's shared OkHttp client instead of a per-call session.

The hand-written Android port already does this: sendOffer uses httpRequest(request, queue = dispatchQueue) and sendDeleteRequest uses httpRequest(request), both backed by the shared client, so the Kotlin file is unchanged.
No other line of the Swift diff touches behaviour, so every Kotlin line stays byte-identical.
The Swift function srtlaCameras() was replaced by updateSrtlaVideoSources() and updateSrtlaVideoSourcesAndMics(), placed in the same position after srtlaServerEnabled().
videoSources.srtla is a MutableStateFlow<List<Camera>>, so the assignment is written as videoSources.srtla.value = ... like other video-source updates in the port.
updateSrtlaMics() is a Model extension in the same package (the mics sibling file) and is called without an import.
Nothing else in the file changed; all imports, declarations and formatting are kept byte-identical.
CIImage is replaced by android.graphics.Bitmap throughout the print pipeline; CatPrinter.print(image:feedPaperDelay:) is assumed to take a Bitmap plus a nullable Double delay.

The SwiftUI ImageRenderer event card is re-implemented with android.graphics.Canvas plus StaticLayout drawn onto a 384px wide white Bitmap; the unavailable AppIconNoBackground asset becomes a grey placeholder circle.
Platform.name() is kept as a function call and Platform.twitch / Platform.kick keep their Swift case names; adjust if the Kotlin Platform exposes name as a property or uses upper-case entries.

Kotlin cannot add a protocol conformance inside an extension, so 'extension Model: CatPrinterDelegate' becomes the class ModelCatPrinterDelegate(model); it must be assigned to CatPrinter.delegate (see enableCatPrinter).

Model members catPrinters, database, currentCatPrinterSettings and statusTopRight come from Model.kt; catPrinters is assumed to be a MutableMap<UUID, CatPrinter> with UUID keys matching SettingsCatPrinter.id.
fetchTwitchProfilePicture / fetchKickProfilePicture are assumed to be suspend functions returning Bitmap? so that createEventImage can await them.
DateFormatter is replaced by java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter with Locale.US and pattern 'MMM d, yyyy HH:mm:ss'; the timestamp uses the system time zone.
Swift Task { } blocks become coroutine launches on a private Main-dispatcher CoroutineScope (mainScope).

StreamDeck's two @Published properties are MutableStateFlow fields exposed as StateFlow (private _isDeviceDriverInstalled/_streamDeck). Because the Model extension functions in this same file mutate them, small setter methods setIsDeviceDriverInstalled/setStreamDeck were added.

StreamDeckKeyItemView is a private @Composable that receives the SettingsStreamDeckKey directly and reads its text/colorColor/function/functionData properties, mirroring the Swift @ObservedObject usage.
StreamDeckKeyView (com.moblin.android.view.settings.streamdeck) is called with its press handler lambda plus a trailing content lambda, matching the Swift two-closure call site.

All Elgato StreamDeckKit layout scaffolding (StreamDeckLayout, StreamDeckKeyAreaLayout, StreamDeckSession) has no Android counterpart, so those bodies are TODO and the SwiftUI key content inside them is not rendered.
UIApplication.canOpenURL for the elgato-device-driver scheme cannot be checked without an Android Context accessor in this file, so it is TODO and assigned via the setter.
The Swift '#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)' compile-time branch is dropped; only the runtime isPad() guard is kept.
The @MainActor annotation on StreamDeck has no Kotlin equivalent; StateFlow provides the thread-safe observation instead.
SettingsStreamDecks.layouts and selectedId are treated as plain Kotlin properties (read/assigned directly) as in the Swift code.
apple_only: StreamDeckKit (StreamDeckSession.setUp, StreamDeckLayout, StreamDeckKeyAreaLayout)
UIApplication.canOpenURL

notes: whipCameras() was removed in Swift and replaced by updateWhipVideoSources(), which now assigns into videoSources.whip instead of returning a list.
videoSources.whip is a MutableStateFlow<List<Camera>> in Kotlin, so the assignment is written as videoSources.whip.value = ...
New updateWhipVideoSourcesAndMics() calls the existing updateWhipVideoSources() and updateWhipMics() extensions in the same package.
Camera ids keep the previous Kotlin translation of stream.id.uuidString as stream.id.toString().
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including the delegate class, mainScope and the buffered audio/video forwarding.
The Swift diff only adds the colorRange parameter, so only the constructor signature and the two SrtServer calls changed.
SrtlaServer now takes colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange after softwareDecoding and forwards it to both SrtServer instances in the same position as Swift.
The colorRange argument requires SrtServer to expose a colorRange parameter; SrtServer.kt is updated by its own change in the same commit, the declaration list shown here predates it.
SettingsStreamColorRange is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
All other members, Android-specific socket handling and helper functions are untouched and byte-identical.
srtlaServerQueue, periodicTimerTimeout, TAG, secureRandom, randomBytes and groupIdKey keep their existing Android implementations.
MicsDelayView.swift contains only SwiftUI views, so the file declares two @Composable functions: the private MicDelayView and the public MicsDelaySettingsView.

The @ObservedObject model is a plain parameter; mic.delay is read as a StateFlow with collectAsState(), and Slider writes go through a mic.setDelay(...) setter on SettingsMicsMic (private _delay MutableStateFlow plus public StateFlow per the port convention).
mic.name is treated as a plain non-observable String property of SettingsMicsMic, so it is read directly instead of collected.
onChange(of: mic.delay) becomes LaunchedEffect(delay) guarded by an initialized flag so it does not fire on first composition (Swift onChange does not fire initially).
Slider(-0.5 ... 0.5, step: 0.01) maps to valueRange = -0.5f..0.5f with steps = 99 in Compose.
Form/Section/footer maps to a LazyColumn with one items() block for the mics and a trailing item() holding the three footer Texts.
.navigationTitle("Delays") becomes a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar, which requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).
Text(...).lineLimit(1) becomes Text(maxLines = 1); Text(...).frame(width: 60) becomes Modifier.width(60.dp) and the Slider takes Modifier.weight(1f).

TextEditNavigationView and MultiLineTextFieldNavigationView are imported from the same package com.moblin.android.view.utils and are called with the same named parameters as the Swift initializer (title/value/onChange/onSubmit/sensitive and title/placeholder/value/onSubmit).
The SwiftUI Section is rendered as a Column whose first child is the section header Text, followed by the section rows.
SettingsOpenAi is taken as a composable parameter; its @Published Swift properties are read with collectAsState().

Writes to the model (`ai.baseUrl = $0`) become `ai.baseUrl.value = it`, assuming the port exposes the published property as a MutableStateFlow; if the model hides it behind a StateFlow plus a setter, change these three assignments to that setter.
`onChange: isValidHttpUrl` becomes `{ isValidHttpUrl() }`; the lambda ignores its argument so it fits either a () -> Boolean or (String) -> Boolean parameter type.
String(localized:) calls use the top-level localized() helper from com.moblin.android.
The header text "OpenAI compatible service" was a plain literal in Swift (no String(localized:)), so it stays a literal here.
No iOS-only frameworks are used, so nothing is stubbed with TODO().
Live2DLoaded is a file-private data class holding the model, renderer and pixel buffer pool, like the Swift private struct.
The model folder is scanned with File.walk(); the first *.model3.json not inside a __MACOSX folder wins, matching FileManager.enumerator.
DispatchQueue.global().async becomes CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch, and the loaded model is published on processorPipelineQueue exactly as in Swift.
The CVPixelBufferPool minimum-buffer-count key has no constant in the Kotlin port, so the pool is created with the platform defaults.
The Swift Double.toDegrees() helper is written as Math.toDegrees(...), which computes the same value.
renderModel keeps Compose Size in its override, as declared by VTuberEffect in the Kotlin port, even though Swift passes a CGSize (the parameter is unused).
AyagamiModel and Live2DRenderer are called through the Live2D shims; pixel buffers come from CVPixelBufferPoolCreatePixelBuffer and return to the pool when garbage collected.
Picture loading happens off the pipeline thread and the private `loaded` field is assigned on processorPipelineQueue, so no lock is needed.

Enum case names are translated with the Kotlin SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE convention (VideoCodec.H264, ElementaryStreamType.ADTS_AAC, MpegTsAudioConfig.Format.OPUS, AvcNalUnitType.SEI, HevcNalUnitType.PREFIX_SEI_NUT, ElementaryStreamDescriptiorTag.EXTENSION, ...); rename them if the sibling files of this port use different constants.

MpegTsWriter implements AudioEncoderDelegate and VideoEncoderDelegate directly in the class header, because Kotlin has no equivalent of a protocol-conformance extension; the members are kept in the original order at the end of the class.
CMTime becomes Long microseconds and Data becomes ByteArray. MediaSample has no decode timestamp, so the DTS used for the PES header is derived as presentationTimeUs - decodeTimeStampOffset.
MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream receives a nullable decodeTimeStamp where null stands for the CMTime.invalid passed by the audio path.

The failable Swift initialisers MpegTsVideoConfigAvc/Hevc(formatDescription:) are called as fromFormatDescription(formatDescription), which is assumed to return null on failure - adjust to whatever the sibling avc/hevc files expose.

MpegTsWriterDelegate.writer(doOutputPointer:count:) now passes a ByteArray plus count instead of an UnsafeRawBufferPointer; MpegTsPacket.encodeFixedHeaderInto is called as encodeFixedHeaderInto(buffer, offset).

NAL helpers (addNalUnitStartCodes) are used as top-level functions taking the payload ByteArray and returning the rewritten ByteArray; AvcNalUnit.aud10WithStartCode / aud30WithStartCode and the top-level nalUnitStartCode are used unchanged.
TrueTime's NTP reference time is replaced with Instant.now(), and the audio stream type is detected from MediaFormat MIME types instead of AudioStreamBasicDescription.
The two Swift `write` overloads (Data and UnsafeRawBufferPointer) collapse into one Kotlin `write(data: ByteArray, containsAudio: Boolean)` because ByteArray already provides offset/length chunking.
`payloadSize` is used unqualified exactly as in Swift: it must stay a top-level constant in package com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.srt.
`ContinuousClock.now` becomes `SrtClock.now`; the same timestamp value is passed to both enqueue() and send().
`DispatchQueue.async` on srtlaClientQueue / processorPipelineQueue becomes `CoroutineScope.launch`, so those globals must be CoroutineScope values (Dispatchers.IO).
`@unchecked Sendable` has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped; thread confinement is provided by the dispatchers of the two queues.
`latency: UInt16` stays `UShort` because it is the SRT handshake wire field.
The no-op `writer(writer:doOutputPointer:count:)` override is kept for parity; remove it if MpegTsWriterDelegate in this port no longer declares the legacy pointer overload.
The delegate is stored strongly, matching the Swift `private let delegate` (not weak).
VRM path is a String (as required for VTuberVrmEffect), passed to VRMSceneLoader(withURL = vrm).

The Swift init's DispatchQueue.global().async becomes CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch in an init block; the inner processorPipelineQueue.async becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch since that global is a CoroutineScope.
The local scene val shadows the property exactly as in Swift, so the property assignments use this@VTuberVrmEffect.scene / this@VTuberVrmEffect.cameraNode.
SCNRenderer.snapshot returns a non-null Bitmap, so the Swift optional chain vTuberImage.cgImage?.toEffectImage() collapses to vTuberImage.cgImage.toEffectImage().
Swift time.remainder(dividingBy:) is the IEEE 754 remainder, translated as Math.IEEEremainder.
armsAngle.toRadians() is translated as Math.toRadians(armsAngle); the Moblin Double.toRadians() port was not listed among the declarations of this file's dependencies.
logger.info is translated to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
The unused timeDelta parameter is kept to match VTuberEffect.updateModel.
MetalPetalWidgetShape is renamed to WidgetShape and its borderColor is now a Core Image CIColor, matching the new VideoEffect.modifyWidgetShape declaration.
WidgetShape.apply mutates the data class in place; the Swift inout parameter is the same object on Android, so modifyWidgetShape just calls shape.apply(settings).
ShapeEffectSettings.cropRegion is shared by WidgetShape.apply and ShapeEffect.crop, replacing the two duplicated crop computations.
WidgetShape.placement returns the new WidgetShapePlacement data class in place of the Swift labelled tuple.
rotationRadians() now returns a Double instead of a Float.
WidgetShape.borderWidthPixels and cornerRadius(size:) were removed; cornerRadiusPixels(size:) uses the shared shapeCornerRadiusPixels helper.
MTIColor and MTICornerRadius imports were dropped because the file no longer uses them; CGPoint and SettingsWidgetLayout were added.
MaskImage caching and the shapeSameExtent helper are unchanged.
Only one Swift line changed: the emote segment now uses ChatPostEmote(moving:still:name:) instead of ChatPostUrl(moving:still:).
The Kotlin line now builds ChatPostEmote with name = word; the loop's word is already a String, so no String(word) conversion is needed.
ChatPostEmote comes from com.moblin.android.various, so the file imports it in place of the no longer referenced ChatPostUrl.
Everything else in the file, including formatting, imports and declaration order, is byte-identical to the current Kotlin file.

Swift renamed MetalPetalWidgetShape to WidgetShape in this file only; the Kotlin parameter type and import now use com.moblin.android.videoeffects.WidgetShape with the same ordering/position as before.
modifyMetalPetalWidgetShape was renamed to modifyWidgetShape; the inout parameter keeps the Android in-place mutable shape object (no copy), exactly as before.
widgetShape?.copy() ?? WidgetShape(contentRegion = image.extent) is kept, since a Swift var initialised from a parameter is a copy.
All other lines, formatting and imports are byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.

Network.framework (NWListener/NWConnection/NWEndpoint) is replaced by java.net.ServerSocket/Socket bound to 127.0.0.1; socket reads and writes run on Dispatchers.IO and hop back to a single-thread dispatcher that owns all state.
ContinuousClock.Instant/ContinuousClock.Duration are replaced by a monotonic System.nanoTime() Long, compared against nanosecond constants.

CMTime/CMSampleBuffer/CMFormatDescription/AVAudioFormat are replaced by MediaSample and android.media.MediaFormat, so toMicroseconds() now just clamps an already-microsecond Long and the AudioEncoderDelegate/VideoEncoderDelegate method signatures had to be inferred (audioEncoderOutputFormat(MediaFormat), audioEncoderOutputBuffer(ByteArray, Long), videoEncoderOutputFormat(VideoEncoder, MediaFormat), videoEncoderOutputSampleBuffer(VideoEncoder, MediaSample, Long)).

AVAudioCompressedBuffer has no packet-description equivalent on Android, so handleAudioEncoderOutputBuffer() sends the whole compressed buffer as a single audio frame instead of splitting it per packet description.
The weak delegate reference became a plain constructor val because MobcamStreamDelegate is an interface and the port keeps the delegate alive for the lifetime of the stream.

Because java.net.Socket writes block, congestion is measured with a dedicated writer coroutine draining an unbounded Channel plus an AtomicInteger outstandingByteCount, otherwise outstandingByteCount could never grow and frame dropping would never trigger.
SimpleTimer is used assuming SimpleTimer(queue: CoroutineDispatcher) and startPeriodic(interval: Int, block) with a one-second tick, matching the Swift call sites.
MobcamStreamMessageReader.read() is assumed to return Pair<MobcamStreamMessageType, ByteArray>? to mirror the Swift `while let (type, payload) = try reader.read()`.

libsrt calls go through a SrtNative object (JNI binding) assumed to exist in this same package; SrtNative, CBytePerfMon, SRT_ERROR, SRT_INVALID_SOCK, SRTO_SNDDATA and SRT_ECONNREJ are referenced, not redeclared here.
C out-parameters (&perf, &sndData, &size) are translated as single-element IntArray holders / the CBytePerfMon holder; srt_getlasterror(nil) becomes srt_getlasterror(null).
processorControlQueue and processorPipelineQueue are assumed to be CoroutineScope values, so DispatchQueue.async becomes .launch { }; the callbacks are dispatched there just like the Swift queues.
Kotlin has no weak references: srtStreamDelegate is a plain strong nullable val (matches the Swift 'weak let' name and usage).
Swift deinit becomes 'protected fun finalize()', which forces the class to be 'open'.
The MpegTsWriterDelegate conformance declared in the Swift extension is implemented inside the class body; Data -> ByteArray and UnsafeRawBufferPointer + count -> ByteArray.

URL is mapped to java.net.URI with a port == -1 check; sockaddr_in is mapped to java.net.InetSocketAddress (host resolved with InetAddress.getByName, the AF_INET check becomes 'is Inet4Address') and handed to SrtNative.srt_connect.

srt_getlasterror_str and srt_rejectreason_str are assumed to return String?, SRT_ERROR/SRT_INVALID_SOCK/SRTO_SNDDATA/SRT_ECONNREJ are assumed to be Int members of SrtNative, and srt_send_callback is assumed to accept a Kotlin function reference.

Moblink's @Published properties are exposed as StateFlow backed by internal MutableStateFlow fields (_status, _streamerOk, _scannerDiscoveredStreamers) because the Model extension functions in this same file must be able to write them.
@MainActor is dropped; every Moblink mutation in this file must be executed on the main dispatcher (CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)).
UIDevice.current.name has no exact Android equivalent, android.os.Build.MODEL is used for the streamer name.
Network.NWEndpoint has no Android counterpart, so the tunnel delegate functions take host: String plus port: Int and media.addMoblink/removeMoblink are called with host/port instead of an endpoint.
URL is mapped to java.net.URI; URL(string:) returned nil on bad input while the URI constructor throws, so parsing uses runCatching { URI(...) }.getOrNull().

Kotlin cannot add protocol conformance through extension functions, so the MoblinkStreamerDelegate / MoblinkRelayDelegate / MoblinkScannerDelegate implementations are declared here as Model extension functions that Model must delegate to from its interface overrides.
formatDeviceStatus(name:batteryPercentage:thermalState:) and MoblinkStreamer.getStatuses() come from other files; getStatuses() is destructured as (name, batteryPercentage, thermalState) triples.

statusOther.thermalState is matched against a ThermalState enum assumed to live with StatusOther in com.moblin.android.various.model; the Swift @unknown default case becomes else -> null. logger.info maps to Log.i with tag "Model".

The Swift diff deletes httpGet(from: URL) and httpGet(request: URLRequest); the Kotlin counterparts httpGet(from: String), httpGet(request: Request) and the private OkHttpClient they were built on are removed from this file with them.

Imports (okhttp3.OkHttpClient, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers, kotlinx.coroutines.withContext) are left byte-identical because no Swift import line changed; Request/Response are still used by the URLRequest/URLResponse extensions in this file.
Everything else in the file, including the URLResponse/HTTPURLResponse status helpers, URLRequest header setters and all formatting helpers, is unchanged.

No other Kotlin line changed: imports, declaration order and formatting are preserved.

The nested launch still calls silenceTimer.startPeriodic(interval = 0.1, initial = 0.0) on processorPipelineQueue and returns to outputSilenceWhileInterrupted through the SimpleTimer handler, matching the new Swift nesting.
silenceTimer is a property of AudioUnit, so it can never be nulled by the weak capture; there is no Android equivalent of the Swift optional chaining introduced here.
TalkbackPlayer, AudioMeasurement and the silence timer remain private/Android implementations with no behavioural change from the diff.
whepCameras() was replaced by updateWhepVideoSources(), which assigns videoSources.whep (a MutableStateFlow) through .value.

whepMainScope (Dispatchers.Main) still stands in for DispatchQueue.main.async in the delegate callbacks.

VStack/HStack become Column/Row and the SwiftUI inside-out modifier order is reversed: the row's .padding then .background becomes .background(...).padding(...).
.foregroundStyle(textColor) is applied with CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor) around the whole Column, so every child Text takes that colour.

.font(.system(size:)) on the two rows is provided through CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides SwiftUIFonts.system(...)), the SwiftUI behaviour where a parent font reaches the child Texts; the clock Text overrides it with .monospacedDigit().
Spacer(minLength: 0) inside the team-name columns and Spacer() beside them become Modifier.weight(1f) spacers.
scale is applied to lengths as Dp ((...*scale).dp) and to fonts as a Double handed to SwiftUIFonts.system.
.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5 * scale)) is the outer Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(...)) on the Column, clip ordered before background as Compose draws outside-in.
generic.clock.format() resolves to the Duration.format() extension in com.moblin.android.common.various, and TeamScoreView/PoweredByMoblinView are the ones already declared in this package.

Tesla's @Published properties become MutableStateFlow (vehicleState, vehicleVehicleSecurityConnected, vehicleInfotainmentConnected); views read them with collectAsState, and every assignment here writes .value.

Model's conformance to TeslaVehicleDelegate becomes three Model extension functions plus a private ModelTeslaVehicleDelegate forwarding class, which reloadTeslaVehicle assigns to tesla.vehicle?.delegate.

Tesla protobuf oneof reads use casts: optionalSpeed/optionalPower as CarServer_DriveState.OneOf_* classes, and optionalNowPlayingArtist/optionalNowPlayingTitle as CarServer_MediaState.OneOf_* classes, taking .value.
optionalBatteryLevel and optionalMinutesToChargeLimit are presence checks, so they are translated as '!= null'.

Miles per hour to meters per second is a Measurement(value = speed.toDouble(), unit = UnitSpeed.milesPerHour).converted(to = UnitSpeed.metersPerSecond) from com.moblin.android.common.various, then formatSpeed(speed = ...).
String(localized:) is localized(...) and makeToast(title = ...) stays the existing Model extension.
The switch over TeslaVehicleState uses the Kotlin enum entries idle, connecting and connected.
The switch over the shift oneof uses is-branches on CarServer_ShiftState.OneOf_Type inside a null check.
The three private Swift View structs become private @Composable functions with the same names and parameter lists.
`.foregroundStyle(textColor)` on the root container is translated as CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor) so the player-name Text inherits it.
`.bold()` on the header HStack is folded into each Text's TextStyle weight instead of a parent text-style override.
`.minimumScaleFactor(0.5)` is implemented by the private GolfShrinkText composable, which lowers the font size while TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow, down to half size.
ForEach over golf.players has no edit actions, so it stays players.forEach { key(it.id) { ... } }.
Under par uses iOS green 0xFF34C759 and over par iOS red 0xFFFF3B30, not Material colours.

ThruView's private func format() became a private top-level function taking the player and hole count, and keeps the Swift labels of holesPlayed(numHoles:) and totalRelativeToPar(pars:numberOfHoles:).
Modifier lists are reversed: padding(.leading) after frame(height:) becomes padding then height, while padding before frame(width:height:) becomes width/height then padding.
Added SettingsStreamColorRange property and constructor parameter to RtmpServerClient, matching the new Swift init.
The import com.moblin.android.various.settings.SettingsStreamColorRange was added; it is placed before the com.moblin.android.various.utils import to keep alphabetical order.
The new colorRange parameter is forwarded to RtmpServerChunkStream, so RtmpServerChunkStream.kt must declare a matching colorRange constructor parameter.
RtmpServerClient keeps its primary constructor shape (private val params) instead of a Swift-style init body; only the new field was added.
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous translation.
Added findWidestBackCameraDevice() and the widestBackCameraId lazy global right after bestBackCameraDevice, mirroring the Swift insertion point.
Followed the file's Kotlin naming convention (findBestBackCameraDevice/findBestFrontCameraDevice) for the new private helper.
widestBackCameraId is a String, matching the untyped Swift global; CameraId is a String typealias so both are interchangeable.
No other declarations changed; the rest of the file is byte-identical.

ScoreboardEffectPadelView is a @Composable function; the private Swift helper structs stay private Kotlin data classes and the private helper functions stay private top-level functions with the same names.
Each Swift `let id: UUID = .init()` becomes a data class property defaulted to UUID.randomUUID(), so the call sites keep using only the named home/away or name arguments.
`.foregroundStyle(textColor)` is written as CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor), which the ported Text reads as its default colour.

`.bold(score.isHomeWin())` is not a parameter of the ported TeamScoreView, so boldness is applied by wrapping each call in CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides SwiftUIFonts.system(size, weight = FontWeight.Bold)) — the same size with the bold weight.

SwiftUI's implicit 8 point VStack/HStack spacing is written as Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp) on every Column and Row that has no explicit spacing argument; the outer `spacing: 0` Column gets no arrangement.

ForEach over the Identifiable players and scores becomes items.forEach { key(it.id) { ... } }.

Swift `Float(bitrate)` with optional binding becomes `bitrate.toFloatOrNull()` with an early return.
`value.clamped(to: 0.05 ... 50)` becomes `coerceIn(0.05f, 50f)` on the Float value.
KeyboardType `.numbersAndPunctuation` maps to Compose KeyboardType.Decimal so fractional Mbps values can be typed.
`String(bitrateToMbps(...))` becomes `.toString()`; `Int64(preset.bitrate)` becomes `.toLong()` for formatBytesPerSecond.
The struct View is emitted as a data class holding the preset, with `body` translated to a @Composable `Body()` function.
The only change is `@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` -> `let model: Model`: the model parameter is now required, so the `LocalModel.current` default and its import are removed.
Everything else in the Kotlin file, including the hand-written `KeyboardType.Decimal`, stays byte-identical.
QuickButtonObs @Published properties become MutableStateFlow fields keeping the Swift names; Compose callers read them with collectAsState().
@MainActor has no Kotlin counterpart, so it is dropped; callers are expected to run on the main dispatcher.
CGImage/UIImage is replaced by android.graphics.Bitmap produced with BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray from the OBS screenshot bytes.
ContinuousClock.Instant maps to java.time.Instant and duration(to:) maps to java.time.Duration.between(...), compared against Duration.ofSeconds(...).

Identifiable has no counterpart; ObsSceneInput/ObsSceneMediaSource expose a plain UUID id used as a Compose key.
CameraPosition and StreamState are referenced unqualified assuming they live in com.moblin.android.various.model; imports must be added if they live elsewhere.
Added the third Section with the Photos image quality Picker after the Periodic video bitrate change Section and before the Form closes.
photosImageQuality is collected like the other flows and the write plus model.setPhotosImageQuality() live in the Picker onChange, mirroring the Swift .onChange.
Picker options are the three Swift ForEach literals 0.9, 0.95, 1.0 as Float values (0.9f, 0.95f, 1.0f) so they match the settings property type.
text = { it.toString() } keeps the Swift String(quality) labels of the picker options.
The Section footer is passed as footer = localized(...) since the Swift puts it in footer:.
Neither photosImageQuality nor model.setPhotosImageQuality() appear in the currently listed Kotlin declarations; they are taken from the new Swift code.
Imports, onNavigate and the first two Sections stay byte-identical.
SwiftUI View struct became a @Composable function; @EnvironmentObject model and @ObservedObject defaultZoom are plain function parameters.

AVCaptureDevice.Position has no Android equivalent and is kept as an Int here; callers pass CameraSelector.LENS_FACING_BACK or LENS_FACING_FRONT from androidx.camera.core, and Model.getMinMaxZoomX(position: Int) is expected to take it.
The NavigationLink destination is rendered when the local 'editing' state is true; tapping the row opens TextEditView.
Keyboard type .numbersAndPunctuation maps to androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType.Number.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() function in package com.moblin.android, which is imported explicitly.
SettingsZoomSwitchTo.x and .enabled are read/written as plain mutable properties; if that class exposes StateFlow instead, read them with collectAsState() and write through its setter.
Helpers x() and formatX(x:) that used self in Swift are private top-level functions here; x() now takes defaultZoom as a parameter.

TextEditView and TextItemLocalizedView come from com.moblin.android.view.utils; their exact Kotlin parameters are not in the glossary, so named parameters title/value/keyboardType/onChange plus an assumed onDone to leave the editor are used.
Added the textToSpeechSayEmotes published property, its encode entry and its decode entry in SettingsChat.
The new property uses the Published delegate like the neighbouring textToSpeechSayUsername, so Settings views observe it directly.
The JSON key is textToSpeechSayEmotes in both directions, matching the Swift CodingKeys case.
Default is false in the property initializer and in the decode call, as in Swift.
No other declaration in the file changed.
@EnvironmentObject model has no environment in Compose, so both composables take model as an explicit parameter.
The five submit* methods become private top-level functions taking model/stream, because composables cannot own methods; names and order are kept.
Form/Section become a LazyColumn whose single item is the inner Column, with section headers rendered as header Text items; .navigationTitle becomes a Material 3 TopAppBar title.
Toggles (including the two computed Bindings) become Row { Text(...) ; Switch(checked, onCheckedChange) }, with .disabled mapped to Switch enabled.
model.database.showAllSettings is read with collectAsState() since it is a StateFlow-backed published property.
TextEditNavigationView is called positionally by name (title, value, onChange, onSubmit, footers, sensitive, capitalize) assuming the Kotlin port of that helper keeps the SwiftUI parameter names.
Strings wrapped in String(localized:) use localized(); literal Swift Text("...") headers/footers are kept unlocalized exactly as in the Swift source.
No iOS-only framework is used in this file, so no TODO() placeholders were needed.

StreamingHistoryDatabase is assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties (totalStreams, totalTime, totalBytes, streams); the observed values are read with collectAsState() and the stream list is replaced with a filtered copy on delete, mirroring the @Published var + store() flow.

List.onDelete and .contextMenuDeleteButton have no direct Compose equivalent: each row now has a trailing delete IconButton that calls the same deleteStream/2 logic, so the makeOffsets() helper is not needed because LazyColumn supplies the row index.

NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter; the destination name carries the stream id ("StreamingHistoryStreamSettingsView/<id>") so the parent graph can rebuild StreamingHistoryStreamSettingsView(stream = ...).
Typography mapping: .title2 -> MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge, .subheadline -> bodyMedium, .footnote -> bodySmall (Material 3 has no footnote/subheadline styles).
Form/Section/List/ForEach collapse into a single LazyColumn with itemsIndexed; the Section header was omitted because the Swift section had no header text.
formatStreamTitle() stays a file-private top-level function (a @Composable function cannot own member helpers, so deleteStream() also takes the database/model it needs as parameters).
format() and formatDate() are used as extension functions (Double.format(), Instant.formatDate()); they are imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
formatBytes() is not present in the provided glossary but is used by the Swift source, so it is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various alongside the other formatting helpers.

The Swift diff replaces the @EnvironmentObject model with a plain `let model: Model` property, so the composable takes `model: Model` as a required parameter and the `LocalModel` default and its import are removed.
Everything else in the file stays byte-identical.
View body translated to a single @Composable function keeping the name StreamSrtAdaptiveBitrateSettingsView.
SwiftUI Form -> LazyColumn and each Section -> a header Text item followed by the section's content and footer items.
Picker bound to $adaptiveBitrate.algorithm -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox with DropdownMenuItem entries; the .onChange handler is folded into the item onClick.
SliderView is reused from com.moblin.android.view.utils with the same value/minimum/maximum/step/onSubmit/width/format arguments.
@ObservedObject srt and adaptiveBitrate are taken as plain constructor parameters since their StateFlow shape is defined elsewhere.
powf(_, 0.2) and powf(_, 5) map to kotlin.math.pow on Float.

.navigationTitle("Adaptive bitrate") is not rendered here; the surrounding screen's TopAppBar must supply that title.
SettingsStream's published properties are assumed to be MutableStateFlow: read with collectAsState() and written through .value.
SwiftUI Section has no Compose counterpart, so it is rendered as a header Text, the content, then the footer as a Column.
Form is a LazyColumn; .navigationTitle becomes a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar on the destination screens.
NavigationLink becomes an onNavigate("GoLiveNotificationDiscordSettingsView") callback; no navigation-compose is pulled in here.
@FocusState plus .focused($editingText) becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) } driven by Modifier.onFocusChanged.
.keyboardType/.textInputAutocapitalization/.disableAutocorrection become a KeyboardOptions argument passed to MultiLineTextFieldView.
The Markdown link in the Toggle label is rendered as plain literal text because Compose Text does not interpret Markdown.
GoLiveNotificationDiscordSettingsView stays private as in the Swift source, and the emoji-hint string keeps its exact backslash escaping.
Added the new `font` field to ChatLineStyle and forwarded it to ChatLineContent, matching the Swift diff.
SettingsFont is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; it is a non-serialized settings class so it stays a plain constructor property without a delegate.
Everything else in the file, including the hand-written messageItem URL translation and the content() call shape, is unchanged.
@EnvironmentObject model is received as a Model parameter; it is only used to call bttvEmotesEnabledUpdated/ffzEmotesEnabledUpdated/seventvEmotesEnabledUpdated.
The Swift Binding get/set toggles map directly onto Switch(checked, onCheckedChange), mutating stream.chat flags and notifying model when stream.enabled.

Each toggle mutation also triggers the same model callback as the Swift setter when stream.enabled is true.
FilesLocationView receives 'text: Text' in Swift; it is translated as a String parameter rendered with Text(localized(text)), so call sites pass the raw literal.
