UIPasteboard.general.string is translated to ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip with AppDelegate.context, and UIApplication.shared.open uses the java.net.URI overload with its success completion.
RecordingsSettingsView collects model.stream with collectAsState before reading stream.recording.recordingPath, since model.stream is a StateFlow.
The Swift .sheet modifier on TextButtonView is translated to Sheet placed inside the same Section, next to TextButtonView, so it can animate in and out.
The multi-line ffmpeg string literals and the long Help paragraphs were joined into single-line Kotlin strings with escaped quotes.
Text is androidx.compose.material3.Text so it picks up the app's LocalTextStyle (17.sp body by default).

The SwiftUI struct became one @Composable fun StreamOpenStreamingPlatformSettingsView(model, stream) with the same name; the model and stream are plain parameters instead of @EnvironmentObject and a stored property.

Form/Section became a LazyColumn with one item per TextEditNavigationView row; .navigationTitle became the title of a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
String(localized:) calls use the shared localized(...) helper from package com.moblin.android.

model.isRecording is a StateFlow on Model and is read with collectAsState().
Slider step 32 over 0...320 becomes steps = 9 (Compose counts the values between the endpoints); onEditingChanged's end-of-drag branch becomes onValueChangeFinished.

.navigationTitle("Audio") is rendered by a Scaffold TopAppBar inside the same composable.
calcBitrate keeps its name as a private top-level function and returns Int (the Swift UInt32 maps to Int outside wire-format code).

Adds the new SettingsStreamColorRange enum between SettingsStreamH264Profile and SettingsStreamRateControl, serialized with the Swift raw values "Full"/"Limited".

toString() uses localized() for the two display strings, as everywhere else in this file.
SettingsStream gains a colorRange constructor parameter plus a Published(colorRange) property so Compose observes changes exactly like @Published.
colorRange is added to encode(), decode() (default .full) and clone() at the same positions as in the Swift container and clone body.
The two new imports are placed with the other com.moblin.android.platform imports, keeping the rest of the file byte-identical.
A companion fromRawValue is provided, matching the convention of the neighbouring enums in this file.
Nothing else in the file changed.
Form is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold whose TopAppBar title is the Swift navigationTitle "Audio".
The Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox; SettingsStreamAudioCodec.allCases maps to the Kotlin enum .entries and $0.toString() maps to .toString().
@State bitrate becomes remember { mutableStateOf(...) } seeded from stream.audioBitrate (converted from bps to Mbps).

@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject properties are assumed to be MutableStateFlow and are read with collectAsState(); writes go through .value.

PostView lost its size parameter and the red placeholder rectangle; the deleted-or-visible check is now the outermost branch.

Everything else in the file is unchanged.
The SwiftUI views became @Composable functions with identical names; @EnvironmentObject/SettingsStream model objects are now explicit parameters.

Verify the Kotlin enum constant used in the when-branch: SettingsStreamDetailedProtocol.SRTLA (Swift case .srtla).

TwitchCategoryPickerView in Kotlin keeps its model parameter with a LocalModel.current default, so the explicit pass is compatible.
Everything else, including imports, formatting and declaration order, is unchanged.

NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate(title) callback on UrlsView; the Form destination of the link is emitted by an added composable UrlsViewDestination(status, formatUrl, title, showIPv6) that the navigation host should register under that route name.
The iOS fullScreenCover is rendered as Dialog(properties = DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false)) with a white Box that dismisses on tap.

Image(uiImage:) has no Compose counterpart: generateQrCode(url) is expected to return android.graphics.Bitmap? and is drawn with Bitmap.asImageBitmap(); .interpolation(.none) becomes filterQuality = FilterQuality.None.

urlImage(interfaceType:) returns an SF Symbol name as a String, so the file maps those names to Material icons in the private helper urlIconImageVector; the mapping is approximate and requires the androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended dependency (Wifi, WifiTethering, QrCode, Link, SignalCellularAlt).

status.ipStatuses is read with collectAsState(), so StatusOther must expose that collection as a StateFlow; the IpType of each entry is compared through rawValue ("ipv4"/"ipv6") because that enum lives in another file.

SwiftUI Section is translated as a Column with a MaterialTheme-styled header Text followed by its rows, so UrlsIpv4View/UrlsIpv6View can be placed inside a single LazyColumn item without nesting lazy lists.

CopyToClipboardButtonView, HCenter and the icons are composed exactly where the Swift code used them; CopyToClipboardButtonView and HCenter come from com.moblin.android.view.utils (same package, no import).
A Button with .buttonStyle(.borderless) holding the qrcode image becomes an IconButton with a 20.dp icon, matching the .font(.system(size: 20)).
DrawOnStreamLine becomes a data class; the Swift `let id = UUID()` maps to a constructor default so Identifiable identity is preserved.
`@MainActor private var drawing` becomes a private top-level `var drawing` in this file, since it must survive recomposition like the SwiftUI global did.

DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) maps to Modifier.pointerInput + detectDragGestures; Compose applies touch slop so a zero-length tap may not start a new line (drawing the single-point dot) as it does in SwiftUI.

GeometryReader is replaced by BoxWithConstraints; model.streamViewLayout(...) is called with maxWidth/maxHeight Dp values instead of a GeometryProxy, and the returned layout is expected to expose Dp size/offset - adjust if the model signature differs.
model.drawOnStreamSize is assigned inside the Canvas draw scope exactly like the Swift drawing closure; move it to Modifier.onSizeChanged if that write triggers a recomposition loop.
ColorPicker has no Compose counterpart, so it is a TODO and appears in unsupported.
SF Symbols map as: trash.fill -> Icons.Default.Delete, arrow.uturn.backward -> Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.Undo (requires material-icons-extended).
.font(.title) on the icons becomes Modifier.size(28.dp) and .accentColor becomes SliderDefaults.colors(thumbColor/activeTrackColor) on the Slider.
EffectSlider's Swift @Binding value became a value parameter plus an onValueChange lambda; Slider 'step: 0.01' is expressed as a derived 'steps' count.
SettingsFace is read via collectAsState(); the port's StateFlow properties expose no setter, so every @Binding write is a TODO listed in unsupported.
Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox (with ExposedDropdownMenu) and .tint(.white) applied as white text color.
The PhotosPicker branch is one TODO; model.saveFaceBackgroundImage and model.loadFaceBackgroundImage are only reachable once an Android picker is wired in.
@State selectedImageItem (PhotosPickerItem?) is kept as a remembered ByteArray? placeholder feeding the unsupported photo picker.
title: LocalizedStringKey -> String rendered through localized().
onChange(of:) -> LaunchedEffect(value); note it also fires on first composition, unlike SwiftUI.
SettingsFacePrivacyMode case names are assumed to keep the Swift spellings (blur, pixellate, backgroundImage, icon) and are iterated with .entries.
SlideshowEffectSlide is a plain struct with only stored properties, so it becomes a data class with val fields; widgetId stays a java.util.UUID.
SWIFT `let (effect, prepareEffect) = getEffects(...)` uses `info.presentationTimeStamp.seconds`; in Kotlin presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so it is converted with `/ 1_000_000.0`.
SWIFT `if let currentSlideEndTime` shadows the property with a local; translated as a local val read from `this.currentSlideEndTime`, keeping the same branching and the writes back to the property.
`slides.count` becomes `slides.size`.
logger.info(...) -> android.util.Log.i with the class name "SlideshowEffect" as tag.
setSceneWidget is not declared on the Kotlin VideoEffect base class, so it is a plain (non-override) function here, as in Swift.
The `@unchecked Sendable` conformance has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
execute/executeMetalPetal stay overrides and use the optional-call `?: image` fallback and `prepareEffect?.prepare(...)` exactly like Swift.
PomodoroTimerView becomes a private @Composable function with the same name and the same SwiftUI hierarchy (Column/Row/Box instead of VStack/HStack/ZStack).
The SwiftUI modifier chain .padding(.top).padding([.horizontal,.bottom]).frame(width:).background().clipShape() is reversed to clip/background/width/padding so the background covers the padding.
The effect's init parameter is androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size and is converted once to CGSize (canvasSize.toCGSize()); the private view keeps Swift's CGSize maths and receives the CGSize property.
Point sizes derived from canvasSize are converted to dp/sp when applied, so the widget scales with the stream like on iOS.
phaseColor/phaseIcon/phaseName computed properties become local vals from an exhaustive when over PomodoroPhase (focus, shortBreak).
setup() keeps the single ImageRenderer plus one objectWillChange subscription stored in AnyCancellable?, and the renderer's arguments are copied into locals before the content lambda.
setTimerImage assigns timerImage on processorPipelineQueue with launch (Swift processorPipelineQueue.async).
Swift's @MainActor on setSettings/setup is not carried over; the identity guard, settings assignment and setup() stay synchronous as in the Swift source.

The SwiftUI View struct became the @Composable function ScoreboardEffectModularView; its private @ViewBuilder helpers became private @Composable functions whose names are the Swift method names with an uppercase first letter (StackedHistory, StackedHistoryTeam, Stacked, StackedTeam, SideBySide, SideBySideTeam, Stat, PrimaryScore, TeamName, Possession, MoreStats, InfoBox, Title).
Swift point values (fontSize() * scale, modular.width * scale, modular.rowHeight * scale) are emitted as .dp, since scale already folds the design scale in.
Modifiers are reversed to Compose order: .frame(height:).background(c) became Modifier.background(c).height(...), .padding().frame(maxWidth:.infinity) became Modifier.weight(1f).padding(...).
StackedHistoryTeam takes an extra config parameter because the Swift method read config.global.period implicitly from self.

minimumScaleFactor is implemented by the private MinimumScaleText helper: it lowers the font size in onTextLayout while hasVisualOverflow, down to the factor passed in (0.1 for names/info box, 0.3 for the more-stats cells).
Color.black.opacity(0.25) and .background(.black)/.foregroundStyle(.white) are drawn with background layers and CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides ...), never with Material defaults.
Stat uses Modifier.fillMaxHeight() so its grey box spans the whole row, as the flexible Color inside the SwiftUI ZStack does under the row's .frame(height:).

Calls kept assuming the existing Kotlin declarations: config.periodFull(), config.infoBoxStats(showClock = modular.showClock), modular.fontSize(), modular.width/rowHeight/home/away/layout/isBold/showTitle/showClock/showMoreStats/showGlobalStatsBlock.
Only the position calculation in executeMetalPetal changed: metalPetalLayerPosition(...) is replaced by layoutCenter(...), which lives in the same package (EffectUtils.kt), so no import is added.
layoutCenter keeps the same named arguments (layout, size, streamSize) and returns a CGPoint, so the following MTILayer positions are unchanged.
Everything else, including the Compose Size constructor parameter, the SwiftUI layout DSL views and the ImageRenderer usage, stays byte-identical.

Swift renamed the shape type to `WidgetShape` in `scaleImageMetalPetal`; the Kotlin port keeps `MetalPetalWidgetShape`, the declared Kotlin type of that shape in com.moblin.android.videoeffects, which is already imported and exposes the same members (rotation, rotated, mirrorFlipOptions, rotationRadians).
`rotation: Float(shape.rotationRadians())`: Kotlin's `rotationRadians()` already returns `Float`, so no conversion is written and `MTILayer.rotation` stays `Float`.
No other Kotlin line changed; the Android hooks (swapPool pool release, buffer pool naming, Log.i error logging) stay byte-identical.

The only Swift change is a new stored property `pixelFormatType: OSType` threaded through the initializer, so the Kotlin constructor gains `private val pixelFormatType: Int` at the same position as the Swift parameter.

The output settings in `loadVideoTrackCompletion` keep the Android hook `com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video.pixelFormatType`, which stands in for Moblin's global pixel format and is re-applied by tools/hooks; that Swift line is unchanged by the diff.
Everything else in the file, including the hand-written `close()`, the lease release calls and the Compose overlay rendering, is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin translation.
`OSType` maps to Kotlin `Int`, matching the `kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey` constants in com.moblin.android.platform.video.
The reader is still `internal` because its primary constructor takes a ReplayBufferFile, as required by the replay shims.
StatusTopRight.catPrinterState is observed as a StateFlow with collectAsState; its collected value feeds the private formatCatPrinterState helper.

SettingsCatPrinter's enabled, printChat, printSnapshots, faxMeowSound, bluetoothPeripheralId and bluetoothPeripheralName are MutableStateFlows: read with collectAsState, written with .value; name stays a Published property read directly.

The Model helpers (isCatPrinterEnabled, enableCatPrinter, disableCatPrinter, catPrinterSetFaxMeowSound, catPrinterPrintTestImage, setCurrentCatPrinter) are imported from com.moblin.android.various.model and called with the Swift argument labels.

NavigationLink uses the real destination composables (CatPrinterScannerSettingsView, TwitchAlertsSettingsView, KickAlertsSettingsView) rather than string routes; the nested alerts Form is the destination itself.

The StateFlow values the inner destinations need (device.printTwitch, device.printKick) are collected inside the destination lambda, as the enclosing view leaves composition while a destination is shown.
.onAppear became DisposableEffect(Unit) calling setCurrentCatPrinter on first composition.
UUID(uuidString:) has no failable initializer in Kotlin, so the id is parsed with runCatching { UUID.fromString(value) }.getOrNull() and the guard becomes an early return.
scanner is only used inside the onChange callback, so it keeps discoveredPeripherals.value instead of a collected State.
Tapping a mic now calls model.manualSelectMicById(mic.id) directly when the mic is connected; the updateMicsListAsync wrapper is gone, as in the new Swift.
The .onAppear { model.updateMicsListAsync() } on the form was removed, so the LaunchedEffect(Unit) block is removed too, together with the now-unused LaunchedEffect and updateMicsListAsync imports.
DeleteDisabled and ContextMenuDeleteButton wrappers keep their Swift modifier order: context menu outside, delete-disabled inside.
mics.mics and mics.autoSwitch are StateFlows backed by the _mics/_autoSwitch delegates, so writes go through mics._mics.value and mics._autoSwitch.value.
The footer VStack is a Column with leading alignment and 8.dp spacing (VStack default spacing).
The disabled auto-switch Section is kept behind `if (false)` exactly as the Swift does.
Section(footerContent = ...) is used because the Swift footer contains a VStack, not a single Text.
The checkmark tint uses formPalette().accent for blue and Color.Transparent for clear.

Two SwiftUI Views map to two @Composable functions: the private DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtonSettingsView item row first, then the DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtonsSettingsView screen, matching the Swift declaration order.
@EnvironmentObject model becomes an explicit Model parameter on the private item composable, and is therefore also added as a parameter on the parent composable that hosts it.

@ObservedObject objects are read and mutated directly (button.enabled, button.page, quickButtons.enableScroll, quickButtons.buttons) because DeepLinkCreatorQuickButton/DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtons are plain mutable settings holders in this port; assign the setter side of any binding-style parameter to this pattern if the model uses StateFlow instead.

Form/Section/List become a Column with verticalScroll, a header Text followed by its rows, and a plain Kotlin loop for the buttons list; a LazyColumn cannot be nested inside a vertically scrolling Column.

SwiftUI Picker + fixedSize becomes ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a readOnly OutlinedTextField anchored via Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable) and a fixed width of 120.dp; this needs @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) on both composables.
The iOS 17 availability check around the Picker disappears; the page selector is always rendered on Android.
.navigationTitle becomes a Scaffold/TopAppBar title ("Quick buttons"); if the hosting screen already renders a top bar, drop this Scaffold and let the parent supply the title.
List.onMove has no Compose counterpart: the reorder logic is preserved as the private moveButtons(buttons, froms, toOffset) helper but no drag gesture is wired to it.
Only the model property changed: Swift @EnvironmentObject became a plain `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin parameter loses its LocalModel.current default and is now required.
The LocalModel import is kept unchanged even though it is no longer referenced by a default value.
Everything else in the file stays byte-identical.

MediaPlayerFileSettingsView becomes a @Composable taking model, player, file and onNavigate; the inline SwiftUI NavigationLink destination (Form + TextEditNavigationView) is not rendered here and must live in the screen registered for the "File" route.
Model and file are passed as parameters; Swift's @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject have no state wrapper here because only file.name is read and written.
@State image: UIImage? becomes a remembered Bitmap? state, filled from createThumbnail inside LaunchedEffect(Unit), mirroring .onAppear.
createThumbnail is called with the same trailing-closure shape as the Swift completion handler; if the Kotlin helper is suspend or returns a value, adapt that call.
submitName is kept as a private top-level function (Swift member function) so the file stays complete, even though the pushed form that uses it is built in another file.

Image(uiImage:).resizable().scaledToFit().frame(width: 90) maps to androidx.compose.foundation.Image(bitmap, contentScale = ContentScale.Fit, Modifier.width(90.dp)); the foundation Image is fully qualified to avoid clashing with the imported material icon property.
Image(systemName: "photo") maps to Icon(Icons.Default.Image, contentDescription = null), which requires the androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended artifact.
The navigationTitle "File" is reused as the route name passed to onNavigate.
@ObservedObject var dewarp360 becomes a parameter of type SettingsVideoEffectDewarp360 whose StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().
Swift's .onChange(of:) on each slider becomes a LaunchedEffect keyed on the collected value; it also runs once on first composition.
Slider step: 1 over each range is translated into the Material 3 discrete steps count (359, 179 and 139).
Section with a header becomes a Column with a Text header followed by the three Rows.
Slider writes back to the MutableStateFlow (dewarp360.pan.value = ...) because Compose Slider needs a value change handler instead of a two-way Binding.
Image(systemName:) icons map to Icons.Default.ArrowBack/ArrowForward/ArrowDownward/ArrowUpward/ZoomOut/ZoomIn.
updateWidget() keeps the direct Model calls model.getWidgetDewarp360Effect(widget, effect)?.setSettings(dewarp360.toSettings()) as in the Swift source.
Only the diff is applied: NameEditView now triggers model.updateRtmpVideoSourcesAndMics() when the stream name changes.
Swift .onChange fires only on a real value change, so the Kotlin onNameChange compares the old and new name before running the model update.
The .disabled(model.rtmpServerEnabled()) lines in the diff context are not present in the current Kotlin file and stay absent; the diff does not touch them.
Everything else, including KeyboardType.Number for the latency field (Android hand-written choice instead of .numbersAndPunctuation), is unchanged.
DeepLinkCreator's @Published properties are assumed to be exposed as MutableStateFlow so Compose can read them with collectAsState() and write them through .value from the Switch callbacks.

The private Swift methods stay private top-level Kotlin functions; updateDeepLink() now returns the new deep link string instead of mutating @State, so the composable owns the remember { mutableStateOf } value.
settings.toString() is translated to kotlinx.serialization Json.encodeToString(settings).

addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed) is mapped to android.net.Uri.encode, which percent-encodes a slightly larger character set than urlQueryAllowed; the {}/[]/" un-escaping hack is kept verbatim.
GeometryReader has no Compose equivalent here, so qrCodeHeight() is called without arguments; adjust if the ported helper in com.moblin.android.view.settings.gopro expects screen dimensions.
The resolution comparison assumes the port nests the enum as MoblinSettingsUrlStreamVideo.Resolution.r1920x1080.
UIPasteboard.general.string becomes ClipboardManager obtained through LocalContext, setting a ClipData.
NavigationLink destinations are expressed as onNavigate("<TargetViewName>") callbacks, one per section.
TextViewState now holds one SettingsFont instead of fontFamily/fontStyle; Kotlin keeps it as MutableStateFlow<SettingsFont>.
The private font(...) helper takes font: SettingsFont and uses font.name() like Swift's if let name = state.font.name().
The collected value is named settingsFont locally so it does not shadow the top-level font(...) helper function.
The monospaced-digit check uses settingsFont.family == null, matching state.font.family == nil.
setFontFamily and setFontStyle are replaced by a single setFont(font: SettingsFont) member.
TextEffect's constructor now takes font: SettingsFont in place of fontFamily and fontStyle; callers must be updated.
SettingsFont comes from com.moblin.android.various.settings and is used through its name() function and family property as in Swift; no declarations were supplied for it.

EffectSlider is declared in this same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so it is called without an import; its Kotlin signature is assumed to be (title, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, value: Double, onChange: (Double) -> Unit) mirroring the Swift (title:range:value:) initialiser with a Binding.
The Swift @ObservedObject database becomes a plain Database parameter; its @Published pinchScale is read with collectAsState().
The Swift onChange(of:) side effect is folded into the slider's onChange callback because Compose sliders report the new value directly, so no LaunchedEffect re-trigger is needed.
The $database.pinchScale binding becomes the current value plus an onChange lambda that both updates the model and would update the database StateFlow.
model.setPinchScale is called as a plain (non-suspend) function, matching the direct call in the Swift body.
range: 0.5 ... 1.0 maps to the Kotlin ClosedFloatingPointRange 0.5..1.0.
No NavigationStack, sheets, toolbars or platform-only pickers appear in this file, so nothing was dropped.
The view emits no declared Kotlin types of its own; it only contributes the composable function.
Database is an @ObservedObject, so torchLevel is treated as a MutableStateFlow<Float> read with collectAsState().
EffectSlider is imported from the same package and called with title/range/value/onValueChange; its body lives in EffectSlider.kt.
The Swift .onChange semantics are folded into EffectSlider's onValueChange callback so setTorchLevel is called exactly once per user edit instead of also on first composition.
The Swift ClosedRange 0.01 ... 1 becomes the Float range 0.01f..1f.
model.setTorchLevel keeps its Swift parameter label as a named Kotlin argument.
Kept the @Composable name StreamOverlayRightPixellateView, taking model and database as parameters.
database.pixellateStrength is read with collectAsState() and written back by the slider, so it is treated as a MutableStateFlow in the Database port.
The Swift onChange(of: database.pixellateStrength) became LaunchedEffect(pixellateStrength), which also fires once on first composition as the SwiftUI onChange does not.

EffectSlider lives in this same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so it is called without an import and its expected signature is (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, value: Float, onChange: (Float) -> Unit).
The Swift 0 ... 1 Double range became 0f..1f because Compose Slider works with Float.
The $database.pixellateStrength binding is replaced by the value plus onChange parameter pair.

ObservableObject models (SettingsWidgetBingoCard) are taken as plain parameters and their properties are read/written directly; if the port exposes them as StateFlow, wrap the reads in collectAsState().

Signatures of the re-used Moblin views were inferred from the Swift call sites: MultiLineTextFieldView(value, onValueChange, placeholder, onFocusChanged), MultiLineTextFieldDoneButtonView(editingText, onEditingTextChange), TextButtonView(text, onClick) and RgbColorPickerView(title, color, onColorChange, opacity).
The SwiftUI @FocusState editingText is a local remember { mutableStateOf(false) } that is reported back through onFocusChanged.

backgroundColorColor / foregroundColorColor are assumed to be androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color and the picker callback to deliver the storable RgbColor value, matching the SwiftUI Binding<Color> plus (RgbColor) -> Void closure.

Icons.Filled.CheckBox and Icons.Filled.CheckBoxOutlineBlank replace the SF Symbols square.split.diagonal.2x2 / square and require the material-icons-extended artifact; .font(.title) became Modifier.size(28.dp).
Section headers and the Squares footer are emitted as plain Text / trailing composables, so this file must be placed inside a scrolling Column or LazyColumn by its caller.
LaunchedEffect(bingoCard.squaresText) also runs on first composition, unlike SwiftUI's onChange which skips the initial value; guard with a remembered previous value if that matters.
The private updateEffect() method became a local lambda of the same name so it can be passed to the child composables.

AudioBarView/ChannelsView/SampleRateView become private @Composable functions; their private Swift methods clippingBar/redBar/yellowBar/greenBar become private top-level functions taking the current level value and the bar scale.
audio.muted, audio.numberOfChannels, audio.sampleRate and level.level are StateFlow properties read with collectAsState(); the parent passes model.audio and model.audio.level as parameters.
The Swift modifier chain .background(x).cornerRadius(5) is emitted as .clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).background(x) because in Compose a clip placed after a background would not round it.
bgHeight is a Dp, so rectangle sizes are Modifier.width(w.dp).height(barHeight * scale) with Dp * Float arithmetic.
Image(systemName: "waveform") maps to Icons.Default.GraphicEq, which lives in the material-icons-extended artifact.
smallFont is applied to the Text children (SwiftUI inherited it from the container's .font modifier); the icon's .font is dropped since Icon sizes come from Modifier.size.
compactAudioLevelColors returns a Kotlin Pair that is destructured into foregroundColor/backgroundColor, shadowing the imported backgroundColor for that branch.
Empty HStack spacing 0 and HStack spacing 1 map to Arrangement.spacedBy(0.dp) / Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp).

EffectSlider is assumed to expose (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, value: Float, onChange: (Float) -> Unit) since the SwiftUI version used a Binding; adjust if the shared composable differs.

Database.whirlpoolAngle is read as a StateFlow (collectAsState) because StateFlow-backed published properties cannot be written in place, so a local remembered angle drives the slider and is synced from the flow via LaunchedEffect.
model.setWhirlpoolAngle(angle) is invoked from the slider callback, matching the Swift onChange(of: database.whirlpoolAngle) side effect.
The Swift range .pi / 2 ... .pi * 2 uses Double math; converted to Float with (PI / 2).toFloat() and (PI * 2).toFloat().
EffectSlider lives in the same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so no import is emitted for it.
The composable takes model and database as parameters, replacing @ObservedObject with a parameter whose StateFlow is collected.

Swift changed @EnvironmentObject var model to let model in RtspClientStreamSettingsView, so the Kotlin composable's model parameter lost its LocalModel.current default and must now be passed by the caller.
No other line changes: the hand-written Android split into RtspClientStreamSettingsViewDestination keeps its model = LocalModel.current default and is still called with model = model from the link.
LocalModel stays imported because RtspClientStreamSettingsViewDestination still uses it.
Swift change: the view no longer reads the model from the environment, it receives it; the Kotlin parameter drops the LocalModel.default and the LocalModel import is removed.
All other lines are unchanged from the previous translation.
SettingsBeauty @Published properties are read with collectAsState(); writes assume the shared class exposes a public MutableStateFlow backing property, so they use `.value = ...`.

EffectSlider(...) is called with an assumed signature (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, value: Double, onValueChange: (Double) -> Unit) to match the Double-valued settings; adjust if the shared composable takes Float.
The private helper `setSettings()` is kept as a local function inside each @Composable so both copies can keep the Swift name without clashing.

Toggle -> Row with a Switch plus the picker; the Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only OutlinedTextField using Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable), which needs Material 3 1.3+.
onChange(of:) -> LaunchedEffect(value); unlike SwiftUI it also runs once on first composition, so the beauty settings/state are applied on entry as well.
`.fixedSize()` has no Compose counterpart and is omitted; Compose sizes to content by default.
SettingsBeautySettings.allCases -> SettingsBeautySettings.entries, with the lowercase entry names smoothness/shape from the shared enum in com.moblin.android.various.settings.

segmentHeight is used as a Dp and pickerBackgroundColor / pickerBorderColor as androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color top-level values declared in this same package; the Swift .overlay(RoundedRectangle.stroke) becomes Modifier.border.
PostView and AlertsPostView no longer take the GeometryReader size and no longer draw the red size-wide rule for posts without a user; those branches (and the size parameters) were removed.
The `val size = IntSize(...)` locals were dropped from MessagesView and AlertsMessagesView because nothing consumes the constraints any more.
PostView now starts directly with the `!deleted || showDeletedMessages` guard, as in the new Swift body.
AlertsMessagesView iterates `chat.posts` instead of `quickButtonChat.chatAlertsPosts`.

ChatAlertsView now takes the alerts ChatProvider (`chat`) and reads `chat.paused` / `chat.pausedPostsCount`; quickButtonChat is only passed through for the first-time-chatter and new-follower switches.
The ChatAlertsView call site passes `model.quickButtonChatAlerts` as the new `chat` argument.
No SwiftUI/UIKit API in this file lacks an Android counterpart.

ActionButtonView takes an androidx.compose.ui.graphics.vector.ImageVector instead of an SF Symbol name and gains an `enabled` parameter (Swift's .disabled modifier); the icons Block/Timer/ContentCopy/PersonAdd come from material-icons-extended.

@Binding properties (selectedPost, linkUrl) became plain value parameters plus onChange lambdas (onSelectedPostChange, onLinkUrlChange); @State properties became remember { mutableStateOf() } holders in ChatActionButtonsView.

confirmationDialog and alert became Material3 AlertDialog: destructive entries use MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error instead of role: .destructive, and the timeout dialog renders its three choices in a Column inside confirmButton.

ChatLineView and QuickButtonChatChatterInfoView are called from com.moblin.android.view.utils / com.moblin.android.view.controlbar.quickbutton.chat with their callback passed as a trailing lambda, because the exact Kotlin callback parameter names are not known from this file.

The private view-builder methods (banButton, timeoutButton, deleteButton, copyButton, nicknameButton, infoButton, lineView, saveNickname) are top-level private declarations here; dialog state and the dismiss() helper are passed in as parameters/callbacks.
ChatPost.platform is compared against ChatPlatform.kick, assuming the platform enum lives in com.moblin.android.various, which was not listed in the glossary.
Timeout durations are passed as Int seconds (5 * 60, 3600, 24 * 3600) to model.timeoutUser(post, duration).
swiftui contentShape(Rectangle()) on the dismiss Spacer was replaced with Modifier.clickable; the toast/toast-free layout otherwise matches the Swift body.
SwiftUI Sections become a header Text followed by the section content in a Column; the parent settings screen must supply the scrolling container.
UIImage preview images are translated to android.graphics.Bitmap and drawn with Image(bitmap = ....asImageBitmap()).

SettingsVideoEffectMask properties (points, tension, inverted, backgroundType, backgroundColor, backgroundColorColor, backgroundColorColor2) are assumed to be StateFlow and are read with collectAsState()/.value, written with .value = ...
makeCatmullRomPath is called with (List<Offset>, Float tension) and assumed to return androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Path - verify the signature in com.moblin.android.videoeffects.
The fallback photo asset 'GamlaLinkoping' must be added as R.drawable.gamla_linkoping in com.moblin.android.R.
SF Symbols square.resize.down/square.resize.up/minus.circle/plus.circle/arrow.clockwise map to Icons.Default.Remove/Add/Refresh (material-icons-extended may be required).
The Type picker uses ExposedDropdownMenuBox with Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable), which needs Material3 1.3 or newer.
model.stream.portrait is read directly; if Model exposes stream as a StateFlow it must be wrapped in collectAsState().
The @available(iOS 26, *) gates on the upstream structs have no Android counterpart branch, so every view is always rendered (glassEffect is a platform shim).

GeometryProxy becomes a CGSize taken from BoxWithConstraints maxWidth/maxHeight (dp values used as points); shouldStackVertically, mapSide and offset take the collected isSmall value instead of reading navigation.isSmall.

Navigation and SettingsNavigation StateFlows are collected with collectAsState in each composable and passed to the local helpers; writes to followUser/followHeading go through a cast to MutableStateFlow.

CreateStreamWizard is assumed to expose its wizard fields as MutableStateFlow, so the screen reads them with collectAsState() and writes them with .value = it.

.navigationTitle and .toolbar map to the Scaffold TopAppBar title and actions (CreateStreamWizardToolbar).

NavigationLink to StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView became onNavigate("StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView") on a clickable Box around WizardNextButtonView; nextDisabled() is used as Modifier.clickable(enabled = ...).

nextDisabled() stayed a private member-style helper, moved to a top-level private function taking createStreamWizard and urlError because it must not read Compose state.
model is kept only for signature parity; it is referenced by the navigation destination that is now a route name.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn where each section header Text is emitted before its fields.

CreateStreamWizard published properties (directIngest, directStreamKey, platform, twitchChannelName, networkSetup) are assumed to be MutableStateFlow in the port: reads use collectAsState(), writes use .value.

The networkSetup assignment uses CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.Direct; adjust if NetworkSetup is a top-level enum in com.moblin.android.various.model.
Link(...) is rendered as a clickable Text that opens the URL through LocalUriHandler.

NavigationLink is replaced by an added onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter carrying the destination name "StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView"; model is kept for signature parity and is only needed by that destination.
String(localized:) literals become localized(...) and the toolbar composable is emitted in the TopAppBar actions slot while .navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title.
KeyboardOptions.autoCorrect is deprecated in recent Compose; use autoCorrectEnabled if the project builds against Compose UI 1.7 or newer.

The SwiftUI NavigationLink destination is extracted into a separate GimbalPresetDetailView composable; GimbalPresetView now only renders the clickable name row and reports navigation through an onNavigate(name) callback (no navigation-compose pulled in).

SettingsGimbal and SettingsGimbalPreset are assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties: values are read with collectAsState() and written with .value. Bindings ($preset.name, $gimbal.zoomSpeed, ...) become a value plus an onChange lambda.
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart and is kept as a TODO() marker; the actual row deletion (Swift onDelete/remove(atOffsets:)) is implemented with a Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox.
Float.toRadians() is not part of the glossary, so the degree->radian conversion is inlined as value * PI / 180.
Slider step 1 over the closed range 10...100 becomes valueRange = 10f..100f with steps = 89, and the slider takes Modifier.weight(1f) so it fills the remaining row space like in SwiftUI.
The #available(iOS 18, *) availability check is dropped since the Android port targets API 26+; its content (Save current position) is always shown.
.navigationTitle is rendered with a Scaffold + TopAppBar ('Gimbal' and 'Preset').
The @ViewBuilder position() helper is inlined, and onAppear's LaunchedEffect(Unit) is declared before the state-change effects so it initialises the local x/y/zoomX before the onChange handlers run.
The SwiftUI Form is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold whose TopAppBar title is "Custom" and whose actions slot hosts CreateStreamWizardToolbar, matching the .navigationTitle + .toolbar pair.
The four NavigationLink rows plus the WizardSkipButtonView row become clickable Rows that call onNavigate with the destination view name (no navigation-compose in this file).
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit) and runs the same wizard reset plus makeUniqueName(...) call; localized("Custom") comes from com.moblin.android.

CreateStreamWizard.platform and .customProtocol are set to Swift enum cases .custom and .none; the Kotlin enum type names were not part of the glossary, so those two assignments are TODO() and must be filled in with the real enum cases.
CreateStreamWizardToolbar is invoked with the createStreamWizard parameter exactly as in Swift and is placed in the TopAppBar actions slot.
The Section header "Protocol" is emitted as a plain header Text above the items, per the section mapping rule.
The destination views are not referenced directly because navigation is delegated to onNavigate; they live in the same package as this file.
@ObservedObject createStreamWizard becomes a parameter; its StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState() inside nextDisabled.
@State urlError becomes remember { mutableStateOf("") } and is forwarded to StreamWizardSrtUrlSettingsView as value plus an onUrlErrorChange lambda (SwiftUI Binding).

NavigationLink is replaced by the onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback with destination name "StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView"; model is unused in this file but kept for signature parity with the Swift view.
Form/Section become LazyColumn items, .navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title ("SRT(LA)") and .toolbar places CreateStreamWizardToolbar in the TopAppBar actions.
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit).
WizardNextButtonView is called with named parameters enabled and onClick, matching the .disabled modifier on the NavigationLink.
Only composable functions are declared here, no top-level types.

@ObservedObject createStreamWizard is consumed as MutableStateFlow fields: belaboxUrl is read with collectAsState() and written via createStreamWizard.belaboxUrl.value = it; networkSetup is written the same way.
The Swift nested enum is assumed to stay nested, so the Kotlin reference is CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.belaboxCloudObs.

NavigationLink to StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView becomes the onNavigate callback with route name "StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView"; model is kept for signature parity but is otherwise unused.
onChange(of: belaboxUrl) -> LaunchedEffect(belaboxUrl), onAppear -> LaunchedEffect(Unit) which also assigns networkSetup.
Form is a LazyColumn; the Section header "Ingest URL" is its own item and the footer VStack sits in a following item.
.navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title and .toolbar renders CreateStreamWizardToolbar in the TopAppBar actions slot.
Image asset "BelaboxCloudIngest" is mapped to R.drawable.belabox_cloud_ingest, which must exist in the Android resources.
nextDisabled() and updateUrlError() are kept as local functions inside the composable; urlError is a remember { mutableStateOf("") }.

Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox with ExposedDropdownMenu; the 'General'/'Filters' Sections are rendered as non-clickable label rows inside the menu.

CreateStreamWizard's published fields customRtmpUrl/customRtmpStreamKey/customProtocol are treated as MutableStateFlow: read with collectAsState() inside the composable and mutated with .value in callbacks and helpers.

model is not consumed here; the caller builds StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView when onNavigate("StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView") is invoked (NavigationLink became the onNavigate callback).

navigationTitle("RTMP(S)") has no counterpart in this file: CreateStreamWizardToolbar is used as the Scaffold topBar and is expected to render the app bar title.
updateUrlError() returns the new error string instead of writing @State, because the state lives in the composable (urlError = remember { mutableStateOf("") }).
textInputAutocapitalization(.never) plus disableAutocorrection(true) map to KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.None, autoCorrectEnabled = false).
The .rtmp case assigned in onAppear is written as SettingsStreamProtocol.rtmp; adjust the enum name/entry to match the model package.

The navigation title "OBS" and CreateStreamWizardToolbar are rendered inside a Scaffold TopAppBar (actions slot).
createStreamWizard.obsAddress / obsPort are read with collectAsState() and written through their .value, so they are assumed to be MutableStateFlow in the ported CreateStreamWizard.
createStreamWizard.networkSetup = CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.obs assumes the enum is nested in CreateStreamWizard and keeps the Swift case name 'obs'.
WizardNextButtonView is invoked with onClick/enabled; if the ported view is only a label, wrap it in a Modifier.clickable Box instead.
Image("ObsMediaSourceSrt") becomes painterResource(com.moblin.android.R.drawable.obs_media_source_srt).
Port validation uses toUShortOrNull() to mirror Swift's UInt16(port) initializer and its 1...65535 range check.
model is kept in the signature for parity but is unused here because the destination screen is reached through onNavigate.

SF Symbols were mapped to the closest Material core icons: photo.on.rectangle -> Icons.Default.List, dot.radiowaves.left.and.right -> Icons.Default.Share, appletvremote.gen1 -> Icons.Default.PlayArrow, server.rack -> Icons.Default.Build; only core material-icons (no extended set) were used.
WidgetShortcutView keeps a plain Text label, matching the Swift source which has no systemImage.
The diff only adds a `model:` argument to eight destination views; every one of those call sites in the current Kotlin file already passes `model`, so the file is unchanged.

MediaPlayersSettingsView, DjiDevicesSettingsView, CatPrintersSettingsView, WorkoutDevicesSettingsView, BlackSharkCoolerDevicesSettingsView, WatchSettingsView, DebugSettingsView and SettingsResetView all already carry the model argument, matching the new Swift call sites.

No imports, declaration order or formatting were touched.

Model objects are assumed to expose their @Published properties as MutableStateFlow: reads use collectAsState() (mostly with 'by') and writes use '.value ='.

All user visible strings are routed through localized(...) from package com.moblin.android, including the emoji warning text.
RgbColorPickerView and TextButtonView are invoked with a trailing lambda so the ported callback parameter name does not matter.
Form is translated to a LazyColumn; .navigationTitle becomes the title of a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold (requires ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).

The Swift @Binding arguments (sceneWidget.layout and database.sceneNumericInput) become a value parameter plus an onChange lambda; rename the lambda parameters if WidgetLayoutView's Kotlin signature differs.

widget.type == .scene becomes SettingsWidgetType.scene; keep the Kotlin enum constant naming used in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
model.database.scenes.first(where:) becomes firstOrNull { } inside the same if block, mirroring Swift's combined if/let.
SceneShortcutView is declared in this same package, so it is called without an import.
SceneWidgetSettingsView is emitted as a top-level @Composable function, not a type; the only declared top-level symbol is that function.
ShortcutSectionView's Swift ViewBuilder closure becomes a trailing @Composable lambda.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn with a header Text item followed by the two protocol rows.
NavigationLink destinations are replaced by an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback carrying the destination name; navigation-compose is not pulled in here.
navigationTitle and .toolbar become a Scaffold TopAppBar whose title is "My server(s)" and whose actions host CreateStreamWizardToolbar.

Background execution of the wizard-setup assignment is not needed; the assignment happens once when the composable enters composition.

GeometryReader/GeometryProxy became BoxWithConstraints; qrCodeHeight now takes a Dp width and returns Dp (Swift returned Double from a GeometryProxy).

contextMenuDeleteButton became a long-press Modifier.pointerInput; SwiftUI .onMove drag reordering has no Compose counterpart and is not emitted.

NavigationLink destinations are surfaced as onNavigate route strings; the WiFiSsidEditView / TextEditView / TextEditNavigationView destination screens and their submit callbacks are wired by the caller.

Form/Section/List collapse into a single Column; the list of scene widgets is rendered with forEach over model.widgetsInCurrentScene(onlyEnabled = false), whose element type exposes widget and sceneWidget.

NavigationLink to GoProSettingsView is reported through onNavigate("GoProSettingsView"), ShortcutSectionView is assumed to take a trailing composable content lambda, and .navigationTitle("GoPro") is left to the hosting screen's TopAppBar.

SwiftUI Section became a Column with a header Text; this composable is not itself scrollable, it must be hosted inside the parent settings Column/LazyColumn.
NavigationLink became an onNavigate callback with the destination name "WidgetSettingsView"; the host navigation graph must resolve that destination and pass the widget (e.g. by widget id).

.sheet became ModalBottomSheet around WidgetWizardSettingsView; the @Binding became value plus onPresentingCreateWizardChange, .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline) has no equivalent, and if the Kotlin WidgetWizardSettingsView also declares onNavigate it must be threaded from here.

The YouTube API result switch inside fetchLiveStreams/fetchChannelHandle is left as TODO because the YouTube API port type is not part of the glossary.
PhotoShootCountdownView is new: TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 0.05)) became a LaunchedEffect that refreshes a clock state every 50 ms.
The two stroked circles are drawn with DrawScope.drawArc; the trim arc starts at -90 degrees like rotationEffect(.degrees(-90)) and its sweep is remaining/interval of a full turn.
photoShoot.nextPhotoTime is read as a MutableStateFlow<Instant?> with collectAsState, and remaining seconds are computed from epoch milliseconds.
The countdown text uses SwiftUIFonts.system(size = 28f, weight = FontWeight.Bold).monospacedDigit() so the digits stay monospaced like .monospacedDigit().
PhotoShootInfoView now takes a Database and renders PhotoShootCountdownView instead of the camera symbol plus the 'Taking photos periodically' text.
PhotoShootView passes model.database down to PhotoShootInfoView; the flash button is unchanged.
Swift clips the progress arc to 0...1 by construction; the Kotlin divides by interval only when interval is greater than zero.
Only imports, the new countdown composable and the two PhotoShootInfoView/PhotoShootView lines were touched.
WatchProtocolWorkoutStats.update(statistics:) relied on HealthKit; its body is TODO and the parameter is typed Any because HKStatistics has no Android counterpart in the glossary.
Codable structs became @Serializable data classes; Swift optionals (which decode as missing-key -> nil) keep = null defaults so kotlinx.serialization accepts absent keys.
Raw-value enums keep their Swift case names as entries plus a rawValue property and a companion fromRawValue, so packed strings stay byte-identical.
pack/unpack are companion functions returning Map<String, Any> and Pair<WatchMessageToWatch, Any>? instead of [String: Any] and a Swift tuple.
The two enums with associated values (padel and generic scoreboard actions) became @Serializable sealed classes with nested object/data class cases and @SerialName matching the Swift case names.
URL properties are stored as String, as this file never parses them.
The SwiftUI extension on WatchProtocolColor is now a file-private colorScale extension followed by a Compose Color extension; colors are converted to Float channels.
WatchProtocolChatHighlightKind and WatchProtocolWorkoutType have no raw values, so they are plain @Serializable enum classes whose entry names match the Swift case names.
apple_only: HealthKit (HKStatistics, HKUnit, heart rate / energy / distance / step / power / cadence quantity types)

notes: @Published properties map to a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow, so the Compose/Wear UI can collect them.
StateFlow is not serializable, so each class is annotated @Serializable(with = ...) and carries a nested Serializer object with a private Snapshot data class that reproduces the Swift CodingKeys.
JSON keys and the missing-key fallbacks (17.0, true, false, 30, ...) are byte-identical to the Swift encode(to:)/init(from:) helpers.
The nested CodingKeys enums are kept from Swift for side-by-side reading; the actual element names are set with @SerialName.
chat and show stay plain mutable properties, matching Swift's non-@Published vars; the outer class encodes them through the nested serializers.
The app must serialize with Json { encodeDefaults = true } to match Swift, which always writes every key.
The types stay reference types (plain classes), so equality is identity based, exactly like the Swift classes.
Serializer and Snapshot are Kotlin-only additions required by kotlinx.serialization; no other API was invented.

FontFamilyPickerView and FontStylePickerView are private SwiftUI structs and become private @Composable functions; FontSettingsView stays public and emits its two NavigationLinks as siblings, exactly like the SwiftUI TupleView body.

@Binding var font: SettingsFont becomes font: MutableState<SettingsFont>; SettingsFont is an immutable data class, so font.style = s is font.value = font.value.copy(style = s) and FontSettingsView passes the same state down to both pickers.

The Swift List inside the Form Section is dropped: its rows are rows of the Section, and each row HStack becomes FormRow(onClick = ...) so the whole row is the button, with the checkmark drawn by SystemImage.
Form + navigationTitle is Form(title = "Family") / Form(title = "Style"); the FontStylePickerView List is wrapped in a Section so its rows keep iOS insets and separators.
.onAppear is DisposableEffect(Unit) with an empty onDispose, and it only loads the families when the remembered list is empty.
loadFontFamilies() (a static method of the struct) and fontStyles() (a private method of the second struct) exist as file-private top-level functions with the same names.

fontStyleName keeps Swift's grapheme-cluster semantics: hasPrefix/count/dropFirst are done with java.text.BreakIterator character instances instead of UTF-16 units, since the truncated suffix is displayed.

CoreText and UIFont come from the hand-written shims (CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts/CreateMatchingFontDescriptors/CopyAttribute, UIFont.familyNames, UIFont.fontNames), and GrayTextView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.settings.streams.stream.
The Swift #if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) block is dropped: the whole file applies to Android, so both types are declared unconditionally.
LiveActionFunction is a Codable, Hashable struct, so it becomes @Serializable data class with the same property order (image, text).
LiveActivityAttributes conforms to ActivityAttributes, which is an Android interface without members, so the class header keeps the conformance and the nested ContentState stays nested.
ContentState is Codable, Hashable, so it is an @Serializable data class inside LiveActivityAttributes; 'functions' maps the Swift array to List<LiveActionFunction> and 'showEllipsis' to Boolean.
Section headers come from com.moblin.android.platform.activitykit, the shim that renders the Live Activity as Moblin's ongoing notification; never use NotificationManager for it.
The Swift property names become the JSON keys, so the activity content stays wire-compatible between the two apps.
The Swift labelled tuple (toLinear:toHlg:) becomes the file-private HlgKernels data class so the field labels survive side-by-side reading.
hlgKernels stays a file-private val evaluated with lazy, matching the one-shot Swift initializer.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) plus Data(contentsOf:) collapse into Bundle.readBytes("default", "metallib").
try? CIColorKernel(functionName:fromMetalLibraryData:) becomes runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(), so a failing kernel leaves hlgKernels null as on iOS.
hlgToLinear() and linearToHlg() return the receiver when the kernels are unavailable, exactly like Swift's ?? self.
CIColorKernel.apply is called with named extent/arguments so it resolves to the shim member instead of Kotlin's stdlib apply.
The hlgToLinear and linearToHlg kernels must be registered in CIKernelLibrary (the GLSL port of default.metallib); otherwise the shim constructor throws and both functions pass the image through.
The Mac Catalyst-only test formatDescriptionMatcherAddsColorExtensions is dropped: targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) blocks are Mac only and there is no #else branch.
Swift tuple results (Int, Int, Int) became Triple<Int, Int, Int>, and the argument tuple in processorOutputPixelFormatFollowsColorRange became the private ProcessorOutputCase data class.
@Test(arguments:) suites became one @Test with nested loops that create the queue, tester and encoder inside the loop body.
DispatchQueue(label:) became a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher and lockQueue.sync { } became runBlocking(lockQueue) { }.
try #require(optional) became requireNotNull; CIColor and CGColorSpace are non-null in the shim, so CIColor(...)! and CGColorSpace(name:)! lose their force unwraps.
CMTime(value:timescale:) became Long microseconds (v * 1_000_000L / timescale) and CMTime.invalid became kCMTimeInvalidUs.
encoder.settings.mutate { it.videoSize = Size(320, 240); ... } assumes the platform Atomic exposes mutate(block: (T) -> Unit); VideoEncoderSettings.videoSize is assumed to be android.util.Size.
getIsSync() is called on MediaSample from com.moblin.android.common.various, and luma/chroma bytes are read with ByteBuffer.get(i).toInt() and 0xFF.

Only the waitUntil timeout in cleanupKeepsFilesOfKnownReplays changed from Duration.ofSeconds(2) to Duration.ofSeconds(10); the identical call in orphanedFileIsRemovedAsynchronously keeps Duration.ofSeconds(2).
Everything else in the Kotlin file is unchanged, including the Robolectric runner, the MutableStateFlow `.value` reads and the java.io.File writes that replace the Swift Data().write(to:) calls.
The @MainActor Swift suite becomes a JUnit 4 class; every test body runs inside runMainTest { } from com.moblin.android (TestUtils.kt).
posts, pausedPostsCount and paused are MutableStateFlow in the Kotlin ChatProvider, so they are read with .value; Swift's chat.posts.map(\.id) becomes chat.posts.value.map { it.id }.
RgbColor is imported from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui because it is not listed in the glossary; move the import if the platform layer declares it in another package.
ChatPost.userId has no Swift default in the call site, so it is passed explicitly as userId = null.
Swift timestampTime .now becomes Instant.now() (java.time.Instant).
maximumNumberOfChatMessages is imported from com.moblin.android.various.model.
makePost is kept as a private method of the suite class, called inside runMainTest.
No ByteArray comparisons occur, so assertEquals on the mapped id lists is correct.

UIResponder's first-responder machinery (the private extension, noteFirstResponder and the weak static) has no Android counterpart: currentFirstResponder is a file-private helper returning Activity.currentFocus, canBecomeFirstResponder is init { isFocusable = true; isFocusableInTouchMode = true }, isFirstResponder is hasFocus(), becomeFirstResponder is requestFocus(), window != nil is isAttachedToWindow and resignFirstResponder is clearFocus().

pressesBegan/pressesEnded/pressesCancelled are folded into one dispatchKeyEvent override: ACTION_DOWN is pressed = true, ACTION_UP and ACTION_MULTIPLE are pressed = false; KeyEvent has no cancelled action.

The model call stays model?.handleKeyPresses(event, pressed = ...) with a KeyEvent instead of Set<UIPress>; if the port declares it as an extension function in com.moblin.android.various.model, add import com.moblin.android.various.model.handleKeyPresses.
didMoveToWindow -> onAttachedToWindow and onDetachedFromWindow, both calling claimFocus(), which stops the reclaim timer when the view is detached just like the Swift window == nil guard.
reclaimFocusTimer uses MainTimer.startPeriodic(interval = 1.0) { claimFocus() } and reclaimFocusTimer.stop(), as declared in com.moblin.android.various.MainTimer.
KeyPressView becomes a @Composable wrapping AndroidView(factory, modifier, update); makeUIView's view.backgroundColor = .clear is backgroundColor = Color.Transparent on the platform UIView.
Swift's URLSession is replaced by OkHttp's OkHttpClient, the port's HTTP stack.
URLSession.shared is a process-wide singleton, so the Kotlin client is created once through a file-private lazy value.
The function keeps its Swift name and signature, returning the shared OkHttpClient.
No Apple-only frameworks are used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Added import for spokenEmoteNames from com.moblin.android (TestUtils.kt) and the new assertion in emoji()
Added the new emojiWithoutShortcutsHasNoName test right after emoji(), translated with runMainTest and assertTrue/assertEquals
assertTrue(cond) used for the Swift #expect(segments[0].url != nil) check
spokenEmoteNames returns List<String?> so the expected list is typed String? to keep assertEquals unambiguous
Swift ChatPostEmote is the Kotlin data class ChatPostUrl in com.moblin.android.various; it has the same moving/still fields and url(animated:) method, so the suite builds ChatPostUrl values.
Swift URL values become the URL strings, since ChatPostUrl stores String? fields.
#expect(a == b) is written as assertEquals(b, a), and #expect(x == nil) as assertNull(x).
The private stored let properties of the Swift struct become private val fields of the JUnit 4 test class.
No locale, time zone or main-queue dependency, so no @Config or runMainTest wrapper is needed.
ChatPostTextSuite is a plain JUnit 4 class; no main-looper work is needed because ChatPost construction and text() are pure.
The Kotlin ChatPost constructor has no default for userId, so the extra named argument userId = null is passed.
ChatPostEmote and ChatMessageEmote use String URLs instead of URL, so the Swift URL(string:)! values become string literals.
createTwitchSegments/createKickSegments take an AtomicInteger id in Kotlin, so Swift's inout id becomes a val id = AtomicInteger(0) passed by reference.
ChatMessageEmote lives in com.moblin.android.various (same package), so no import is needed for it.
makeEmotes and createTwitchSegments/createKickSegments are imported from com.moblin.android and com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.twitch.
timestampTime: .now becomes Instant.now() since ChatPost stores a java.time.Instant.
RgbColor comes from com.moblin.android.common.various, not platform.swiftui.
